wikimedia-pekingese-bailey-dirk.note: Photograph (1280 x 1202 px) of a fawn Pekingese by Dirk (originally posted to Flickr as Bailey; captured 2007-11-22, uploaded by Flickr upload bot 2008-10-21). Licensed under CC BY 2.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-affenpinscher-official-standard.name: FCI - Affenpinscher Official Breed Standard No. 186
fci-affenpinscher-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 186 (valid standard dated 2009-03-26, English PDF published 2009-09-02). Covers German origin, Group 2 Section 1.1 Pinschers without working trial, monkey-like expression, pure black harsh wire coat with black undercoat, height 25-30 cm, and weight approx. 4-6 kg.

fci-affenpinscher-nomenclature.name: FCI - Affenpinscher Breed Nomenclature (No. 186)
fci-affenpinscher-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Germany as country of origin, Group 2 Section 1 Subsection Pinscher without working trial, definitive recognition date (1955-07-15), and valid standard date (2009-03-26).

akc-affenpinscher-breed-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Affenpinscher
akc-affenpinscher-breed-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Toy Group) establishing preferred height (9.5 to 11.5 inches), square proportions, harsh wiry coat, acceptable colors (black, gray, silver, red, black and tan, or belge), slightly undershot bite, and game, alert temperament.

akc-affenpinscher-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Affenpinscher Dog Breed Information
akc-affenpinscher-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile covering 17th-century German ratter history, height (9-11.5 inches), weight (7-10 pounds), lifespan (12-15 years), temperament, training, grooming, and health screening overview.

aca-affenpinscher-health.name: Affenpinscher Club of America - Official Breed Club Health Statement
aca-affenpinscher-health.note: Official Affenpinscher Club of America health statement hosted by AKC, specifying CHIC required tests (eyes and OFA patellas), optional breeder evaluations (hips, elbows, Legg-Calve-Perthes, and heart), and noting no known breed-specific genetic malfunction.

ofa-affenpinscher-chic-requirements.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals - Affenpinscher CHIC Requirements
ofa-affenpinscher-chic-requirements.note: Official OFA Canine Health Information Center (CHIC) testing requirements for the Affenpinscher (AF): Patella Evaluation and Ophthalmologist Evaluation.

fci-dachshund-official-standard.name: FCI - Dachshund Official Breed Standard No. 148
fci-dachshund-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 148 (published 2022-03-14). Covers German origin, Group 4 Dachshunds with working trial, elongated low-to-ground build, Smooth-haired, Wire-haired, and Long-haired varieties, color patterns (including Dapple/Merle and Brindle), and classification by chest circumference.

fci-dachshund-nomenclature.name: FCI - Dachshund Breed Nomenclature (No. 148)
fci-dachshund-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Germany as country of origin, Group 4 classification with working trial, definitive recognition, English/French/German names (Dachshund, Teckel), and standard publication date (2022-03-14).

akc-dachshund-breed-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Dachshund
akc-dachshund-breed-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Hound Group) establishing weight bands (standard usually 16 to 32 pounds; miniature 11 pounds and under), three coat varieties, accepted colors/patterns (including wild boar, dapple, brindle, piebald), and disqualifications.

akc-dachshund-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Dachshund Dog Breed Information
akc-dachshund-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile covering German badger-hunting history, height (8-9 in standard, 5-6 in miniature), weight (16-32 lb standard, 11 lb & under miniature), lifespan (12-16 years), recommended health tests (Patella, Cardiac, Ophthalmologist), grooming, and back-care guidance.

dca-health-statement.name: Dachshund Club of America - Official Health Statement
dca-health-statement.note: Official Dachshund Club of America Health Statement (revised May 2022) specifying CHIC screening protocols (Patella evaluation at 12+ months, ACVO/CAER eye exam within 2 years prior to breeding, Basic Cardiac exam at 12+ months and within 2 years prior to breeding) and breeder consideration of Lafora disease, IVDD, and PRA.

ofa-dachshund-chic-requirements.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals - Dachshund CHIC Requirements

ukc-portuguese-sheepdog-breed-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (Herding Dog Group, recognized 2006) covering conformation, rectangular proportions, monkey-like facial expression, and highly intelligent herding behavior.

wikimedia-cao-da-serra-de-aires-erk.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Cao da serra de aires.jpg
wikimedia-cao-da-serra-de-aires-erk.note: High-resolution photograph (799 x 600 px) of an adult Cão da Serra de Aires standing outdoors by Erk (captured 2005-09-24, uploaded by Erk~commonswiki 2006-03-31). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-cao-da-serra-de-aires-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Cão da Serra de Aires 1.jpg
wikimedia-cao-da-serra-de-aires-canarian.note: Photograph (1774 x 1222 px) featuring a close-up of a Cão da Serra de Aires by Canarian (captured and uploaded 2013-10-18). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-shikoku-official-standard.name: FCI - Shikoku Official Breed Standard No. 319
fci-shikoku-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 319. Covers Japanese origin, Group 5 Spitz and primitive types, Section 5 Asian Spitz and related breeds classification without working trial, sesame/red coat colors, and withers height (males 52 cm, females 49 cm, with a tolerance of +/- 3 cm).

fci-shikoku-nomenclature.name: FCI - Shikoku Breed Nomenclature (No. 319)
fci-shikoku-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Japan as country of origin, Group 5 Section 5 classification without working trial, definitive recognition date (1982-01-26), and official multilingual name (Shikoku).

nippo-shikoku-breed-standard.name: Nihon Ken Hozonkai (NIPPO) - Shikoku Standard and Data
nippo-shikoku-breed-standard.note: Official Japanese parent club and primary registry (NIPPO) breed data detailing Kochi-ken regional history, wild boar hunting utility, and specific working weight ranges (17-23 kg for males, 15-18 kg for females).

akc-shikoku-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Shikoku Dog Breed Information
akc-shikoku-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Foundation Stock Service) covering Japanese national monument designation, primitive hunting heritage, lifespan (12-15 years typically), temperament, high prey drive, and grooming.

wikimedia-shikoku-dog-bigsteeve.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Shikoku dog.jpg
wikimedia-shikoku-dog-bigsteeve.note: Photograph (362 x 480 px) of an adult Shikoku dog shown in profile, with a curled tail, by Bigsteeve (uploaded by Caronna 2006-10-28). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-shikoku-ken-1-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Shikoku Ken 1.jpg
wikimedia-shikoku-ken-1-canarian.note: Photograph (4592 x 3056 px) of a sesame Shikoku standing alert outdoors by Canarian (captured and uploaded 2016-12-10). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

akc-american-hairless-terrier-breed-stan.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the American Hairless Terrier
akc-american-hairless-terrier-breed-stan.note: Official AKC breed standard (Terrier Group, approved 2015, effective 2016) establishing height (12 to 16 inches), proportionate weight, hairless and coated varieties, complete dentition, and energetic terrier temperament.

akc-american-hairless-terrier-breed-prof.name: American Kennel Club - American Hairless Terrier Dog Breed Information
akc-american-hairless-terrier-breed-prof.note: Official AKC breed profile covering Louisiana history, Josephine foundation, recessive SGK3 mutation, weight (12-16 pounds), lifespan (14-16 years), apartment adaptability, temperament, and skin care.

ukc-american-hairless-terrier-breed-stan.name: United Kennel Club - American Hairless Terrier Breed Standard
ukc-american-hairless-terrier-breed-stan.note: Official UKC breed standard (Terrier Group, recognized 2004) covering conformation, rectangular proportions, skin colors, lack of dominant lethal dental issues, and highly affectionate companion behavior.

ahtca-american-hairless-terrier-health.name: American Hairless Terrier Club of America - Health and Disease Testing
ahtca-american-hairless-terrier-health.note: Official national parent club health portal documenting structural health risks and mandatory pre-breeding health testing, explicitly requiring Primary Lens Luxation (PLL), PRA-prcd, Cardiac, and Patellar Luxation screenings.
ahtca-american-hairless-terrier-health.publisher: American Hairless Terrier Club of America

ofa-american-hairless-terrier-chic-requi.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals - American Hairless Terrier CHIC Requirements
ofa-american-hairless-terrier-chic-requi.note: Official OFA Canine Health Information Center (CHIC) testing requirements for the American Hairless Terrier, mandating CAER Eye examination, Clinical Patellar Luxation, Legg-Calve-Perthes, Cardiac, and DNA tests for PLL and PRA-prcd.

wikimedia-american-hairless-terrier-in-f.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:American Hairless Terrier in Finland.jpg
wikimedia-american-hairless-terrier-in-f.note: High-resolution photograph (600 x 526 px) of a male American Hairless Terrier standing outdoors by Canarian (captured and uploaded 2016-10-29). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-american-hairless-terrier-adel.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:American Hairless Terrier Adelor.jpg
wikimedia-american-hairless-terrier-adel.note: Photograph (1536 x 2304 px) featuring an adult American Hairless Terrier standing on a rocky surface by Nyaah (captured and uploaded 2009-07-23). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

van-asch-2005-portuguese-dog-mtdna.name: van Asch B. et al. (2005). MtDNA diversity among four Portuguese autochthonous dog breeds: a fine-scale characterisation. BMC Genetics 6:37
van-asch-2005-portuguese-dog-mtdna.note: Sampled 143 dogs from four Portuguese breeds. The Castro Laboreiro Dog showed a 95% frequency of a single newly described haplotype in haplogroup A. Notes that 96 Castro Laboreiro dogs were registered with the Portuguese Kennel Club in 2003 and describes the region as secluded. doi:10.1186/1471-2156-6-37.

grupo-lobo-castro-laboreiro-genealogical.name: Grupo Lobo - Genealogical analysis of Castro Laboreiro Dog nucleus reveals a healthy group
grupo-lobo-castro-laboreiro-genealogical.note: Wolf-conservation association's report on a pedigree study of its Castro Laboreiro breeding nucleus (168 animals), done with the Clube do Cão de Castro Laboreiro and the University of Lisbon; found the population genetically healthy. No inbreeding figures are given.

royal-canin-castro-laboreiro-dog.name: Royal Canin - Castro Laboreiro Dog breed page
royal-canin-castro-laboreiro-dog.note: Pet-food company breed page. Gives average life expectancy 11-13 years, size category Large and 'requires minimal grooming'. Lists no breed-specific health conditions.

ucdavis-vgl-american-eskimo-dog-genetic-.name: UC Davis Veterinary Genetics Laboratory - Genetic Diversity Testing for American Eskimo Dogs (May 2021 report)
ucdavis-vgl-american-eskimo-dog-genetic-.publisher: University of California, Davis, Veterinary Genetics Laboratory
ucdavis-vgl-american-eskimo-dog-genetic-.note: Preliminary report on 112 dogs (60 Standard, 38 Miniature, 14 Toy). Finds low overall diversity, Standards most inbred (about 6.8%), Toy and Miniature more diverse. Breed history: German multipurpose farm dog; renamed when Mr. and Mrs. F.M. Hall registered dogs with UKC under the kennel name 'American Eskimo'; 1930s circuses including Barnum and Bailey; studbook closed 1969; AEDCA named 1985; AKC recognition 1995.

cai-2019-american-eskimo-dog-diabetes-he.name: Cai S.V. et al. (2019). Heritability and complex segregation analysis of diabetes mellitus in American Eskimo Dogs. Journal of Veterinary Internal Medicine 33(5)
cai-2019-american-eskimo-dog-diabetes-he.note: PMID 31318104. 156 American Eskimo Dogs (38 with diabetes). Heritability 0.62 (wide interval); polygenic inheritance with no single gene of large effect. Neutered dogs had much higher predicted probability of diabetes than intact dogs. Recruited sample, so not a prevalence estimate.

healthy-paws-american-eskimo-dog.name: Healthy Paws Pet Insurance - American Eskimo Dog breed guide
healthy-paws-american-eskimo-dog.note: Medically reviewed by a veterinarian. Weight Toy 6-10 lb, Miniature 10-20 lb, Standard 25-35 lb; life expectancy 13 to 15 years; shedding high.

hills-american-eskimo-dog.name: Hill's Pet Nutrition - American Eskimo Dog breed page
hills-american-eskimo-dog.note: Gives sex-specific weights (males Toy 8-11, Miniature 12-21, Standard 22-40 lb; females Toy 6-9, Miniature 10-19, Standard 20-35 lb) and longevity 12-14 years, which differ from the commonly quoted figures.

fci-fox-terrier-wire-official-standard.name: FCI - Fox Terrier (Wire) Official Breed Standard No. 169
fci-fox-terrier-wire-official-standard.note: English FCI Standard No. 169 (original valid standard dated 2026-09-08; document dated 2026-10-06). Origin Great Britain; Group 3, Section 1. Height at withers not exceeding 39 cm in dogs, females slightly less; ideal show weight 8,25 kg for males, females slightly less; dense, very wiry coat 2 cm on shoulder to 4 cm on withers with softer undercoat; white predominates with black, black and tan or tan markings.

fci-fox-terrier-wire-nomenclature.name: FCI - Fox Terrier (Wire) Breed Nomenclature (No. 169)
fci-fox-terrier-wire-nomenclature.note: FCI nomenclature record: official names in English, French, German and Spanish; Group 3 Terriers, Large and medium sized Terriers; working trial only for countries that applied for it; country of origin Great Britain; accepted on a definitive basis 1955-05-13; valid standard published 2026-09-08.

royal-kennel-club-fox-terrier-wire-breed.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Fox Terrier (Wire) Breed Standard
royal-kennel-club-fox-terrier-wire-breed.note: UK (country of origin) breed standard, last updated 1 August 2025. Height at withers not exceeding 39 cms (15½ ins) in dogs, bitches slightly less; ideal show weight 8 kgs (18 lbs) for dogs, bitches slightly less; dense, very wiry coat; white predominating with black, tan, or black and tan markings; temperament friendly, forthcoming and fearless.

royal-kennel-club-fox-terrier-wire-breed.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Fox Terrier (Wire) Breed Information
royal-kennel-club-fox-terrier-wire-breed.note: Breed page: size small; exercise up to 1 hour per day; small house; small/medium garden; grooming more than once a week; coat medium; sheds; lifespan over 12 years; not a vulnerable native breed. Pre-breeding screening: BVA/KC/ISDS eye scheme. History of separate Wire classes in the 1870s and the post-war toy on a wheeled frame.

akc-wire-fox-terrier-breed-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Wire Fox Terrier
akc-wire-fox-terrier-breed-standard.note: AKC standard approved February 9, 1991, effective March 27, 1991. Height should not exceed 15½ inches at the withers; 18 pounds in show condition, bitch some two pounds less with a margin of one pound either way; coat ¾ to one inch on shoulders and neck, lengthening to 1½ inches on withers, back, ribs and quarters.

akc-wire-fox-terrier-health-testing.name: American Kennel Club - Terrier Group Health Testing Requirements (Wire Fox Terrier)
akc-wire-fox-terrier-health-testing.note: National breed club recommended tests for the Wire Fox Terrier: Patella Evaluation and Cardiac Exam. The page covers every Terrier Group breed; this entry records the Wire Fox Terrier row only.

wire-fox-terrier-breed-health-conservati.name: Breed Health and Conservation Plan - Wire Fox Terrier (Version 1, July 2020)
wire-fox-terrier-breed-health-conservati.publisher: The Kennel Club / Wire Fox Terrier Association
wire-fox-terrier-breed-health-conservati.note: Kennel Club BHCP, Version 1, July 2020, hosted by the Wire Fox Terrier Association. Priorities: VDEGS and health data collection; allergic skin disease named as a concern. 2020 survey of 1,070 dogs: skin/coat/ear 30.6% (allergic skin disease 74.3% of these), tumours 17%, digestive 12.5%, eye 11.9%; average age at death 11.3 years; cancer and degenerative myelopathy leading causes of death. DNA tests for VDEGS, PLL and DM (not KC recognised). Publication day not stated.

hytonen-2016-canine-rare-bone-diseases-v.name: Hytönen et al. (2016) - Canine Models of Human Rare Bone Diseases: Caffey, van den Ende-Gupta, and Raine Syndromes
hytonen-2016-canine-rare-bone-diseases-v.note: PLoS Genet 12(5):e1006037, PMID 27187611. Describes a congenital skeletal syndrome in Wire Fox Terriers (severe underbite and severe patellar luxation) caused by a SCARF2 deletion (c.865_866delTC), a model of human van den Ende-Gupta syndrome.

american-fox-terrier-club-breed-standard.name: American Fox Terrier Club - Breed Standards and History
american-fox-terrier-club-breed-standard.note: US parent club history: first AKC Fox Terrier registration (Cricket, 1885); Wire ancestry and early Smooth crosses; Caesar in King Edward VII's 1910 funeral procession; Thin Man and Asta in the 1930s; AKC separate recognition of Smooth and Wire in 1985. Its Westminster count (13) is out of date.

akc-westminster-fun-facts.name: American Kennel Club - Fun Facts About the Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show
akc-westminster-fun-facts.note: Article updated 16 January 2026. States that Wire Fox Terriers have won Best in Show at Westminster 15 times, the first being Ch Matford Vic in 1915.

wikimedia-fox-terrier-wire-state-farm-01.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:01 Wire Fox terrier.jpg
wikimedia-fox-terrier-wire-state-farm-01.note: Photograph by State Farm (Flickr), taken 2013-02-23, uploaded to Commons 2014-03-08 via Flickr upload bot by Frei sein; 2307 × 1656 px; Flickr licence review confirmed CC BY 2.0.

wikimedia-fox-terrier-wire-lilly-m-r01.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Fox Terrier Wire R 01.JPG
wikimedia-fox-terrier-wire-lilly-m-r01.note: Photograph by Małgorzata Miłaszewska (Lilly M) at a dog show in Racibórz, taken 2007-06-10, uploaded 2007-06-27; 2710 × 1814 px. Offered under GFDL 1.2+ and CC BY-SA 2.5 / 2.0 / 1.0; this catalog uses CC BY-SA 2.5.

fci-polish-lowland-sheepdog-official-sta.name: FCI - Polish Lowland Sheepdog (Polski Owczarek Nizinny) Official Breed Standard No. 251
fci-polish-lowland-sheepdog-official-sta.note: English FCI Standard No. 251 (valid standard published 07.08.1998; translation by Mrs. Peggy Davis). Origin Poland; Group 1, Section 1 Sheepdogs, without working trial. Height males 45 - 50 cm, females 42 - 47 cm; no weight given; height to length 9 : 10; coarse, dense, thick coat with soft undercoat; all colours and patches acceptable.

fci-polish-lowland-sheepdog-nomenclature.name: FCI - Polish Lowland Sheepdog Breed Nomenclature (No. 251)
fci-polish-lowland-sheepdog-nomenclature.note: FCI nomenclature record: official names in English, French, German, Spanish and Polish; Group 1 Sheepdogs and Cattledogs, Section Sheepdogs; no working trial; country of origin Poland; accepted on a definitive basis 1963-10-05; valid standard published 1998-08-07.

royal-kennel-club-polish-lowland-sheepdo.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Polish Lowland Sheepdog Breed Standard
royal-kennel-club-polish-lowland-sheepdo.note: UK breed standard, last updated 1 April 2025. Dogs 45-50 cm (17 3/4-19 3/4 in), bitches 42-47 cm (16 1/2-18 1/2 in); no weight; long, dense, shaggy coat of harsh texture with soft undercoat; trimming to alter outline not permitted; all colours other than merle; lively but self-controlled, watchful, clever, perceptive, excellent memory, easy to train.

royal-kennel-club-polish-lowland-sheepdo.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Polish Lowland Sheepdog Breed Information
royal-kennel-club-polish-lowland-sheepdo.note: Breed page: size medium; exercise more than 2 hours per day; small house; large garden; grooming every day; coat long; sheds; lifespan over 10 years. Best Practice screening: BVA/KC/ISDS eye scheme, BVA/KC hip dysplasia scheme, and PRA (rcd4) DNA test recognised May 2026 (Best Practice from December 2026). History: often born without a tail; dogs in Scotland from the 16th century.

akc-polish-lowland-sheepdog-breed-standa.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Polish Lowland Sheepdog
akc-polish-lowland-sheepdog-breed-standa.note: AKC standard approved May 12, 2009, effective July 1, 2009. Height 18 to 20 inches for dogs and 17 to 19 inches for bitches; no weight; double coated; all coat colors acceptable; stable and self confident.

akc-polish-lowland-sheepdog-health-testi.name: American Kennel Club - Herding Group Health Testing Requirements (Polish Lowland Sheepdog)
akc-polish-lowland-sheepdog-health-testi.note: National breed club recommended tests for the Polish Lowland Sheepdog: Hip Evaluation and Ophthalmologist Evaluation. The page covers every Herding Group breed; this entry records the Polish Lowland Sheepdog row only.

akc-polish-lowland-sheepdog-history-arti.name: American Kennel Club - Polish Lowland Sheepdog History: Rebuilding the Breed After WWII
akc-polish-lowland-sheepdog-history-arti.note: AKC Staff article (8 October 2021): Central Asian ancestry; 1514 voyage to Scotland story; 1924 Warsaw show; Psyche legend; Polish Kennel Club formed 1948; Danuta Hryniewicz and Smok; Polish standard accepted 1959; first international show 1965 in Czechoslovakia; APONC formed 1987; AKC Herding Group recognition 2001. Its 1959 date for FCI recognition differs from the FCI nomenclature (1963).

ucdavis-vgl-polish-lowland-sheepdog-gene.name: UC Davis Veterinary Genetics Laboratory - Genetic Diversity Testing for Polish Lowland Sheepdog
ucdavis-vgl-polish-lowland-sheepdog-gene.note: Breed genetic diversity report (generated 2024-02-28, updated 2024-07-24; 103 dogs). Smok sired the first ten litters in the 1950s; average lifespan 12 to 14 years; OFA hip dysplasia 16% (n=114); PRA rcd4 found in at least 90% of affected dogs from Sweden and the US; other conditions hypothyroidism, cataracts, NCL, PDA; genetic diversity among the lowest of breeds tested; breeding recommendations.

svensson-2016-pon-progressive-retinal-at.name: Svensson et al. (2016) - Progressive retinal atrophy in the Polski Owczarek Nizinny dog: a clinical and genetic study
svensson-2016-pon-progressive-retinal-at.note: Vet Ophthalmol. 2016;19(3):195-205, doi 10.1111/vop.12284 (epub 2015-05-22). Clinical study of 82 Swedish PON dogs: PRA is late-onset with slow progression, early rod loss and later cone loss; the rcd4 mutation in C2ORF71 was associated with most cases tested; other forms cannot be excluded.

narfstrom-2007-pon-neuronal-ceroid-lipof.name: Narfström et al. (2007) - Neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis: clinical and morphologic findings in nine affected Polish Owczarek Nizinny (PON) dogs
narfstrom-2007-pon-neuronal-ceroid-lipof.note: Vet Ophthalmol 2007;10(2):111-20, PMID 17324167. Nine Swedish PON dogs with NCL showed behavioural abnormalities, motor disturbances and visual impairment or blindness; granular storage deposits in brain and retina.

wikimedia-polish-lowland-sheepdog-pleple.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Polski owczarek nizinny rybnik-kamien pl.jpg
wikimedia-polish-lowland-sheepdog-pleple.note: Photograph by Pleple2000 of a Polish Lowland Sheepdog at a dog show in Rybnik-Kamień, Poland; 2468 × 2172 px. Offered under CC BY-SA 4.0, 3.0, 2.5, 2.0 and 1.0 and GFDL 1.2+; this catalog uses CC BY-SA 4.0. The page's date field reads '07.10.07', which is ambiguous, so no capture date is recorded.

wikimedia-polish-lowland-sheepdog-beltap.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Storalvens Dione.JPG
wikimedia-polish-lowland-sheepdog-beltap.note: Photograph by Beltapar of the Polish Lowland Sheepdog Storälvens Dione; uploaded 2009-02-03; 3264 × 2448 px; licensed CC BY 3.0. The page's date field is malformed ('21 November 0008'), so no capture date is recorded.

koiramuseo-finnish-spitz-history.name: Koiramuseo (Finnish Dog Museum) - The Finnish Spitz is bred from a native landrace
koiramuseo-finnish-spitz-history.note: Finnish Kennel Club founded 1889; Hugo Sandberg's description of the Finnish Barking Bird Dog; Hugo Roos breeding and testing dogs in Lapland and Kainuu; first breed show in Oulu in 1892 with 93 dogs; new standard and name Finnish Spitz in 1897; current Finnish name form from 1946.

kennelliitto-suomenpystykorva-flag-day-2.name: Suomen Kennelliitto - Press release: a flag day for Finland's national dog (2023)
kennelliitto-suomenpystykorva-flag-day-2.note: The Finnish Spitz club (Suomen Pystykorvajärjestö) declared the first Saturday of August the breed's flag day, first celebrated on 5 August 2023 in Siilinjärvi.

mnb-erdelyi-kopo-collector-coin-2023.name: Magyar Nemzeti Bank - Transylvanian Hound collector coin (3 October 2023)
mnb-erdelyi-kopo-collector-coin-2023.note: Hungary's central bank announced a 3,000-forint collector coin 'Erdélyi kopó' issued 4 October 2023. States that Parliament declared all domestic dog breeds national treasures in 2004, that the breed declined after World War II, and that it was bred again from 1968.

hungarian-native-dog-breeds-decree-2016.name: Hungarian government decree 62/2016 on the conservation of Hungarian dog breeds (Nemzeti Jogszabálytár)
hungarian-native-dog-breeds-decree-2016.note: Lists nine Hungarian dog breeds: drótszőrű magyar vizsla, erdélyi kopó, komondor, kuvasz, magyar agár, mudi, puli, pumi and rövidszőrű magyar vizsla.

petmd-transylvanian-hound.name: PetMD - Transylvanian Hound breed page
petmd-transylvanian-hound.note: Says the breed lives an average of 10 to 12 years, is generally healthy, sheds an average amount, and lists hip and elbow dysplasia as issues to be aware of. Not a breed-specific health study.

fci-south-russian-shepherd-dog-official-.name: FCI - South Russian Shepherd Dog Official Breed Standard No. 326
fci-south-russian-shepherd-dog-official-.note: English FCI Standard No. 326 (official valid standard published 22.08.2017; document dated 12.12.2017; translated by Dmitry Mamontov and Anna Samsonova, edited by Dr. Eugene Yerusalimsky). Origin Russia; Group 1, Section 1, without working trial. History: Spanish ancestry noted in 1830 law collection, 1867 Paris gold medal, 1898 Askania-Nova selection, first standard early 1930s. Height males not less than 66 cm, females not less than 62 cm; weight males not less than 35 kg, females not less than 30 kg; coat not less than 10 cm.

fci-south-russian-shepherd-dog-nomenclat.name: FCI - South Russian Shepherd Dog Breed Nomenclature (No. 326)
fci-south-russian-shepherd-dog-nomenclat.note: FCI nomenclature record: official names in English, French, German and Spanish; Group 1, Section Sheepdogs; no working trial; country of origin Russian Federation; accepted on a definitive basis 1983-09-30; valid standard published 2017-08-22.

ukc-south-russian-shepherd-dog-standard.name: United Kennel Club - South Russian Shepherd Dog Breed Standard
ukc-south-russian-shepherd-dog-standard.note: UKC standard revised 1 January 2009. Recognized 1 January 1996 as the South Russian Ovcharka; renamed South Russian Shepherd Dog and moved to the Herding Dog Group effective 1 January 2009. Height males minimum 25 inches, females minimum 24 inches; no weight; distrustful of strangers and dominant in character; adapts to many climates; colours include white, straw, shades of grey and grey speckled.

wikimedia-south-russian-ovcharka-przykut.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Owczarek południoworosyjski jużak 00p.jpg
wikimedia-south-russian-ovcharka-przykut.note: Photograph by Przykuta of a South Russian Ovcharka at a dog show in Racibórz, Poland, taken June 2007 (day not stated); 3112 × 1980 px; licensed CC BY-SA 3.0.

wikimedia-south-russian-ovcharka-mason-1.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Owtchar aka Russian Sheepdog from 1915.JPG
wikimedia-south-russian-ovcharka-mason-1.note: Historical illustration from W. E. Mason, Dogs of All Nations (1915); author not named; 1812 × 1353 px; marked public domain in the United States as first published before 1931.

fci-border-collie-official-standard.name: FCI - Border Collie Official Breed Standard No. 297
fci-border-collie-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 297 (valid standard dated 2009-06-24, published 2009-10-28). Covers Great Britain origin, Group 1 Sheepdogs and Cattledogs, Section 1 Sheepdogs classification with working trial, athletic build, 'intense eye', two coat varieties (rough and smooth), and ideal withers height (males 53 cm, females slightly less).

fci-border-collie-nomenclature.name: FCI - Border Collie Breed Nomenclature (No. 297)
fci-border-collie-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Great Britain as country of origin, Group 1 Section 1 classification with working trial, definitive recognition date (1977-09-28), and official multilingual name (Border Collie).

akc-border-collie-breed-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Border Collie
akc-border-collie-breed-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Herding Group, approved 2004) establishing height (19-22 inches males, 18-21 inches females), proportionate weight, stealthy gait, keen expression, and highly intelligent working temperament.

akc-border-collie-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Border Collie Dog Breed Information
akc-border-collie-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile covering Anglo-Scottish border history, Old Hemp foundation, weight (30-55 pounds), lifespan (12-15 years), extreme intelligence, and grooming.

bcsa-border-collie-health.name: Border Collie Society of America - Breed Health and Genetics
bcsa-border-collie-health.note: Official national parent club health portal documenting structural health risks and mandatory pre-breeding health testing, explicitly detailing Collie Eye Anomaly (CEA), Trapped Neutrophil Syndrome (TNS), MDR1 sensitivity, Epilepsy, and Deafness (BAER).

ofa-border-collie-chic-requirements.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals - Border Collie CHIC Requirements
ofa-border-collie-chic-requirements.note: Official OFA Canine Health Information Center (CHIC) testing requirements for the Border Collie, mandating Radiographic Hip Dysplasia evaluation, CAER Eye examination, and Collie Eye Anomaly (CEA) DNA test.

wikimedia-border-collie-portrait-canaria.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Border Collie portrait.jpg
wikimedia-border-collie-portrait-canaria.note: High-resolution photograph (2500 x 1667 px) of a classic black and white Border Collie standing outdoors by Canarian (captured and uploaded 2018-05-14). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-border-collie-working-sannse.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Border Collie working.jpg
wikimedia-border-collie-working-sannse.note: Photograph (800 x 600 px) featuring a Border Collie in a low, crouching stance working in a grassy field by Sannse (captured and uploaded 2004-10-12). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-pont-audemer-spaniel-official-standa.name: FCI - Pont-Audemer Spaniel (Epagneul de Pont-Audemer) Official Breed Standard No. 114
fci-pont-audemer-spaniel-official-standa.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 114 (valid standard dated 1964-05-06, published 1998-09-25). Covers French origin, Group 7 Pointing Dogs, Section 1.2 Continental Pointing Dogs (Spaniel type) classification with working trial, stocky build, curly brown or roan coat, distinct curly topknot, and withers height (52 to 58 cm).

fci-pont-audemer-spaniel-nomenclature.name: FCI - Pont-Audemer Spaniel Breed Nomenclature (No. 114)
fci-pont-audemer-spaniel-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming France as country of origin, Group 7 Section 1.2 classification with working trial, definitive recognition date (1954-12-14), and official multilingual name (Epagneul de Pont-Audemer).

scc-epagneul-de-pont-audemer-standard.name: Société Centrale Canine - Standard et Profil de l'Epagneul de Pont-Audemer
scc-epagneul-de-pont-audemer-standard.note: Official French kennel club (Société Centrale Canine / SCC) breed profile and standard for Epagneul de Pont-Audemer, documenting Marais Vernier heritage, height, weight (20-27 kg), hunting traits, and exceptionally docile 'petit clown' character.

akc-pont-audemer-spaniel-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Pont-Audemer Spaniel Dog Breed Information
akc-pont-audemer-spaniel-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Foundation Stock Service) covering 'petit clown des marais' nickname, water spaniel crosses, weight (44-60 pounds), lifespan (12-14 years), temperament, and grooming.

ukc-pont-audemer-spaniel-breed-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Pont-Audemer Spaniel Breed Standard
ukc-pont-audemer-spaniel-breed-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (Gun Dog Group, recognized 1996) covering conformation, curly topknot, stocky build, flat curly brown and white coat, and pointing behavior.

club-epagneul-pont-audemer-profile.name: Club des Épagneuls de Picardie et Pont Audemer (CEPPA) - L'Epagneul de Pont-Audemer
club-epagneul-pont-audemer-profile.note: Official French parent breed club portal (CEPPA) documenting the morphological traits, curly coat rules, average weight, lifespan, and mandatory health screening requirements for Hip Dysplasia.
club-epagneul-pont-audemer-profile.publisher: Club des Épagneuls de Picardie et Pont Audemer

wikimedia-epagneul-de-pont-audemer-canar.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Epagneul de Pont-Audemer.jpg
wikimedia-epagneul-de-pont-audemer-canar.note: High-resolution photograph (2592 x 1944 px) of an adult Pont-Audemer Spaniel standing outdoors by Canarian (captured and uploaded 2015-05-18). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-pont-audemer-spaniel-1-lilly-m.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Pont Audemer Spaniel 1.jpg
wikimedia-pont-audemer-spaniel-1-lilly-m.note: Photograph (2304 x 1728 px) of a Pont-Audemer Spaniel in a grassy field by Lilly M (captured 2007-06-16, uploaded 2007-06-25). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-jamthund-official-standard.name: FCI - Jämthund (Swedish Elkhound) Official Breed Standard No. 42
fci-jamthund-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 42 (valid standard dated 2019-09-04, published 2019-10-28). Covers Swedish origin, Group 5 Spitz and primitive type, Section 2 Nordic Hunting Dogs classification with working trial, large rectangular spitz build, grey coat with cream 'wolf markings', loosely curled tail, and withers height (males 57-65 cm, females 52-60 cm).

fci-jamthund-nomenclature.name: FCI - Jämthund Breed Nomenclature (No. 42)
fci-jamthund-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Sweden as country of origin, Group 5 Section 2 classification with working trial, definitive recognition date (1954-12-11), and official multilingual names (Jämthund, Swedish Elkhound).

skk-jamthund-breed-standard.name: Svenska Kennelklubben - Standard för Jämthund
skk-jamthund-breed-standard.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed standard and profile detailing the 1946 recognition driven by Aksel Lindström, distinction from the Norwegian Elkhound, moose hunting heritage, and working weight conventions.

ukc-jamthund-breed-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Jämthund Breed Standard
ukc-jamthund-breed-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (Northern Breed Group, recognized 2006) covering conformation, rectangular proportions, primitive spitz build, grey double coat, and independent big-game hunting behavior.

wikimedia-jamthund-woods-aanvandare.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Jämthund (Swedish Elkhound) in the woods- 2 years old male- 2013-07-06 13-55.jpg
wikimedia-jamthund-woods-aanvandare.note: High-resolution photograph (2048 x 1536 px) of a two-year-old male Jämthund standing in the woods by a Wikimedia Commons User (uploaded by Aanvändare 2013-07-06). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-jamthund-drvd-anka-friedrich.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Jämthund drvd.png
wikimedia-jamthund-drvd-anka-friedrich.note: Photograph (1632 x 1178 px) featuring a Jämthund in profile by Anka Friedrich (derivative of original work by Jörgen Blom, uploaded 2009-04-19). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

akc-bedlington-terrier-breed-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Bedlington Terrier
akc-bedlington-terrier-breed-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Terrier Group, approved September 12, 1967) establishing height (males 16-17.5 inches, females 15-16.5 inches), weight (17-23 pounds), pear-shaped head without stop, linty crisp coat, and lithe galloping build.

akc-bedlington-terrier-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Bedlington Terrier Dog Breed Information
akc-bedlington-terrier-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile covering English history, Rothbury Terrier nickname, 'head of a lamb and heart of a lion' descriptor, lifespan (12-14 years), apartment adaptability, extreme speed, and Copper Toxicosis health notes.

ofa-bedlington-terrier-chic-requirements.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals - Bedlington Terrier CHIC Requirements
ofa-bedlington-terrier-chic-requirements.note: Official OFA Canine Health Information Center (CHIC) testing requirements for the Bedlington Terrier, mandating CAER Eye examination, Clinical Patellar Luxation, and a DNA test for Copper Toxicosis (CT - BED).

wikimedia-bedlington-terrier-jeffrey-bea.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Bedlington Terrier.jpg
wikimedia-bedlington-terrier-jeffrey-bea.note: High-resolution photograph (4143 x 3228 px) of a Bedlington Terrier standing outdoors in profile by Jeffrey Beall (captured 2012-02-18, uploaded by Ltshears 2012-07-13). Licensed under CC BY-SA 2.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-bedlington-terrier-david-owsia.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Bedlington terrier.jpeg
wikimedia-bedlington-terrier-david-owsia.note: Photograph (2816 x 2120 px) featuring two Bedlington Terriers resting on the grass by David Owsiany (captured and uploaded 2009-07-29). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

the-kennel-club-estrela-mountain-dog-sta.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Estrela Mountain Dog Breed Standard
the-kennel-club-estrela-mountain-dog-sta.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Pastoral Group, updated April 2025) covering mastiff-type livestock-guardian conformation, small rose-shaped ears, hooked tail tip, coarse goat-hair-textured short and long coat varieties, and height (dogs 65-72 cm, bitches 62-68 cm, +4 cm tolerance).

estrela-mountain-dog-hip-dysplasia-study.name: Early Hip Laxity Examination in Predicting Moderate and Severe Hip Dysplasia in Estrela Mountain Dog (J Small Anim Pract 2008)
estrela-mountain-dog-hip-dysplasia-study.publisher: Journal of Small Animal Practice / PubMed
estrela-mountain-dog-hip-dysplasia-study.note: Peer-reviewed clinical study (Ginja et al., J Small Anim Pract 2008;49(12):641-646, PMID 18684138) evaluating early passive hip laxity between 4 and 12 months and adult radiographic hip scoring in 104 Estrela Mountain Dogs.

estrela-mountain-dog-hip-genetics-study-.name: Comparison of Estimates of Hip Dysplasia Genetic Parameters in Estrela Mountain Dog Using Linear and Threshold Models (J Anim Sci 2007)
estrela-mountain-dog-hip-genetics-study-.note: Peer-reviewed genetic study (Silvestre et al., J Anim Sci 2007;85(8):1880-1884, PMID 17468417) analyzing radiographic hip scores in 313 Estrela Mountain Dogs and estimating moderate-to-high heritability (0.38-0.43).

wikimedia-estrela-mountain-dog-6-month-m.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Estrela Mountain Dog 6 month old male.jpg
wikimedia-estrela-mountain-dog-6-month-m.note: Photograph (736 x 541 px) of a six-month-old fawn male Estrela Mountain Dog by Tracey Conner (Traceywashere), uploaded 2007-05-16. Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-thai-ridgeback-official-standard.name: FCI - Thai Ridgeback Dog Official Breed Standard No. 338
fci-thai-ridgeback-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 338 (valid standard dated 2003-05-26, published 2004-02-25). Covers Thailand origin, Group 5 Spitz and primitive types, Section 7 Primitive Type-Hunting Dogs classification without working trial, distinctive back ridge, spotted tongue, withers height (males 22-24 inches, females 20-22 inches, 1 inch tolerance).

fci-thai-ridgeback-nomenclature.name: FCI - Thai Ridgeback Breed Nomenclature (No. 338)
fci-thai-ridgeback-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Thailand as country of origin, Group 5 Section 7 classification without working trial, definitive recognition date (2003-05-26), and official multilingual name (Thai Ridgeback Dog).

akc-thai-ridgeback-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Thai Ridgeback Dog Breed Information
akc-thai-ridgeback-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Foundation Stock Service) covering ancient Thai origins, weight (35-75 pounds), lifespan (14-15 years), temperament, and grooming.

wikimedia-thai-ridgeback-dog-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Thai Ridgeback Dog.jpg
wikimedia-thai-ridgeback-dog-canarian.note: Photograph (590 x 600 px) of a female blue Thai Ridgeback standing outdoors by Canarian (captured and uploaded 2016-09-03). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-german-shorthaired-pointer-official-.name: FCI - German Shorthaired Pointer (Deutsch Kurzhaar) Official Breed Standard No. 119
fci-german-shorthaired-pointer-official-.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 119 (valid standard dated 2000-10-25). Covers German origin, Group 7 Pointing Dogs classification, versatile utility, short dense coat, solid brown or brown roan colors, and typical hunting conformation.

fci-german-shorthaired-pointer-nomenclat.name: FCI - German Shorthaired Pointer Breed Nomenclature (No. 119)
fci-german-shorthaired-pointer-nomenclat.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Germany as country of origin, Group 7 Section 1.1 classification, and official multilingual names (Deutsch Kurzhaar, German Shorthaired Pointer).

akc-german-shorthaired-pointer-breed-sta.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the German Shorthaired Pointer
akc-german-shorthaired-pointer-breed-sta.note: Official AKC breed standard (Sporting Group, approved 1992) establishing height (23-25 inches males, 21-23 inches females), weight (55-70 lbs males, 45-60 lbs females), solid liver or liver/white coat, webbed feet, and highly energetic working temperament.

akc-german-shorthaired-pointer-breed-pro.name: American Kennel Club - German Shorthaired Pointer Dog Breed Information
akc-german-shorthaired-pointer-breed-pro.note: Official AKC breed profile covering German hunting history, Prince Albrecht zu Solms-Braunfels, lifespan (10-12 years), extreme energy levels, 'velcro dog' affectionate nature, and grooming needs.

ofa-german-shorthaired-pointer-chic-requ.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals - German Shorthaired Pointer CHIC Requirements
ofa-german-shorthaired-pointer-chic-requ.note: Official OFA Canine Health Information Center (CHIC) testing requirements for the GSP, mandating Radiographic Hip and Elbow Dysplasia evaluation, CAER Eye examination, Cone Degeneration (CD) DNA test, and Basic Cardiac Evaluation.

wikimedia-german-shorthaired-pointer-ril.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:German Shorthaired Pointer (Deutsch Kurzhaar) in field.jpg
wikimedia-german-shorthaired-pointer-ril.note: High-resolution photograph (5184 x 3456 px) of a liver and white German Shorthaired Pointer standing alert in a field by ~riley (captured 2014-09-09, uploaded 2016-05-10). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

west-highland-white-terrier-vetcompass-s.name: West Highland White Terriers Under Primary Veterinary Care in the UK in 2016: Demography, Mortality and Disorders (Canine Genet Epidemiol 2019)
west-highland-white-terrier-vetcompass-s.publisher: Canine Genetics and Epidemiology / PubMed Central
west-highland-white-terrier-vetcompass-s.note: Peer-reviewed VetCompass epidemiological study (O'Neill et al., Canine Genet Epidemiol 2019;6:7, PMID 31497326, PMC6720841) of 6,605 UK West Highland White Terriers documenting mean adult bodyweight (10.1 kg males, 9.0 kg females), median longevity (13.4 years), and most common disorders (dental disease 15.7%, ear disease 10.6%, overgrown nails 7.2%, allergic skin disorder 6.5%, overweight 6.1%, cutaneous group 22.7%).

west-highland-white-terrier-ipf-study-20.name: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis in West Highland White Terriers: An Update (Vet J 2018)
west-highland-white-terrier-ipf-study-20.note: Peer-reviewed veterinary review (Clercx et al., Vet J 2018;242:53-58, PMID 30503545) detailing the clinical presentation, diagnostic imaging, secondary pulmonary hypertension, and pathology of canine idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (CIPF) in West Highland White Terriers.

west-highland-white-terrier-atopic-derma.name: Genome-Wide Linkage Study of Atopic Dermatitis in West Highland White Terriers (BMC Genet 2011)
west-highland-white-terrier-atopic-derma.note: Peer-reviewed genetic study (Baranowska Körberg et al., BMC Genet 2011;12:37, PMID 21507250, PMC3111396) characterizing heritable canine atopic dermatitis and secondary skin infections in West Highland White Terriers.

vetcompass-conformational-eyelid-disorde.name: Conformational Eyelid Disorders in Dogs Under Primary Veterinary Care in the UK (PLoS ONE 2025)
vetcompass-conformational-eyelid-disorde.note: Peer-reviewed UK VetCompass epidemiological study (PMC12208470) evaluating 2,250,417 dogs under primary veterinary care, including 10,741 Patterdale Terriers (0.07% conformational eyelid disorder prevalence).

wikimedia-patterdale-terrier-chilepine.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Patterdale.JPG
wikimedia-patterdale-terrier-chilepine.note: Photograph (1155 x 1080 px) of a black-and-tan Patterdale Terrier released into the public domain by author Chilepine (uploaded 2005-08-29).

appenzeller-sennenhund-ectopic-ureter-om.name: OMIA 001891-9615: Ectopic Ureter in Canis lupus familiaris (Swiss Mountain Dogs)
appenzeller-sennenhund-ectopic-ureter-om.publisher: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Animals (OMIA) / University of Sydney
appenzeller-sennenhund-ectopic-ureter-om.note: Veterinary genetics reference documenting congenital ectopic ureters in Swiss mountain dogs, including Bitterli (2011, Vetsuisse Faculty, University of Zurich) on the prevalence and clinical relevance of ectopic ureters in Entlebucher and Appenzeller Sennenhunde.

appenzeller-sennenhund-omia-nsdhl-2024.name: OMIA 002117-9615: Verrucous Epidermal Keratinocytic Nevi (NSDHL) in Canis lupus familiaris
appenzeller-sennenhund-omia-nsdhl-2024.publisher: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Animals (OMIA) / University of Sydney
appenzeller-sennenhund-omia-nsdhl-2024.note: Veterinary genetics record (OMIA Variant ID 1686, PMID 38659285, 2024) documenting an X-linked NSDHL gene variant associated with verrucous epidermal keratinocytic nevi in an Appenzeller Sennenhund.

fci-galgo-espanol-official-standard.name: FCI - Spanish Greyhound (Galgo Español) Official Breed Standard No. 285
fci-galgo-espanol-official-standard.note: English FCI Standard No. 285 (document dated 24.05.2002; official valid standard published 26.05.1982; translation by Mrs. Peggy Davis; official language Spanish). Group 10, Section 3, without working trial; origin Spain. Height males 62 to 70 cm, females 60 to 68 cm, 2 cm more admitted in subjects of perfect proportions; no weight. Smooth and semi-long hard-haired coats; all colours admitted.

fci-galgo-espanol-nomenclature.name: FCI - Spanish Greyhound (Galgo Español) Breed Nomenclature (No. 285)
fci-galgo-espanol-nomenclature.note: FCI nomenclature record: official names SPANISH GREYHOUND, LEVRIER ESPAGNOL, SPANISCHER WINDHUND, GALGO ESPAÑOL; section Short-haired Sighthounds; not subject to a working trial; country of origin Spain; accepted on a definitive basis 1971-08-10; official valid standard published 1982-05-26; official authentic language Spanish.

ukc-spanish-greyhound-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Spanish Greyhound Breed Standard
ukc-spanish-greyhound-standard.note: UKC standard (copyright 2006; no revision day printed). Recognized by the UKC in 2006; Sighthound & Pariah Dog Group. Ideal height 24.5 to 27.5 inches (males), 23.5 to 26.5 inches (females), tolerance of 3/4 inch in otherwise excellent specimens; no weight. Serious and reserved, yet energetic and lively when hunting.

akc-how-breed-becomes-akc-recognized.name: American Kennel Club - How Does a Dog Breed Become AKC-Recognized?
akc-how-breed-becomes-akc-recognized.note: Article updated 6 November 2026. States the Galgo Español has hunted hare in Spain for millennia but too few dogs live in the United States to form a national club; the breed is not AKC-recognised and not in the Foundation Stock Service.

mesa-sanchez-2012-galgo-haematology.name: Mesa-Sanchez et al. (2012) - Haematological, blood gas and acid-base values in the Galgo Español (Spanish greyhound)
mesa-sanchez-2012-galgo-haematology.note: J Small Anim Pract 2012;53:398-403, PMID 22747732. Galgos had higher haematocrit, haemoglobin, erythrocyte count and pH, and lower platelet count, than dogs of other breeds. Publication day not confirmed.

zaldivar-lopez-2011-galgo-blood-gas.name: Zaldívar-López et al. (2011) - Blood gas analysis in a Spanish sighthound breed (Galgo Español)
zaldivar-lopez-2011-galgo-blood-gas.note: Vet Rec 2011;168:486 (short communication, May 2011; day not stated). Blood gas comparison of 20 Galgos Españoles with 17 mixed-breed dogs.

martinez-duran-2026-galgo-vector-borne-d.name: Martínez-Durán et al. (2026) - Vector-borne pathogen seroprevalence in Galgos Españoles from central Spain
martinez-duran-2026-galgo-vector-borne-d.publisher: Veterinary Parasitology: Regional Studies and Reports
martinez-duran-2026-galgo-vector-borne-d.note: Vet Parasitol Reg Stud Reports 2026;68:101437. In 160 galgos from central Spain, seroprevalence was Anaplasma phagocytophilum 10%, Ehrlichia canis 3.1%, Leishmania infantum 13.1% and Dirofilaria immitis 0%. DOI confirmed via the University of Zaragoza repository; publication day not confirmed. The name field paraphrases the article's subject.

shiel-2007-greyhound-thyroid-values.name: Shiel et al. (2007) - Thyroid hormone concentrations in young, healthy, pretraining greyhounds
shiel-2007-greyhound-thyroid-values.note: Vet Rec 2007;161:616-619, PMID 17982140. Total T4 was below the non-breed-specific reference range in 42 of 46 healthy young Greyhounds (91.3%). Used as general sighthound evidence, not as a Galgo-specific finding.

court-1999-sighthound-anesthesia.name: Court (1999) - Anesthesia of the sighthound
court-1999-sighthound-anesthesia.publisher: Clinical Techniques in Small Animal Practice / PubMed
court-1999-sighthound-anesthesia.note: Clin Tech Small Anim Pract 1999;14(1):38-43, PMID 10193044. Describes impaired drug biotransformation and prolonged recovery from some intravenous anaesthetics, especially thiopental, in sighthounds. General sighthound evidence, not Galgo-specific.

boe-ley-7-2023-animal-welfare.name: Ley 7/2023, de 28 de marzo, de protección de los derechos y el bienestar de los animales
boe-ley-7-2023-animal-welfare.publisher: Agencia Estatal Boletín Oficial del Estado
boe-ley-7-2023-animal-welfare.note: Spanish national animal welfare law, published in BOE no. 75 on 2023-03-29, in force 2023-09-29. Article 1 excludes hunting dogs, rehalas and auxiliary hunting animals from its scope, stating they remain covered by other European, state and regional rules.

fundacion-affinity-el-nunca-lo-haria-202.name: Fundación Affinity - Él Nunca Lo Haría Abandonment and Adoption Study (2026)
fundacion-affinity-el-nunca-lo-haria-202.note: Annual study of dogs and cats entering Spanish shelters. The 2026 study (2025 data) lists the end of the hunting season among the main reported reasons for dogs entering shelters, at 10.5% of cases. Figures cover all hunting dogs, not galgos alone. Publication day not stated.

wikimedia-galgo-espanol-netspy-running.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Galgo español running.jpg
wikimedia-galgo-espanol-netspy-running.note: Photograph by Netspy (own work), date field 20 April 2011, uploaded 2011-04-26; 3874 × 2583 px; licensed CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported.

wikimedia-galgo-espanol-tux-man-004.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Galgo espagnol 004.jpg
wikimedia-galgo-espanol-tux-man-004.note: Photograph by Tux-Man of a brindle male Galgo, date field and upload 2009-03-22; 2304 × 3072 px. Offered under GFDL 1.2+ and CC BY-SA 4.0, 3.0, 2.5, 2.0 and 1.0; this catalog uses CC BY-SA 4.0.

wikimedia-galgo-espanol-tux-man-male-bri.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Galgo Spanish male brindle.jpg
wikimedia-galgo-espanol-tux-man-male-bri.note: Photograph by Tux-Man, caption 'Lévrier Galgo Espagnol, mâle, de robe bringée', date field and upload 2009-01-21; 1260 × 1128 px. Offered under GFDL and CC BY-SA 3.0, 2.5, 2.0 and 1.0; this catalog uses CC BY-SA 3.0.

fci-chien-francais-blanc-et-noir-standar.name: FCI - French White and Black Hound (Chien Français Blanc et Noir) Official Breed Standard No. 220
fci-chien-francais-blanc-et-noir-standar.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 220. Covers French origin, Group 6 Scenthounds classification, large pack hound build, white and black coat with pale tan roebuck markings, and withers height (males 65-72 cm, females 62-68 cm).

fci-chien-francais-blanc-et-noir-nomencl.name: FCI - Chien Français Blanc et Noir Breed Nomenclature (No. 220)
fci-chien-francais-blanc-et-noir-nomencl.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming France as country of origin, Group 6 Section 1.1 classification with working trial, definitive recognition date (1957-12-15), and official multilingual name (Chien Français Blanc et Noir).

scc-francais-blanc-et-noir-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine - Standard et Profil du Francais blanc et noir
scc-francais-blanc-et-noir-profile.note: Official French kennel club (Société Centrale Canine / SCC) breed profile and standard for Francais blanc et noir, documenting its Hound of Saintonge origins, weight (environ 30 kg), deer hunting capabilities, and friendly, docile character.

wikimedia-francais-noir-et-blanc-abujoy.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Français noir et blanc.JPG
wikimedia-francais-noir-et-blanc-abujoy.note: Photograph (674 x 506 px) of a Chien Français Blanc et Noir standing in the pack at La Bourbansais by Abujoy (captured 2016-04-30, uploaded 2016-05-06). Licensed under CC BY 4.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

the-kennel-club-azawakh-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Azawakh (Imp) Breed Standard
the-kennel-club-azawakh-standard.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Hound Group, updated April 2025) establishing 9:10 body length to height ratio, prominent hip bones, withers height (dogs 64-74 cm, bitches 60-70 cm), weight (dogs 20-25 kg, bitches 15-20 kg), and reserved yet affectionate temperament.

azawakh-sighthound-hematology-study-2013.name: Haematological and Biochemical Variations Among Eight Sighthound Breeds (Aust Vet J 2013)
azawakh-sighthound-hematology-study-2013.note: Peer-reviewed clinical pathology study (Uhríková et al., Aust Vet J 2013;91(12):452-459, PMID 24571299) comparing 192 dogs across eight sighthound breeds including the Azawakh and establishing breed-specific hematological and biochemical reference variations.

azawakh-leukomyeloencephalopathy-case-20.name: A Leukomyeloencephalopathy of Unknown Origin in an Azawakh Dog (J Vet Med Sci 2017)
azawakh-leukomyeloencephalopathy-case-20.publisher: Journal of Veterinary Medical Science / PubMed
azawakh-leukomyeloencephalopathy-case-20.note: Peer-reviewed neurological case report (Mandrioli et al., J Vet Med Sci 2017;79(10):1678-1682, PMID 28926781) describing diffuse bilaterally symmetrical leukomyeloencephalopathy in a 6-year-old male Azawakh.

fci-poitevin-official-standard.name: FCI - Poitevin Official Breed Standard No. 24
fci-poitevin-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 24 (valid standard dated 1978-11-17, English publication dated 1997-03-04). Covers French origin, Group 6 Section 1.1 Large-sized Hounds classification with working trial, conformation, dewlap prohibition, wolf-foot structure, short glossy coat, tricolour/white-and-orange/wolf-coloured hair, black-and-white disqualification, and withers height (males 62-72 cm, females 60-70 cm). Does not publish weight or a historical summary.

fci-poitevin-nomenclature.name: FCI - Poitevin Breed Nomenclature (No. 24)
fci-poitevin-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming France as country of origin, Group 6 Section 1.1 Large-sized Hounds classification with working trial, definitive acceptance date (1963-09-30), and official multilingual names (Poitevin, Sabueso Poitevin).

club-du-chien-d-ordre-poitevin.name: Club du Chien d'Ordre (SCC) - Le Poitevin
club-du-chien-d-ordre-poitevin.note: Official French parent breed club portal affiliated with the Société Centrale Canine overseeing the Poitevin among Chiens d'Ordre bred for traditional French vénerie (pack hunting).
club-du-chien-d-ordre-poitevin.publisher: Club du Chien d'Ordre / Société Centrale Canine

ria-horter-poitevin-monograph.name: Ria Hörter - Poitevin 'Chien du Haut-Poitou': A Worker in the Grande Vénerie (Canine Chronicle)
ria-horter-poitevin-monograph.note: Published historical breed monograph (Canine Chronicle, May 2010, pp. 226-230) documenting Poitou province origins, Pictones etymology, 1692 creation, Ceris and Montemboeuf influences, 1957 adoption of the name Poitevin, 'hurleur' crying voice, 'Greyhound among the French hounds' nickname, 7-hour hunting endurance (citing Vicomte de Brissac, 1966), UKC 1996 recognition, and unsuitability for solitary or city living.

wikimedia-poitevin-hound-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Poitevin Hound.jpg
wikimedia-poitevin-hound-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (1800 x 1785 px current version; edited by GodeNehler on 2022-05-09 from original uploaded by Canarian on 2018-01-27, EXIF capture date 2017-12-09) of an adult Poitevin standing outdoors. Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-poitevin-hound-4-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Poitevin Hound 4.jpg
wikimedia-poitevin-hound-4-canarian.note: High-resolution side-profile photograph (2032 x 1660 px) of a Poitevin by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2017-12-09, uploaded 2018-01-27). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

royal-kennel-club-english-cocker-spaniel.name: The Royal Kennel Club — Spaniel (Cocker) Breeds A to Z
royal-kennel-club-english-cocker-spaniel.note: UK breed profile documenting 1893 separate breed recognition, historical under-25 lb classification, Welsh Springer outcrosses, grooming and exercise needs, Colour Watch, and Good/Best Practice health screening (AMS, prcd-PRA, AON, FN, eye/gonioscopy, hip scoring).

ecsca-health-clearances.name: ECSCA Health & Rescue Organization — Health Clearance Guidelines
ecsca-health-clearances.publisher: English Cocker Spaniel Club of America Health & Rescue Organization
ecsca-health-clearances.note: Parent-club health clearance recommendations covering DNA testing for FN, AON, prcd-PRA, AMS, and EIC, plus hip, patella, thyroid, CAER eye, and BAER hearing evaluations.

vetcompass-english-cocker-spaniel-2023.name: Demography and disorders of English Cocker Spaniels under primary veterinary care in the UK (VetCompass)
vetcompass-english-cocker-spaniel-2023.note: Primary-care epidemiological study of 10,313 English Cocker Spaniels in the UK (PMID 37202773) reporting periodontal disease (20.97%), otitis externa (10.09%), obesity (9.88%), anal sac impaction (8.07%), aggression (4.01%, higher in males and solid-colored dogs), median adult bodyweight (15.05 kg), average lifespan (11.44 years), and neoplasia as the leading cause of death.

english-cocker-spaniel-prcd-pra-2019.name: Allele Frequency of the C.5G>A Mutation in the PRCD Gene Responsible for Progressive Retinal Atrophy in English Cocker Spaniel Dogs
english-cocker-spaniel-prcd-pra-2019.note: Peer-reviewed study (PMID 31640229) evaluating the PRCD c.5G>A mutation causing progressive rod-cone degeneration (prcd-PRA) in English Cocker Spaniels.

wikimedia-english-cocker-spaniel-bill-gr.name: Wikimedia Commons — File:"Bill" - Cocker spaniel anglais 3.jpg
wikimedia-english-cocker-spaniel-bill-gr.note: Photograph of a 12-month-old English Cocker Spaniel by Jean-Pol GRANDMONT (captured 2016-10-16, uploaded 2021-01-28, 2404 x 3450 px). Licensed under CC BY 4.0.

fci-miniature-schnauzer-official-standar.name: FCI - Miniature Schnauzer (Zwergschnauzer) Official Breed Standard No. 183
fci-miniature-schnauzer-official-standar.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 183 (valid standard dated 2007-03-06, published 2007-04-18). Covers German origin (Frankfurt am Main area), Group 2 Section 1.2 Schnauzer classification without working trial, square build, harsh wiry double coat, four colours (pure black, pepper and salt, black/silver, pure white), withers height (30 to 35 cm), and weight (approximately 4 to 8 kg).

fci-miniature-schnauzer-nomenclature.name: FCI - Miniature Schnauzer Breed Nomenclature (No. 183)
fci-miniature-schnauzer-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Germany as country of origin, Group 2 Section 1.2 classification without working trial, four recognised coat colour varieties, and official multilingual names (Zwergschnauzer, Schnauzer Nain, Miniature Schnauzer).

akc-miniature-schnauzer-breed-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Miniature Schnauzer
akc-miniature-schnauzer-breed-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Terrier Group) establishing nearly square proportions, height (12 to 14 inches), hard wiry double coat, three AKC-allowed colours (salt and pepper, black and silver, solid black), and alert, spirited, obedient temperament.

akc-miniature-schnauzer-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Miniature Schnauzer Dog Breed Information
akc-miniature-schnauzer-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile covering 1890s German farm ratting history, Standard Schnauzer/Affenpinscher/Poodle ancestry, height (12-14 inches), weight (11-20 pounds), life expectancy (12-15 years), apartment adaptability, vocal watchdog nature, and recommended eye and cardiac testing.

amsc-miniature-schnauzer-health-topics.name: American Miniature Schnauzer Club - Canine Health Topics & Recommended Testing
amsc-miniature-schnauzer-health-topics.note: Official US parent breed club health portal documenting breed health priorities (cataracts, hyperlipidemia, Mycobacterium avium complex, pancreatitis, portosystemic shunts, urolithiasis) and recommended screenings (annual ACVO eye exam, cardiologist cardiac exam, and DNA tests for Myotonia Congenita, MAC, and PRA Type B HIVEP3).

miniature-schnauzer-mac-card9-study-2024.name: Increased susceptibility to Mycobacterium avium complex infection in miniature Schnauzer dogs caused by a codon deletion in CARD9 (Scientific Reports)
miniature-schnauzer-mac-card9-study-2024.note: Peer-reviewed study in Scientific Reports (Vol. 14, Article 10346, 2024) identifying an autosomal-recessive codon deletion in the CARD9 gene causing inherited susceptibility to systemic Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) infection in Miniature Schnauzers.

wikimedia-miniature-schnauzer-mattie-arm.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Miniature Schnauzer portrait Mattie.jpg
wikimedia-miniature-schnauzer-mattie-arm.note: Portrait photograph (1350 x 1600 px) of a black-and-silver Miniature Schnauzer named Mattie by Ron Armstrong (captured 2007-03-26, uploaded to Wikimedia Commons by Pharaoh Hound 2007-05-03, reviewed by FlickreviewR 2007-05-04). Licensed under CC BY 2.0.

wikimedia-miniature-schnauzer-female-max.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Miniature Schnauzer female at 7 months old.jpg
wikimedia-miniature-schnauzer-female-max.note: High-resolution photograph (3456 x 2304 px) of a 7-month-old female Miniature Schnauzer by Maxlens51 (EXIF capture date 2008-10-29, uploaded 2008-11-07). Released into the public domain by the copyright holder on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-pyrenean-sheepdog-longhaired-officia.name: FCI - Pyrenean Sheepdog Long-Haired (Chien de Berger des Pyrénées à poil long) Official Breed Standard No. 141
fci-pyrenean-sheepdog-longhaired-officia.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 141 (valid standard dated 2009-03-26, English publication dated 2009-05-25). Covers French Pyrenees origin, Group 1 Section 1 Sheepdogs classification with working trial, triangular head, tight black-edged lips, goat-to-wool coat forming cadenettes and matelotes, windswept muzzle hair leaving eyes visible, coat colours (fawn, grey, harlequin/slate blue, brindle, black), and withers height (males 42-48 cm, females 40-46 cm, +/- 2 cm tolerance). Does not publish numerical weight.

fci-pyrenean-sheepdog-longhaired-nomencl.name: FCI - Chien de Berger des Pyrénées à poil long Breed Nomenclature (No. 141)
fci-pyrenean-sheepdog-longhaired-nomencl.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming France as country of origin, Group 1 Section 1 Sheepdogs classification subject to a working trial, definitive acceptance date (1955-01-28), and official names (Chien de Berger des Pyrénées à poil long, Long-Haired Pyrenean Sheepdog).

scc-berger-des-pyrenees-poil-long-standa.name: Société Centrale Canine - Standard et Profil du Berger des Pyrénées à poil long
scc-berger-des-pyrenees-poil-long-standa.note: Official French kennel club (Société Centrale Canine / SCC) breed profile for Berger des Pyrénées à poil long documenting 1921-1925 first standard drafting, WWI military liaison dog service, weight listed as unspecified (NP), cadenettes/matelotes coat texture, headstrong yet sensitive temperament, exercise needs, and strong intolerance of solitude in flats or yards.

akc-pyrenean-shepherd-breed-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Pyrenean Shepherd
akc-pyrenean-shepherd-breed-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Herding Group, recognized 2009) covering Rough-Faced and Smooth-Faced varieties, rough-faced height (males 15.5-18.5 inches, females 15-18 inches), windswept muzzle coat, tight-fitting lips, scissors bite, 'shaves the earth' gait, and colour disqualifications.

akc-pyrenean-shepherd-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Pyrenean Shepherd Dog Breed Information
akc-pyrenean-shepherd-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile covering Pyrenees pastoral history alongside Great Pyrenees, weight (15-30 pounds across both varieties), life expectancy (17-19 years), moderate shedding, high exercise demands, clicker-friendly trainability, and health screening for hip dysplasia, patellar subluxation, PDA, epilepsy, and eye diseases.

psca-pyrenean-shepherd-health.name: Pyrenean Shepherd Club of America - Health and Genetics
psca-pyrenean-shepherd-health.note: Official US parent breed club health portal outlining CHIC pre-breeding testing guidelines: hip dysplasia evaluation (OFA/PennHIP/OVC), annual ACVO ophthalmologist eye examination (plus puppy eye exams at 5-7 weeks of age), and congenital or advanced cardiac evaluation.

wikimedia-berger-des-pyrenees-caronna.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Berger des Pyrénées.jpg
wikimedia-berger-des-pyrenees-caronna.note: High-resolution photograph (1809 x 1707 px) of an adult long-haired Pyrenean Sheepdog (FCI 141) by Caronna (EXIF capture date 2005-01-28, uploaded 2005-02-14). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported (and GFDL) on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-berger-des-pyrenees-poil-long-.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Berger des Pyrénées à poil long 1 - Helsinki 6 Dec 2015.JPG
wikimedia-berger-des-pyrenees-poil-long-.note: Photograph (1600 x 1200 px) of a long-haired Pyrenean Sheepdog at the Finnish Winner 2015 show in Helsinki by Yulia Petrova / Томасина (EXIF capture date 2015-12-06, uploaded 2015-12-18). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-danish-swedish-farmdog-education.name: FCI — Danish-Swedish Farmdog Breed-Specific Education Presentation
fci-danish-swedish-farmdog-education.note: Official FCI judges education presentation for FCI Standard No. 356 detailing pinscher heritage, non-aggressive doorbell watchdog temperament, circus history, and conformation.

danish-swedish-farmdog-cystine-uroliths-.name: A retrospective study on epidemiology and management of canine cystine uroliths in one part of Norway from 2015 to 2020
danish-swedish-farmdog-cystine-uroliths-.note: Retrospective Norwegian veterinary study (PMID 37964384) identifying the Danish-Swedish Farmdog among the three breeds most commonly affected by cystine urolithiasis.

danish-swedish-farmdog-bobtail-ltv-study.name: Association between the natural bobtail phenotype and lumbosacral transitional vertebra in Brittany dogs and Danish-Swedish Farmdogs
danish-swedish-farmdog-bobtail-ltv-study.note: Cross-sectional radiographic study of 935 Danish-Swedish Farmdogs in Norway (PMC13429198) reporting 11.0% natural bobtail prevalence and 14.9% lumbosacral transitional vertebra (LTV) prevalence, with no statistically significant association between bobtail and LTV in the breed (P = 0.05).

danish-swedish-farmdog-pelger-huet-2011.name: Congenital Pelger-Huët anomaly in a Danish/Swedish Farmdog: case report
danish-swedish-farmdog-pelger-huet-2011.note: Isolated case report (PMID 21362186) documenting congenital Pelger-Huët anomaly in a 13-year-old Danish-Swedish Farmdog from Denmark.

fci-polish-hunting-dog-official-standard.name: FCI - Polish Hunting Dog (Gończy Polski) Official Breed Standard No. 354
fci-polish-hunting-dog-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 354 (definitive acceptance and valid standard dated 2017-11-07, published 2017-11-23). Covers Polish origin (Southern Poland / Podkarpacie), Józef Pawłusiewicz (1903-1979) breeding revival, Group 6 Section 1.2 Medium-sized Hounds classification with working trial, 9:10 rectangular proportions, elbow-to-ground ratio, harsh close-lying double coat, black-and-tan/brown-and-tan/red colours, melodic hunting voice, and withers height (males 55-59 cm, females 50-55 cm). Omits weight.

fci-polish-hunting-dog-nomenclature.name: FCI - Gończy Polski (Polish Hunting Dog) Breed Nomenclature (No. 354)
fci-polish-hunting-dog-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Poland as country of origin, Group 6 Section 1.2 Medium-sized Hounds classification with working trial, definitive recognition date (2017-11-07), and official multilingual names (Gończy Polski, Polish Hunting Dog, Chien Courant Polonais).

zkwp-polish-hunting-dog-commentary.name: Związek Kynologiczny w Polsce (ZKwP) - Commentary to FCI Standard No. 354 (Polish Hunting Dog)
zkwp-polish-hunting-dog-commentary.note: Official Polish Kennel Club (ZKwP) illustrated commentary on the Polish Hunting Dog documenting the 1764 Kleck estate manuscript naming 'gończy polski', Wiktor Kozłowski's 1821 treatise, Ignacy Bobiatyński (1823-1825), Ernest Buttler (1829), and Jan Szyttler's 1839 distinction between ogar and gończy.

polish-hunting-dog-ocular-abnormalities-.name: Ocular abnormalities in Polish Hunting Dogs (PLOS ONE / PMC8570502)
polish-hunting-dog-ocular-abnormalities-.note: Peer-reviewed veterinary ophthalmology study (PMID 34739488, PMC8570502) examining 193 Polish Hunting Dogs (aged 3 months to 12 years), documenting retinal lesions (8.3%), cataract (2.6%), iris coloboma (1.6%), PRA (1.6%), SARDS (1 dog), ocular dermoid (0.5%), retinal dysplasia, distichiasis, and entropion, and recommending periodic ophthalmological examinations.
polish-hunting-dog-ocular-abnormalities-.publisher: PLOS ONE / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

wikimedia-gonczy-polski-huntingdog-assoc.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Gończy Polski.jpg
wikimedia-gonczy-polski-huntingdog-assoc.note: Photograph (801 x 641 px) of an adult black-and-tan Polish Hunting Dog by Huntingdog association (EXIF capture date 2020-02-14, uploaded 2024-10-04). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-gonzcy-polski-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Gonzcy Polski Polish Hunting Dog.JPG
wikimedia-gonzcy-polski-canarian.note: Photograph (566 x 396 px) of a red male Polish Hunting Dog by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2013-12-13, uploaded 2014-05-11). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-volpino-italiano-official-standard.name: FCI - Volpino Italiano (Italian Volpino) Official Breed Standard No. 195
fci-volpino-italiano-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 195 (valid standard dated 2023-09-08, English publication dated 2023-09-21). Covers Italian origin, Bronze Age European Spitz heritage, Vittore Carpaccio 1502 painting, Group 5 Section 4 European Spitz classification without working trial, square build, pyramid head, harsh long stand-off coat, uniform white/red/black and other accepted colours, and withers height (males 27-30 cm, females 25-28 cm; weight proportionate to height).

fci-volpino-italiano-nomenclature.name: FCI - Volpino Italiano Breed Nomenclature (No. 195)
fci-volpino-italiano-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Italy as country of origin, Group 5 Section 4 European Spitz classification without working trial, and official multilingual names (Volpino Italiano, Italian Volpino, Volpino Italien, Italienischer Volpino).

enci-volpino-italiano-profile.name: Ente Nazionale della Cinofilia Italiana (ENCI) - Volpino Italiano
enci-volpino-italiano-profile.note: Official Italian Kennel Club (ENCI) breed page for Volpino Italiano documenting the early-21st-century recovery of the red coat variety and Riproduzione Selezionata health screening requirements (hereditary ocular diseases and patellar luxation grade 0/1).

akc-volpino-italiano-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Volpino Italiano Dog Breed Information
akc-volpino-italiano-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Foundation Stock Service) covering Italian countryside watchdog history, weight (males 10-16 pounds, females 8-12 pounds), life expectancy (12-15 years), shedding, temperament, and Primary Lens Luxation (PLL) DNA testing.

donner-2018-canine-genetic-variants-stud.name: Frequency and distribution of 152 genetic disease variants in over 100,000 mixed breed and purebred dogs (PLOS Genetics)
donner-2018-canine-genetic-variants-stud.note: Peer-reviewed large-scale canine genetic screening study (PLOS Genetics, PMC5945203) documenting the ADAMTS17 Primary Lens Luxation variant in 7.7% (2/26) of tested Volpino Italiano dogs.
donner-2018-canine-genetic-variants-stud.publisher: PLOS Genetics / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

wikimedia-italianvolpino2-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:ItalianVolpino2.jpg
wikimedia-italianvolpino2-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (1303 x 1074 px) of an adult white Volpino Italiano standing outdoors by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2021-07-03, uploaded 2021-07-05). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-cucciolo-volpino-italiano-ross.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Cucciolo volpino italiano rosso.jpg
wikimedia-cucciolo-volpino-italiano-ross.note: High-resolution photograph (2030 x 2048 px) of a young red Volpino Italiano by Cinvic (captured 2023-04-22, uploaded 2023-06-12). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

griffon-bruxellois-cm-sm-quantitative-20.name: Quantitative analysis of Chiari-like malformation and syringomyelia in the Griffon Bruxellois dog
griffon-bruxellois-cm-sm-quantitative-20.note: Peer-reviewed MRI morphometry study (Knowler et al., PLoS ONE 2014, PMID 24533070) characterizing cranial base shortening and brain reorganization in Griffon Bruxellois dogs with Chiari-like malformation and syringomyelia.

griffon-bruxellois-sm-breeding-guideline.name: Effectiveness of breeding guidelines for reducing the prevalence of syringomyelia
griffon-bruxellois-sm-breeding-guideline.note: Peer-reviewed study of 550 Cavalier King Charles Spaniels and 93 Griffon Bruxellois (PMID 21998144) showing 73% of Griffon Bruxellois offspring were SM-free when both parents were SM-free compared with 100% SM-affected when both parents had SM.

bca-barbet-health-statement.name: Barbet Club of America - BCA Health Statement
bca-barbet-health-statement.note: Official AKC parent club health statement documenting hip dysplasia, eye conditions, elbow dysplasia, ~40% prcd-PRA carrier frequency identified in summer 2017 among genetically tested Barbets, plus reported occurrences of epilepsy, immune system problems, and tick-related illnesses.

bca-barbet-chic-requirements.name: Barbet Club of America - Canine Health (CHIC) Requirements
bca-barbet-chic-requirements.note: Official Barbet Club of America CHIC health testing panel detailing required OFA/PennHIP hip evaluation, OFA elbow evaluation, prcd-PRA DNA test, and ACVO ophthalmologist CAER eye exam (minimum age 12 months), plus optional cardiac, thyroid, knee, and D-locus testing.

leroy-2006-french-breeds-genetic-variabi.name: Leroy et al. (2006) - Genetic variability in French dog breeds assessed by pedigree data
leroy-2006-french-breeds-genetic-variabi.note: Peer-reviewed pedigree analysis of nine French dog breeds (Journal of Animal Breeding and Genetics, 2006; PMID 16420259) reporting an effective number of ancestors of 6.7 and average inbreeding coefficient of 12.4% in the 1997–2001 Barbet cohort.
leroy-2006-french-breeds-genetic-variabi.publisher: Journal of Animal Breeding and Genetics (PubMed)

fci-wetterhoun-official-standard.name: FCI - Wetterhoun Official Breed Standard No. 221
fci-wetterhoun-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 221 (valid standard dated 2023-06-08, English publication dated 2023-07-06). Covers Dutch origin, Group 8 Section 3 Water Dogs classification with working trial, Baltic Sea origin history, otter hunting and dog-cart utility, 1:1 square proportions, coarse greasy curly coat with short-haired head/legs, mason's-trowel ears, spiral tail, ideal height (males 59 cm, females 55 cm), and approximate weight (males 34 kg, females 28 kg).

fci-wetterhoun-nomenclature.name: FCI - Wetterhoun Breed Nomenclature (No. 221)
fci-wetterhoun-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming The Netherlands as country of origin, Group 8 Section 3 Water Dogs classification subject to a working trial, and official multilingual names (Wetterhoun, Chien d'Eau Frison, Friesischer Wasserhund).

raad-van-beheer-wetterhoun-profile.name: Raad van Beheer (Houden van honden) - Wetterhoun Rasprofiel & Foknormen
