wikimedia-steirische1-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (1638 x 1359 px) of an adult female Styrian Coarse-haired Hound (Steirische Rauhhaarbracke) by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2019-03-31 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2019-04-04). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-steirische-rauhhaarbracke-u235.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Steirische Rauhhaarbracke.jpg
wikimedia-steirische-rauhhaarbracke-u235.note: High-resolution photograph (1476 x 1608 px) of a six-month-old Styrian Coarse-haired Hound by U235~commonswiki (captured 2005-11-13, uploaded 2006-01-20). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported (and GFDL) on Wikimedia Commons.

rkc-belgian-shepherd-dog-groenendael-bre.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Belgian Shepherd Dog (Groenendael) Breeds A to Z
rkc-belgian-shepherd-dog-groenendael-bre.note: Official Royal Kennel Club Breeds A to Z profile covering medieval Belgian herding origins, 1891 breed club and Prof. Adolphe Reul's examination of 117 dogs, four coat varieties, and police/armed forces versatility.

akc-keeshond-official-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Keeshond
akc-keeshond-official-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Non-Sporting Group; approved October 8, 2024, effective January 1, 2025). Establishes pronunciation ('kayz-hawnd'), ideal height (18 inches males, 17 inches bitches, +/- 1 inch variance acceptable), square compact build, orbital 'spectacles' hallmark, tight black lips, scissor bite, natural untrimmed stand-off double coat, blended grey/black/cream coloration, double-tracking gait, and outgoing, friendly, alert temperament.

akc-keeshond-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Keeshond Dog Breed Information
akc-keeshond-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile covering Netherlands barge-dog and Dutch Patriot history, plural 'Keeshonden', 1930 AKC registration, ideal height (18 in male, 17 in female), weight (35-45 pounds), life expectancy (12-15 years), high double-coat shedding, and affectionate, vocal watchdog temperament.

rkc-keeshond-breed-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Keeshond Breed Standard
rkc-keeshond-breed-standard.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Utility Group) confirming compact medium spitz conformation, harsh off-standing coat, dense ruff, pale undercoat, spectacles, and confident, alert, friendly temperament.

kca-keeshond-health-information.name: Keeshond Club of America (KCA) - Keeshond Health Information & CHIC Requirements
kca-keeshond-health-information.note: Official US parent breed club health portal documenting OFA/CHIC screening requirements (hip dysplasia, elbow dysplasia, patellar luxation, ACVO eye exam), additional OFA-listed screenings (PHPT DNA test, thyroid, cardiac), and breed health research priorities including Primary Hyperparathyroidism (PHPT), copper toxicosis, epilepsy, and PRA.

keeshond-club-uk-history.name: The Keeshond Club (UK) - The History of the Keeshond
keeshond-club-uk-history.note: Official UK parent breed club historical account documenting Dutch barge-dog traditions, 1923 British show debut as Dutch Barge Dog, 1925 club founding, 1926 renaming to The Keeshond Club, Dutch plural 'Keeshonden', naturally odourless untrimmed coat, and clever companion temperament.

pubmed-wade-2025-keeshond-sirt6-phpt.name: Autosomal dominant primary hyperparathyroidism in the Keeshond dog breed is strongly associated with a missense variant in sirtuin-6 (Animal Genetics 2025)
pubmed-wade-2025-keeshond-sirt6-phpt.note: Peer-reviewed genomic study by Wade et al. (Anim Genet 2025 Dec;56(6):e70056, PMID 41134522) identifying a likely pathogenic exon 2 missense/possible splice-site variant in SIRT6 (XM_038567756.1:c.193A>G; p.65R>G) strongly associated with autosomal dominant Primary Hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) in Keeshonden and highly concordant with the EEF2 promoter test marker used since 2008.

pubmed-goldstein-2007-keeshond-phpt.name: Inheritance, mode of inheritance, and candidate genes for primary hyperparathyroidism in Keeshonden (JVIM 2007)
pubmed-goldstein-2007-keeshond-phpt.note: Peer-reviewed veterinary internal medicine study by Goldstein et al. (J Vet Intern Med 2007 Jan-Feb;21(1):199-203, PMID 17338170) establishing autosomal dominant inheritance of Primary Hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) in Keeshonden.
pubmed-goldstein-2007-keeshond-phpt.publisher: Journal of Veterinary Internal Medicine / PubMed

pubmed-werner-2005-keeshond-conotruncal.name: The keeshond defect in cardiac conotruncal development is oligogenic (Human Genetics 2005)
pubmed-werner-2005-keeshond-conotruncal.note: Peer-reviewed molecular genetics study by Werner et al. (Hum Genet 2005 Apr;116(5):368-377, Epub 2005-02-12, PMID 15711798) demonstrating oligogenic inheritance of congenital cardiac conotruncal defects (including Tetralogy of Fallot) in Keeshonden.

pubmed-hall-wallace-1996-keeshond-epilep.name: Canine epilepsy: a genetic counselling programme for keeshonds (Veterinary Record 1996)
pubmed-hall-wallace-1996-keeshond-epilep.note: Peer-reviewed study by Hall and Wallace (Vet Rec 1996 Apr 13;138(15):358-360, PMID 8737262) analyzing inherited idiopathic epilepsy predisposition and breeding counselling in Keeshonden.

wikimedia-keeshond-3-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Keeshond 3.jpg
wikimedia-keeshond-3-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (1655 x 1450 px) of an adult Keeshond outdoors by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2020-08-23 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2020-08-24). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-keeshond-image-001-dancing-wit.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Keeshond image 001.jpg
wikimedia-keeshond-image-001-dancing-wit.note: High-resolution close-up portrait (1600 x 1812 px) of a Keeshond by Flickr user dancing_with_wolves (captured 2007-01-24, cropped and uploaded to Wikimedia Commons by Ltshears on 2007-03-05, reviewed by MECU on 2007-04-12). Licensed under CC BY 2.0 Generic.

rkc-basset-bleu-de-gascogne-breed-standa.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Basset Bleu De Gascogne (Imp) Breed Standard
rkc-basset-bleu-de-gascogne-breed-standa.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Hound Group) describing the smooth-coated, athletic, aristocratic basset, deep sonorous voice, and temperament.

rkc-basset-bleu-de-gascogne-breed-profil.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Basset Bleu De Gascogne Breeds A to Z
rkc-basset-bleu-de-gascogne-breed-profil.note: Official Royal Kennel Club Breeds A to Z profile confirming Medium size, high exercise needs (more than 2 hours per day), southwestern French origin, and blue mottled markings with tan points.

fci-croatian-shepherd-dog-education-2014.name: FCI / Croatian Kennel Club - Croatian Shepherd Dog Breed-Specific Education Presentation (No. 277)
fci-croatian-shepherd-dog-education-2014.note: Official FCI/HKS breed-specific education presentation detailing Slavonian history (1374 Bishop Petar, 1719 Bishop Petar Bakić, 1935 Prof. Stjepan Romić, 1949 Zagreb show, 1951 Dr. Otto Rohr), proportions, eyes, and pricked/semi-pricked ear geometry.
fci-croatian-shepherd-dog-education-2014.publisher: Fédération Cynologique Internationale / Hrvatski kinološki savez

pmc-canine-tbxt-bobtail-review-2025.name: Incorporating Morphological Evaluations into Breeding Soundness Examinations in Dogs (PMC)
pmc-canine-tbxt-bobtail-review-2025.note: Peer-reviewed veterinary review covering canine natural bobtail genetics (heterozygous TBXT mutation and early in-utero reabsorption of homozygous embryos when two bobtailed dogs are mated).

fci-east-siberian-laika-official-standar.name: FCI - East Siberian Laika (Vostotchno-Sibirskaïa Laïka) Official Breed Standard No. 305
fci-east-siberian-laika-official-standar.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 305 (revised valid standard dated 2010-10-13, English publication dated 2011-03-02). Covers Russian origin in Eastern Siberia and the Far East, Group 5 Section 2 Nordic Hunting Dogs classification with working trial, multipurpose hunting and sledge/draught use, wedge-shaped head, dry tight lips, sickle/ring tail, coarse dense double coat, accepted colours, and withers height (males 57-64 cm, females 53-60 cm). Omits weight.

fci-east-siberian-laika-nomenclature.name: FCI - Vostotchno-Sibirskaïa Laïka (East Siberian Laika) Breed Nomenclature (No. 305)
fci-east-siberian-laika-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Russia as country of origin, Group 5 Section 2 Nordic Hunting Dogs classification subject to a working trial, English standard publication date (2011-03-02), and official multilingual names (Vostotchno-Sibirskaïa Laïka, East Siberian Laika, Laïka de Sibérie Orientale, Ostsibirischer Laika).

kennelliitto-itasiperianlaika-standard.name: Suomen Kennelliitto - Itäsiperianlaika Rotumääritelmä (FCI 305)
kennelliitto-itasiperianlaika-standard.note: Official Finnish Kennel Club (Suomen Kennelliitto) publication of FCI Standard No. 305 detailing Tungus/Yakut/Baikal/Amur laika origins, 1947 breed recognition, 1949 provisional standard, 1981 approval, Irkutsk/Leningrad/Smolensk/Tver breeding regions, body-length ratios (1.04-1.09 males, 1.06-1.11 females), equilateral-triangle head shape, and friendly, trusting, autonomous temperament.

skk-ostsibirisk-lajka-breed-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Östsibirisk lajka Rasprofil
skk-ostsibirisk-lajka-breed-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for Östsibirisk lajka confirming Eastern Siberian origin (Yenisei River to Pacific coast), 1978 first Swedish import, height (57-64 cm males, 53-60 cm females), largest/strongest laika status, easy-care double coat with regular shedding, unsuitability solely as a companion dog, and documentation that hip dysplasia (HD) can occur.

scc-laika-de-siberie-orientale-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Laïka de Sibérie orientale
scc-laika-de-siberie-orientale-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile for Laïka de Sibérie orientale documenting Evenk/Lamut/Amur crossbreeding origins, vocal 'laïka' ('barker') character, approximate unsexed weight note (20-30 kg), and firm consistent training requirements.

suomen-laikajarjesto-isl-jto-2026-2030.name: Suomen Laikajärjestö - Itäsiperianlaikan Jalostuksen Tavoiteohjelma (JTO) 2026-2030
suomen-laikajarjesto-isl-jto-2026-2030.note: Official Finnish Laika Club (Suomen Laikajärjestö) Breeding Target Programme (JTO 2026-2030) for the East Siberian Laika documenting 1979 Finnish breed introduction, Aljo kennel history, genetic-diversity inbreeding limits (<=6.25% over 5 generations), and PEVISA-linked health screening priorities (hips, eyes, and POAG DNA testing).

pmc-ding-2011-canine-ychromosome-east-as.name: Origins of domestic dog in southern East Asia is supported by analysis of Y-chromosome DNA (Heredity 2011)
pmc-ding-2011-canine-ychromosome-east-as.note: Peer-reviewed study by Ding et al. (Heredity 2012 May;108(5):507-514, Epub 2011-11-01, PMID 22108628, PMC3330686) documenting Y-chromosome haplogroup HG9 shared between the East Siberian Laika and African Basenji dogs.

pmc-anderson-2020-ancient-mc1r-r301c.name: Comprehensive genetic testing combined with citizen science reveals a recently characterized ancient MC1R mutation associated with partial recessive red phenotypes in dog (PLOS Genetics 2020)
pmc-anderson-2020-ancient-mc1r-r301c.note: Peer-reviewed genomic study of 11,750 dogs (PMC7643265) identifying the ancient MC1R R301C ('eA') coat-colour allele across 35 breeds including old Nordic spitzes such as the East-Siberian Laika.
pmc-anderson-2020-ancient-mc1r-r301c.publisher: PLOS Genetics / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

wikimedia-east-siberian-laika-przemekl.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:East Siberian Laika.jpg
wikimedia-east-siberian-laika-przemekl.note: High-resolution photograph (1600 x 1200 px) of a young East Siberian Laika taken during the World Dog Show 2006 in Poznań by PrzemekL (EXIF capture date 2006-11-09, uploaded 2006-11-14). Released into the public domain by the copyright holder on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-eastsiberianlaika-mirtu.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Eastsiberianlaika.JPG
wikimedia-eastsiberianlaika-mirtu.note: High-resolution photograph (2592 x 1952 px) of an adult East Siberian Laika outdoors by Mirtu (EXIF capture date 2005-10-08 on HP PhotoSmart R707, uploaded 2007-04-22). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported (multi-licensed with 2.5/2.0/1.0 and GFDL) on Wikimedia Commons.

rkc-harrier-breed-profile.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Harrier Breeds A to Z
rkc-harrier-breed-profile.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed profile covering exercise (>2 hours/day), Breed Watch status (no points of concern), recognised standard colours, and Hare Hound heritage.

wikimedia-harrier-pedigree-evforce.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Harrier Hound -Pedigree Harrier.jpg
wikimedia-harrier-pedigree-evforce.note: CC BY-SA 4.0 photograph (3072 x 4608 px) of a pedigree Harrier by Evforce, replacing broken File:Harrier_600.jpg.

fci-basset-artesien-normand-official-sta.name: FCI - Basset Artésien Normand (Norman Artesien Basset) Official Breed Standard No. 34
fci-basset-artesien-normand-official-sta.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 34 (valid standard dated 2023-08-01, English publication dated 2023-08-29). Covers French origin, 1870s controlled breeding of short-haired French bassets, Group 6 Section 1.3 Small-sized Hounds classification with working trial, proportions (5:8 height:length, 2:3 chest:height, 1:2 skull width:head length, 10:10 muzzle:skull), noble domed head, corkscrew-curled drop ears, slightly crooked forelegs with light wrist folds, prohibition on altering tail appearance, smooth short tricolour/bicolour coat, withers height (30-36 cm for both sexes, +/- 1 cm tolerance), and weight (15-20 kg).

fci-basset-artesien-normand-nomenclature.name: FCI - Basset Artésien Normand Breed Nomenclature (No. 34)
fci-basset-artesien-normand-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming France as country of origin, Group 6 Section 1.3 Small-sized Hounds classification with working trial, definitive acceptance date (1963-10-29), valid standard date (2023-08-01), English publication date (2023-08-29), and official multilingual names (Basset Artésien Normand, Norman Artesien Basset, Basset artesiano de Normandía).

scc-basset-artesien-normand-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Basset artésien normand
scc-basset-artesien-normand-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile for Basset artésien normand confirming 19th-century cross of Basset Normand and Basset d'Artois, athletic build without heaviness, height (30-36 cm), weight (15-20 kg, ~17 kg average), cheerful calm child-patient temperament, apartment adaptation if accustomed young with frequent outings, and recommendation of two daily meals.

cfban-club-basset-artesien-normand.name: Club Français du Basset Artésien Normand et du Chien d'Artois - Site Officiel
cfban-club-basset-artesien-normand.note: Official French parent breed club affiliated with the Société Centrale Canine overseeing the Basset Artésien Normand and Chien d'Artois, documenting breeding evaluations, hunting trials, and the club's preliminary survey on early-onset blindness (Enquête préliminaire cécité précoce).
cfban-club-basset-artesien-normand.publisher: Club Français du Basset Artésien Normand et du Chien d'Artois

skk-basset-artesien-normand-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Basset artésien normand Rasprofil
skk-basset-artesien-normand-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for Basset artésien normand documenting French origin (1870s breeding, lyre-shaped forelegs, 1966 first Swedish litter), height (30-36 cm), weight (15-20 kg), easy-care short coat, cheerful affectionate hunting temperament, and health notes covering ear and throat/neck diseases as well as post-hunt respiratory distress and abnormal fatigue (jaktödem).

nku-chondrodysplastic-ed-exclusion-2025.name: Nordic Kennel Union (NKU) X-ray Panel - Chondrodysplastic Breeds Excluded from ED Screening (2025)
nku-chondrodysplastic-ed-exclusion-2025.note: Official Nordic Kennel Union (NKU) X-ray Panel veterinary guidance (January 2025, published via Dansk Kennel Klub) listing Basset artésien normand among chondrodysplastic breeds excluded from standard radiographic elbow-dysplasia (ED) screening due to breed-defining curved foreleg anatomy, citing Parker et al. (Science 2009) and Batcher et al. (Genes 2019) on FGF4 retrogenes and intervertebral disc disease (IVDD).
nku-chondrodysplastic-ed-exclusion-2025.publisher: Nordic Kennel Union / Dansk Kennel Klub

wikimedia-ban-skogvaktarens-queen-sally-.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Grupp 6 BASSET ARTÉSIEN NORMAND, Skogvaktarens Queen Sally (24180074612).jpg
wikimedia-ban-skogvaktarens-queen-sally-.note: High-resolution photograph (1656 x 1104 px) of a tricolour Basset Artésien Normand (Skogvaktarens Queen Sally) at MyDOG in Gothenburg by Johan Frick-Meijer / Svenska Mässan (EXIF capture date 2016-01-08 on Nikon D800, uploaded to Wikimedia Commons via Flickr2Commons by Томасина on 2016-03-30). Licensed under CC BY 2.0 Generic.

wikimedia-basset-artesien-normand-sonvis.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Basset Artésien Normand.jpg
wikimedia-basset-artesien-normand-sonvis.note: High-resolution outdoor portrait (2848 x 4272 px) of a tricolour Basset Artésien Normand by Bernt Sønvisen (EXIF capture date 2010-10-31 on Canon EOS 450D, uploaded to Wikimedia Commons via Flickr upload bot by Ltshears on 2012-08-06). Licensed under CC BY 2.0 Generic.

peru-info-viringo-cultural-heritage.name: Perú Info (PROMPERÚ) - Conoce al perro sin pelo, raza oriunda de Perú
peru-info-viringo-cultural-heritage.note: Official Peruvian tourism and cultural portal documenting Law No. 27537 (2001) National Cultural Heritage status, June 12 national day, Viringo/Calato etymology, pre-Inca ceramics, and seasonal skin tanning.

wikimedia-peruvian-hairless-dog-medio-co.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Peruvian Hairless Dog Medio Coated.jpg
wikimedia-peruvian-hairless-dog-medio-co.note: CC BY-SA 4.0 photograph (600 x 578 px) of a medium-sized coated Peruvian Hairless Dog by Canarian (captured 2016-12-04, uploaded 2016-12-05), replacing broken File:Peruvian_Hairless_Dog_600.jpg.

fci-irish-wolfhound-official-standard.name: FCI - Irish Wolfhound Official Breed Standard No. 160
fci-irish-wolfhound-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 160 (valid standard dated 2026-04-10, English publication dated 2026-04-17). Covers Irish origin, Group 10 Section 2 Rough-haired Sighthounds classification without working trial, Greyhound-like commanding giant conformation, rough harsh coat, accepted colours, minimum height at withers (males 79 cm, females 71 cm), and minimum expected weight (males 54.5 kg for 79 cm, females 40.5 kg for 71 cm, increasing proportionally with height).

fci-irish-wolfhound-nomenclature.name: FCI - Irish Wolfhound Breed Nomenclature (No. 160)
fci-irish-wolfhound-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Ireland as country of origin, Group 10 Section 2 Rough-haired Sighthounds classification without working trial, definitive acceptance date (1955-04-26), English publication date (2026-04-17), and official multilingual names (Irish Wolfhound, Lévrier Irlandais, Irischer Wolfshund).

rkc-irish-wolfhound-breed-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Irish Wolfhound Breed Standard
rkc-irish-wolfhound-breed-standard.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Hound Group, last updated August 1, 2025) confirming gentle, kind, friendly temperament, dark elliptical eyes, small velvet rose ears, complete scissor bite, dewlap-free arched neck, rough harsh coat, recognised colours (grey, brindle, red, black, pure white, fawn, wheaten, steel grey), minimum height (dogs 79 cm, bitches 71 cm; desired male average 81-86 cm), and minimum weight (dogs 54.5 kg, bitches 40.9 kg).

akc-irish-wolfhound-official-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Irish Wolfhound
akc-irish-wolfhound-official-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Hound Group; approved September 12, 1950). Establishes conformation, rough hard coat wiry over eyes and underjaw, dewlap-free arched neck, minimum height (32 inches dogs, 30 inches bitches), minimum weight (120 pounds dogs, 105 pounds bitches), and List of Points in Order of Merit.

akc-irish-wolfhound-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Irish Wolfhound Dog Breed Information
akc-irish-wolfhound-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile documenting ancient Irish history (391 AD Symmachus letter, 1862 Captain George Augustus Graham revival, 1897 AKC recognition, Irish Guards mascot since 1902), life expectancy (6-8 years), moderate shedding (3/5), quiet vocalization (1/5), calm dignified temperament, and recommended health evaluations (hips, elbows, cardiac, ophthalmologist, serum bile acids).

iwca-chic-health-testing.name: Irish Wolfhound Club of America (IWCA) - CHIC Health Screening Program
iwca-chic-health-testing.note: Official US parent breed club CHIC health screening guide detailing the four required adult screenings (board-certified veterinary cardiologist echocardiogram plus recommended annual ECG, board-certified ophthalmologist eye exam including PRA, hip dysplasia radiograph, and elbow dysplasia radiograph).

iwca-adult-health-issues.name: Irish Wolfhound Club of America (IWCA) - Health Issues in Adult Irish Wolfhounds
iwca-adult-health-issues.note: Veterinary health article by C.A. Krowzack, DVM (copyright 2014) hosted by the Irish Wolfhound Club of America covering GDV/bloat, heart disease and routine ECG monitoring, osteosarcoma, lymphoma, acute rapid-onset pneumonia requiring prolonged antibiotics, and reduced anesthetic induction dosing (typically 1/2 to 2/3 calculated dose).

pmc-simpson-2016-iw-dcm-genetics.name: Multiple Genetic Associations with Irish Wolfhound Dilated Cardiomyopathy (BioMed Research International 2016)
pmc-simpson-2016-iw-dcm-genetics.note: Peer-reviewed study by Simpson et al. (Biomed Res Int 2016:6374082, Epub 2016-12-13, PMID 28070514, PMC5187458) documenting polygenic associations for Dilated Cardiomyopathy (DCM) in Irish Wolfhounds and summarizing UK demographic longevity (median age at death 7.04 years, maximum 11.83 years) and leading causes of death (cardiac disease, osteosarcoma, bronchopneumonia, and GDV).
pmc-simpson-2016-iw-dcm-genetics.publisher: BioMed Research International / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-vollmar-2016-iw-dcm-clinical-trial.name: Long-term Outcome of Irish Wolfhound Dogs with Preclinical Cardiomyopathy, Atrial Fibrillation, or Both Treated with Pimobendan, Benazepril Hydrochloride, or Methyldigoxin Monotherapy (JVIM 2016)
pmc-vollmar-2016-iw-dcm-clinical-trial.note: Peer-reviewed blinded randomized clinical trial of 75 Irish Wolfhounds (Vollmar & Fox, J Vet Intern Med 2016, PMC4913600) demonstrating that early detection and pimobendan therapy significantly prolonged time to congestive heart failure or sudden death (median 1,991 days vs. 858 days for benazepril, P = 0.002), supporting routine cardiac screening.
pmc-vollmar-2016-iw-dcm-clinical-trial.publisher: Journal of Veterinary Internal Medicine / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-iw-osteosarcoma-heritability-2021.name: Heritability and genetic variance estimation of Osteosarcoma (OSA) in Irish Wolfhound, using deep pedigree information (Canine Medicine and Genetics 2021)
pmc-iw-osteosarcoma-heritability-2021.note: Peer-reviewed pedigree genetics study (Canine Med Genet 2021, PMC8502365) analyzing 5,110 purebred Irish Wolfhounds (332 OSA cases, 360 controls over age 10), estimating high complex-trait heritability for osteosarcoma (h² = 0.65) and reporting that 93% of OSA-related deaths occurred before 10 years of age.
pmc-iw-osteosarcoma-heritability-2021.publisher: Canine Medicine and Genetics / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pubmed-kerr-1999-iw-portosystemic-shunt.name: Mass screening of Irish wolfhound puppies for portosystemic shunts by the dynamic bile acid test (Veterinary Record 1999)
pubmed-kerr-1999-iw-portosystemic-shunt.note: Peer-reviewed veterinary diagnostic study by Kerr et al. (Vet Rec 1999 Jun 19;144(25):693-696, PMID 10420483) validating dynamic (postprandial) serum bile acid testing for mass screening of Irish Wolfhound puppies for congenital portosystemic liver shunts.

pubmed-urfer-2007-iw-lifespan-diseases.name: Lifespan and disease predispositions in the Irish Wolfhound: a review (Veterinary Quarterly 2007)
pubmed-urfer-2007-iw-lifespan-diseases.note: Peer-reviewed breed health review by Urfer et al. (Vet Q 2007 Sep;29(3):102-111, PMID 17970287) reviewing longevity and major documented conditions in Irish Wolfhounds including DCM, osteosarcoma, GDV, intrahepatic portosystemic shunt, rhinitis, epilepsy, progressive retinal atrophy (PRA), von Willebrand disease, and juvenile fibrocartilaginous embolism.

wikimedia-irish-wolfhound-brindle-1-cana.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Irish Wolfhound brindle 1.jpg
wikimedia-irish-wolfhound-brindle-1-cana.note: High-resolution photograph (1907 x 1432 px) of an adult brindle male Irish Wolfhound standing outdoors by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2020-08-23 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2020-08-24). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-irish-wolfhound-dschoen.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Irish Wolfhound.jpg
wikimedia-irish-wolfhound-dschoen.note: High-resolution photograph (1410 x 1910 px) of an Irish Wolfhound by D.Schoen (EXIF capture date 2007-09-02 on Canon Digital IXUS 800 IS, uploaded 2007-12-28 by Connection reset by peer). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported (and GFDL) on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-montenegronak-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Montenegronak.jpg
wikimedia-montenegronak-canarian.note: High-resolution CC BY 4.0 photograph (2299 x 1857 px) of a Montenegrin Mountain Hound by Canarian (2024-04-26), replacing nonexistent File:Crnogorski_planinski_gonic.JPG.

wikimedia-montenegrin-mountain-hound-2-c.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Montenegrin Mountain Hound 2.jpg
wikimedia-montenegrin-mountain-hound-2-c.note: CC BY-SA 4.0 photograph (444 x 510 px) of a black-and-tan female Montenegrin Mountain Hound by Canarian (captured 2014-08-09, uploaded 2015-08-01), replacing nonexistent File:Crnogorski_planinski_gonic_600.jpg.

fci-burgos-pointing-dog-official-standar.name: FCI - Burgos Pointing Dog (Perdiguero de Burgos) Official Breed Standard No. 90
fci-burgos-pointing-dog-official-standar.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 90 (valid standard dated 1982-05-26, English publication dated 1998-11-09). Covers Spanish origin, Group 7 Section 1.1 Continental Pointing Dogs ('Braque' type) classification with working trial, fur-and-feather hunting utilization, calm docile temperament, divergent head axes, corkscrew ears with visible vein plexus, double dewlap, square body, chest perimeter (+1/4 withers height), 100°/125° forelimb angles, steady economical trot, pink skin with brown mucous membranes, white-and-liver short coat (black and tan inadmissible), pronounced sexual dimorphism, and withers height (males 62-67 cm, females 59-64 cm). Omits weight.

fci-burgos-pointing-dog-nomenclature.name: FCI - Perdiguero de Burgos (Burgos Pointing Dog) Breed Nomenclature (No. 90)
fci-burgos-pointing-dog-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Spain as country of origin, Group 7 Section 1.1 Continental Pointing Dogs ('Braque' type) classification with working trial, definitive acceptance date (1954-11-12), valid standard date (1982-05-26), English publication date (1998-11-09), and official multilingual names (Perdiguero de Burgos, Burgos Pointing Dog, Perdiguero von Burgos).

rsce-perdiguero-de-burgos-standard.name: Real Sociedad Canina de España (RSCE) - Estándar del Perdiguero de Burgos
rsce-perdiguero-de-burgos-standard.note: Official Spanish Kennel Club (RSCE) breed standard for Perdiguero de Burgos detailing eumetric mediolinear square proportions, croup inclination (<45°), exact limb ratios (forearm twice carpus-to-ground, thigh 3/4 lower leg), corkscrew ears reaching lip corner, complete scissor bite with all premolars, height (males 62-67 cm, females 59-64 cm), pronounced sexual dimorphism, and calm, docile, intelligent character.

aeppb-perdiguero-de-burgos-origenes.name: Asociación Española del Perro Perdiguero de Burgos (AEPPB) - Orígenes e historia antigua
aeppb-perdiguero-de-burgos-origenes.note: Official Spanish parent breed association (AEPPB) historical monograph (authored by veterinary geneticist Dr. José Manuel Sanz Timón) documenting the breed's formation across the northern Castilian plateau (Castile and León) rather than exclusively inside Burgos city.
aeppb-perdiguero-de-burgos-origenes.publisher: Asociación Española del Perro Perdiguero de Burgos

aeppb-boletin-2001-salud-displasia.name: Asociación Española del Perro Perdiguero de Burgos (AEPPB) - Boletín y Normativa de Cría (Displasia de Cadera)
aeppb-boletin-2001-salud-displasia.note: Official AEPPB breeding bulletin archive documenting parent-association health provisions including radiographic hip dysplasia evaluation ('prueba de displasia de cadera') for breeding dogs.
aeppb-boletin-2001-salud-displasia.publisher: Asociación Española del Perro Perdiguero de Burgos

unileon-melo-alonso-perdiguero-burgos-hd.name: Universidad de León - Índice de distracción en el diagnóstico de la displasia de cadera en razas caninas autóctonas castellano-leonesas: el Perdiguero de Burgos
unileon-melo-alonso-perdiguero-burgos-hd.note: Veterinary academic research from the University of León (Beatriz Melo Alonso) evaluating radiographic distraction-index diagnostics for hip dysplasia specifically in native Castile and León dog breeds including the Perdiguero de Burgos.

jordana-variabilidad-genetica-razas-espa.name: Variabilidad genética en diez razas caninas españolas (Jordana et al., Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona)
jordana-variabilidad-genetica-razas-espa.note: Peer-reviewed population-genetics research by Jordi Jordana et al. evaluating genetic variability across ten native Spanish dog breeds and reporting notably low observed heterozygosity (0.125) in the Perdiguero de Burgos.

wikimedia-burgos-pointer-canarian-2016.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Burgos Pointer.jpg
wikimedia-burgos-pointer-canarian-2016.note: Photograph (600 x 523 px) of an adult liver-roan female Burgos Pointer by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2016-12-10 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2016-12-11). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-burgos-pointer-perdiguero-cana.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Burgos Pointer or Perdiguero de Burgos.JPG
wikimedia-burgos-pointer-perdiguero-cana.note: Photograph (597 x 445 px) of a female Burgos Pointer standing in profile by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2013-06-29, uploaded 2013-09-23). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-billy-official-standard.name: FCI - Billy Official Breed Standard No. 25
fci-billy-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 25 (valid standard dated 1973-12-28, English publication dated 1997-04-24). Covers French origin, Group 6 Section 1.1 Large-sized hounds classification with working trial, forequarters more powerful than hindquarters, clean non-fleshy lips, relatively high-set flat drop ears, very deep narrow chest, fine supple white skin with optional dark spots, short harsh white/milk-coffee/orange-or-lemon coat (black or red hair disqualified), 1/2 cm slight overshot tolerance, and withers height (dogs 60-70 cm, bitches 58-62 cm). Omits weight.

fci-billy-nomenclature.name: FCI - Billy Breed Nomenclature (No. 25)
fci-billy-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming France as country of origin, Group 6 Section 1.1 Large-sized Hounds classification with working trial, definitive acceptance date (1963-10-14), valid standard date (1973-12-28), English publication date (1997-04-24), and official multilingual name (Billy).

scc-billy-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Billy
scc-billy-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile for the Billy documenting late-19th-century Poitou origin under Hublot du Rivault (recreating King Louis XII's Chiens Blancs du Roy / Chiens Blancs Greffiers), height (58-70 cm), weight explicitly listed as unspecified (NP), 40-50 km daily hunting gallop, early pack-obedience training, unsuitability for solitary city life, and seasonal hunting versus maintenance nutrition.

scc-club-du-chien-d-ordre-billy.name: Club du Chien d'Ordre (SCC) - Le Billy
scc-club-du-chien-d-ordre-billy.note: Official French parent breed club (Club du Chien d'Ordre, affiliated with the Société Centrale Canine) breed portal for Le Billy ('chien de Billy'), overseeing traditional French grande vènerie pack hounds.

canine-chronicle-billy-ria-horter.name: Ria Hörter - Billy: The French Pack Hound (Canine Chronicle)
canine-chronicle-billy-ria-horter.note: Published historical breed monograph by Ria Hörter (Canine Chronicle, September 2018) detailing French grande vènerie pack-hunting traditions and the history of the Billy.

wikimedia-billy-tivoli-rallye-gaillardet.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Tivoli au Rallye Gaillardet en 2023.jpg
wikimedia-billy-tivoli-rallye-gaillardet.note: Photograph (634 x 636 px) of an adult Billy hound ('Tivoli au Rallye Gaillardet') by MylèneTM (EXIF capture date 2023-10-21, uploaded 2023-10-21). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-newfoundland-official-standard.name: FCI - Newfoundland Official Breed Standard No. 50
fci-newfoundland-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 50 (valid standard dated 1996-10-29, English publication dated 1996-11-06). Covers Canadian origin, Group 2 Section 2.2 Mountain-type Molossoids classification without working trial, benevolence/gentleness temperament, massive head, soft flews, 30° croup slope, webbed toes, rudder tail, water-resistant double coat, black / white-and-black / brown colours, average height (71 cm males, 66 cm females), and approximate average weight (68 kg males, 54 kg females).

fci-newfoundland-nomenclature.name: FCI - Newfoundland Breed Nomenclature (No. 50)
fci-newfoundland-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Canada as country of origin, Group 2 Section 2.2 Mountain-type Molossoids classification without working trial, definitive acceptance date (1954-08-04), valid standard date (1996-10-29), English publication date (1996-11-06), and official multilingual names (Newfoundland, Chien de Terre-Neuve, Neufundländer, Terranova).

akc-newfoundland-official-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Newfoundland
akc-newfoundland-official-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Working Group; approved May 8, 1990). Establishes sweet disposition, draft and lifesaving multipurpose role, average adult height (28 inches dogs, 26 inches bitches), approximate weight (130-150 pounds dogs, 100-120 pounds bitches), webbed cat feet, flat water-resistant double coat, four recognized colours (black, brown, gray, white and black), and smooth gait with slight roll of the skin.

akc-newfoundland-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Newfoundland Dog Breed Information
akc-newfoundland-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile covering Canadian coastal water-rescue history (including Seaman on the Lewis and Clark expedition and SS Ethie rescue), height (28 in male, 26 in female), weight (130-150 lb male, 100-120 lb female), life expectancy (9-10 years), heavy shedding, high drooling, and gentle family temperament.

ckc-newfoundland-profile.name: Canadian Kennel Club (CKC) - Newfoundland Breed Profile
ckc-newfoundland-profile.note: Official Canadian Kennel Club (country of origin) breed profile for the Newfoundland (Terre-Neuve), covering island province origins, Sir Edwin Landseer's painting ('A Distinguished Member of the Humane Society'), St. Bernard hospice revival, height (26-28 in), weight (120-150 lb), oily water-resistant coat, gentle family nature, and early training needs.

rkc-newfoundland-breed-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Newfoundland Breed Standard
rkc-newfoundland-breed-standard.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Working Group, updated April 1, 2025) confirming extreme-climate evolution, exceptionally gentle docile temperament, oily coarse water-resistant double coat, well-sprung ribs, level underline, and free effortless gait with slight skin roll.

rkc-newfoundland-breed-profile.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Newfoundland Breeds A to Z
rkc-newfoundland-breed-profile.note: Official Royal Kennel Club Breeds A to Z profile specifying large house requirement, daily grooming, shedding, up to 1 hour daily exercise baseline, Breed Watch Category 2 status, Good Practice pre-breeding tests (Cystinuria DNA, BVA/KC Hip and Elbow Dysplasia Schemes), and Best Practice Eye Scheme.

nca-newfoundland-clearances.name: Newfoundland Club of America (NCA) - CHIC Health Screening Clearances
nca-newfoundland-clearances.note: Official Newfoundland Club of America puppy health portal documenting CHIC breeding requirements: Hip Dysplasia (OFA or PennHIP), Elbow Dysplasia (OFA), OFA Congenital Cardiac Clearance (NCA recommends cardiologist echocardiogram for all breeding stock), and Cystinuria DNA testing.

pubmed-newfoundland-cystinuria-slc3a1-20.name: Efficient screening of the cystinuria-related C663T Slc3a1 nonsense mutation in Newfoundland dogs by denaturing high-performance liquid chromatography (JVDI 2006)
pubmed-newfoundland-cystinuria-slc3a1-20.note: Peer-reviewed diagnostic genetics study (J Vet Diagn Invest 2006 Jan;18(1):102-105, PMID 16566266) evaluating screening for the autosomal-recessive cystinuria-causing C663T nonsense mutation in the SLC3A1 gene in Newfoundland dogs.
pubmed-newfoundland-cystinuria-slc3a1-20.publisher: Journal of Veterinary Diagnostic Investigation / PubMed

pubmed-reist-marti-2012-newfoundland-sas.name: Genetic evidence of subaortic stenosis in the Newfoundland dog (Veterinary Record 2012)
pubmed-reist-marti-2012-newfoundland-sas.note: Peer-reviewed genetic study by Reist-Marti et al. (Vet Rec 2012 Jun 9;170(23):597, Epub 2012-05-29, PMID 22645160) establishing autosomal inheritance of subaortic stenosis (SAS) in the Newfoundland dog, noting its elevated breed predisposition and risk of early-adulthood death.

pmc-chetboul-2025-newfoundland-cardiac-s.name: Congenital pulmonic and aortic stenosis in Newfoundland dogs: Results of a 14-year French cardiovascular screening program (921 dogs) (PMC11781725)
pmc-chetboul-2025-newfoundland-cardiac-s.note: Peer-reviewed retrospective study by Chetboul et al. (2025, PMC11781725) analyzing 921 adult Newfoundland dogs screened via transthoracic echocardiography and ECG from 2010 to 2023 in France, finding 0.9% (8/876) affected by aortic stenosis (predominantly subvalvular) and 0.2% (2/879) by pulmonic stenosis, with zero cases detected in the final 3 years while underscoring continued cardiac screening.

pubmed-wilke-2006-newfoundland-cclr.name: Inheritance of rupture of the cranial cruciate ligament in Newfoundlands (JAVMA 2006)
pubmed-wilke-2006-newfoundland-cclr.note: Peer-reviewed veterinary genetics study by Wilke et al. (J Am Vet Med Assoc 2006 Jan 1;228(1):61-64, PMID 16426167) establishing a genetic basis for naturally occurring cranial cruciate ligament rupture (CCLR) in Newfoundland dogs (recessive major gene model with 0.60 allele frequency and 51% partial penetrance).
pubmed-wilke-2006-newfoundland-cclr.publisher: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association / PubMed

wikimedia-newfoundland-dog-001-illryion.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Newfoundland dog 001.jpg
wikimedia-newfoundland-dog-001-illryion.note: High-resolution photograph (3292 x 2466 px) of an adult Newfoundland dog by Flickr user illryion (EXIF capture date 2008-09-28 on Canon PowerShot S5 IS, uploaded to Wikimedia Commons via Flickr upload bot by Ltshears on 2008-11-02). Licensed under CC BY 2.0 Generic.

wikimedia-newfoundland-brown-2-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Newfoundland brown 2.jpg
wikimedia-newfoundland-brown-2-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (1615 x 1351 px) of an adult brown male Newfoundland standing outdoors by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2020-09-13 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2020-09-15). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-australian-terrier-official-standard.name: FCI - Australian Terrier Official Breed Standard No. 8
fci-australian-terrier-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 8 (valid standard dated 2012-10-08, English publication dated 2012-12-05). Covers Australian origin (first breed developed in Australia), Group 3 Section 2 Small-sized Terriers classification without working trial, low-set rectangular build, untrimmed harsh 6 cm topcoat with ruff and soft topknot, blue-and-tan / clear sandy / red colours (white on chest or feet penalized), desirable height (approx. 25 cm dogs, bitches slightly less), and desirable weight (approx. 6.5 kg dogs, bitches slightly less).

fci-australian-terrier-nomenclature.name: FCI - Australian Terrier Breed Nomenclature (No. 8)
fci-australian-terrier-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Australia as country of origin, Group 3 Section 2 Small-sized Terriers classification without working trial, definitive acceptance date (1963-06-20), valid standard date (2012-10-08), English publication date (2012-12-05), and official multilingual names (Australian Terrier, Terrier Australien).

dogs-australia-australian-terrier-profil.name: Dogs Australia (ANKC) - Australian Terrier Breed Profile
dogs-australia-australian-terrier-profil.note: Official country-of-origin kennel club (Dogs Australia / ANKC) profile documenting First Fleet British shipboard ratters, bush vermin and snake hunting, goldfields watchdog role, 1887 Victoria first written standard, protective ruff and apron, winter-to-summer seasonal undercoat shedding, and height/weight notes (dogs approx. 25 cm and 6.5 kg, bitches slightly less).

akc-australian-terrier-official-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Australian Terrier
akc-australian-terrier-official-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Terrier Group; approved January 12, 2021, effective April 7, 2021). Establishes height (10 to 11 inches at the withers), equal skull and muzzle lengths, desirable inverted V-shaped bare black nose-bridge leather, tight dark-rimmed lips, scissor bite, 90° shoulder-to-upper-arm angle, 2.5-inch harsh straight outer coat with soft undercoat, ruff, apron, and silky topknot, accepted colours (blue and tan, solid red, solid sandy), and spirited, affectionate temperament.

akc-australian-terrier-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Australian Terrier Dog Breed Information
akc-australian-terrier-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile documenting 1960 AKC admission (114th breed and first terrier addition in 24 years), height (10-11 inches), weight (15-20 pounds), life expectancy (11-15 years), dirt-repelling double coat, high terrier energy, strict leash/fence advice due to chasing instinct, and short varied training sessions.

rkc-australian-terrier-breed-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Australian Terrier Breed Standard
rkc-australian-terrier-breed-standard.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Terrier Group, updated April 1, 2025) confirming friendly, extroverted, obedient temperament suited to town or country, harsh 6.35 cm (2.5 in) coat with ruff and silky topknot, natural/docked high-set upright tail, and size guide (approx. 25.5 cm / 10 in; approx. 6.5 kg / 14 lb).

rkc-australian-terrier-breed-profile.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Australian Terrier Breeds A to Z
rkc-australian-terrier-breed-profile.note: Official Royal Kennel Club Breeds A to Z profile specifying small size, flat/apartment and small/medium garden suitability, up to 1 hour daily exercise, grooming more than once weekly, shedding, lifespan over 12 years, and Breed Watch Category 1 status.

austtrust-australian-terrier-health.name: Australian Terrier Health Education Trust (AustTrust / ATCA) - Health Issues & CHIC Screening
austtrust-australian-terrier-health.note: Breed health education resource documenting Australian Terrier Club of America (ATCA) CHIC pre-breeding screening recommendations (thyroid, patellar luxation, and congenital eye disease / OFA Eye Certification Registry including PRA) as well as Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease.

pmc-mui-2020-australian-terrier-diabetes.name: Heritability and complex segregation analysis of naturally-occurring diabetes in Australian Terrier Dogs (PLOS ONE 2020)
pmc-mui-2020-australian-terrier-diabetes.note: Peer-reviewed study by Mui, Famula, Henthorn, and Hess (PLoS One 2020 Sep 24;15(9):e0239542, PMID 32970763, PMC7514011) investigating heritability and complex segregation of naturally occurring diabetes mellitus in US-bred Australian Terriers, noting genetic uniformity for diabetes-susceptibility genes in the cohort.
pmc-mui-2020-australian-terrier-diabetes.publisher: PLOS ONE / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-hess-2019-ins-diabetes-australian-te.name: An Exploratory Association Analysis of the Insulin Gene Region With Diabetes Mellitus in Two Dog Breeds (Journal of Heredity 2019)
pmc-hess-2019-ins-diabetes-australian-te.note: Peer-reviewed two-stage genetic association study (J Hered 2019 Dec 17;110(7):793-800, PMID 31587057, PMC6916661) identifying 5 Bonferroni-significant SNPs in the INS gene region associated with diabetes mellitus in Australian Terriers and Samoyeds, and citing US epidemiological risk showing Australian Terriers are 32 times more likely than mixed-breed dogs to develop diabetes.
pmc-hess-2019-ins-diabetes-australian-te.publisher: Journal of Heredity / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

wikimedia-australian-terrier-001-u-lilly.note: High-resolution photograph (2400 x 1800 px) of an adult Australian Terrier standing on grass at the XXXIII Dog Show in Ustroń, Poland, by Lilly M (EXIF capture date 2007-07-01 on Nikon D80, uploaded 2007-07-05). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported (multi-licensed with 2.5/2.0/1.0 and GFDL) on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-australian-terrier-krumel-kett.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Australian Terrier Krümel in der Abendsonne.jpg
wikimedia-australian-terrier-krumel-kett.note: High-resolution photograph (4000 x 3000 px) of an adult female Australian Terrier resting on a lawn by Ketterechts (EXIF capture date 2014-09-07 on Nikon Coolpix P7800, uploaded 2021-04-11). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-austrian-black-and-tan-hound-officia.name: FCI - Austrian Black and Tan Hound (Brandlbracke, Vieräugl) Official Breed Standard No. 63
fci-austrian-black-and-tan-hound-officia.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 63 (valid standard dated 1995-10-10, English publication dated 1996-06-18). Covers Austrian origin, Keltenbracke (Celtic Hound) descent, Group 6 Section 1.2 Medium-sized Scenthounds classification with working trial, agreeable temperament, sensitive nose giving tongue above all for hare, broad skull, close-fitting pigmented lips, 42-tooth scissor bite (max 2 missing PM1/PM2), dewlap-free neck, smooth resilient ~2 cm coat with coarse hair on tail underside, black coat with small fawn markings and mandatory eyebrow spots (Vieräugl), and withers height (overall 48-56 cm; dogs 50-56 cm, bitches 48-54 cm). Omits weight.

fci-austrian-black-and-tan-hound-nomencl.name: FCI - Brandlbracke - (Vieräugl) Breed Nomenclature (No. 63)
fci-austrian-black-and-tan-hound-nomencl.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Austria as country of origin, Group 6 Section 1.2 Medium-sized Hounds classification with working trial, definitive acceptance date (1954-09-03), English publication date (1996-06-18), and official multilingual names (Brandlbracke - Vieräugl, Austrian Black and Tan Hound, Brachet Noir & Feu).

obv-brandlbracke-rasseportrait.name: Österreichischer Brackenverein (ÖBV) - Rasseportrait Brandlbracke
obv-brandlbracke-rasseportrait.note: Official Austrian parent breed club (Österreichischer Brackenverein) breed portrait for the Brandlbracke, documenting its trail-voiced (spurlaut), biddable (leichtführig) woodland and mountain hunting passion, good family suitability, calm district companionship, Austrian solo-hunting ('Brackieren') use on hare, fox, badger, marten, and wild boar, and wounded-game blood tracking ('Nachsuche').

obv-chronik-geschichte.name: Österreichischer Brackenverein (ÖBV) - Chronik & Geschichte
obv-chronik-geschichte.note: Official Österreichischer Brackenverein historical chronicle documenting Ritter von Frank's 1883 purebred breeding initiative using 'Kärntner Brandl' (Vieräugl) strains, the 1884 first Austrian Studbook volume featuring Brandlbracke 'Bergmann' (owned by F. X. Pleban) as Entry No. 1, the 1896 founding of the Österreichischer Brackenklub, and the 1950 founding of the Österreichischer Brackenverein.

scc-brachet-noir-et-feu-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Brachet noir et feu
scc-brachet-noir-et-feu-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile for Brachet noir et feu (Brandlbracke / Vieräugl) confirming height (males 50-56 cm, females 48-54 cm), unsexed approximate weight note ('Environ 20 kg'), smooth dense flexible coat, Celtic hound historical summary, and agreeable companion temperament.

wikimedia-austrian-brandlbracke-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Austrian Brandlbracke.JPG
wikimedia-austrian-brandlbracke-canarian.note: Photograph (747 x 506 px) of an adult Austrian Black and Tan Hound (Brandlbracke) at World Dog Show Helsinki 2014 by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2014-08-09 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2015-08-01). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-brandlbracke-caronna.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Brandlbracke.JPG
wikimedia-brandlbracke-caronna.note: High-resolution photograph (997 x 1287 px) of an Austrian Black and Tan Hound (Brandlbracke) by Steffen Heinz / Caronna (EXIF capture date 2006-11-05 on Konica Minolta DiMAGE X31, uploaded 2006-11-05). Licensed under CC BY-SA 2.5 Generic on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-cavalier-king-charles-spaniel-offici.name: FCI - Cavalier King Charles Spaniel Official Breed Standard No. 136
fci-cavalier-king-charles-spaniel-offici.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 136 (valid standard dated 2026-09-08, English publication dated 2026-10-06). Covers Great Britain origin, Group 9 Section 7 English Toy Spaniels classification without working trial, sporting/affectionate/fearless non-aggressive temperament, almost flat skull, shallow stop, ~1.5 in (3.8 cm) muzzle, non-pendulous lips, complete scissor bite, untrimmed long silky coat, four recognized colours (Black and Tan, Ruby, Blenheim with lozenge spot, Tricolour), and weight (5.4-8 kg). Omits height.

fci-cavalier-king-charles-spaniel-nomenc.name: FCI - Cavalier King Charles Spaniel Breed Nomenclature (No. 136)
fci-cavalier-king-charles-spaniel-nomenc.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Great Britain as country of origin, Group 9 Section 7 English Toy Spaniels classification without working trial, definitive recognition, four colour varieties, and official breed name.

rkc-cavalier-king-charles-spaniel-breed-.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Cavalier King Charles Spaniel Breed Standard
rkc-cavalier-king-charles-spaniel-breed-.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Toy Group, updated April 2025) confirming active, graceful, fearless, gay, non-aggressive character, almost flat skull, ~3.8 cm (1.5 in) muzzle, non-pendulous lips, complete scissor bite, untrimmed silky coat, four accepted colours (Black and Tan, Ruby, Blenheim with lozenge spot, Tricolour), and weight (5.4-8.2 kg / 12-18 lbs).

rkc-cavalier-king-charles-spaniel-breed-.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Cavalier King Charles Spaniel Breeds A to Z
rkc-cavalier-king-charles-spaniel-breed-.note: Official Royal Kennel Club Breeds A to Z profile confirming 1928 breed club formation and 1945 separate breed recognition, flat/apartment suitability, small/medium garden, up to 1 hour daily exercise, shedding, grooming more than once weekly, lifespan over 12 years, Breed Watch Category 2, Good Practice pre-breeding tests (CC/DE DNA, EF DNA, KC Heart Scheme for MVD), Best Practice Eye Scheme, and collaborative BVA/KC SM screening.

akc-cavalier-king-charles-spaniel-offici.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel
akc-cavalier-king-charles-spaniel-offici.note: Official AKC breed standard (Toy Group; approved January 10, 2023, effective March 29, 2023). Establishes height (12 to 13 inches at the withers), weight (13 to 18 pounds proportionate to height), nearly square body slightly longer than tall, withers-to-elbow equal to elbow-to-ground, ~1.5-inch muzzle, silky untrimmed coat with foot feathering, and four allowed colours (disqualifying disallowed colours).

akc-cavalier-king-charles-spaniel-breed-.name: American Kennel Club - Cavalier King Charles Spaniel Dog Breed Information
akc-cavalier-king-charles-spaniel-breed-.note: Official AKC breed profile documenting King Charles I & II history, 1995 AKC recognition, height (12-13 inches), weight (13-18 pounds), life expectancy (12-15 years), adaptable gentle temperament, off-leash safety caveats due to scenting/hunting instincts, and calorie/weight management.

ackcsc-cavalier-health-information.name: American Cavalier King Charles Spaniel Club (ACKCSC) - Cavalier Health Information & CHIC
ackcsc-cavalier-health-information.note: Official US parent breed club health portal detailing CHIC breeding requirements (OFA/PennHIP hips, OFA patellas, annual cardiologist heart screening, periodic ophthalmologist eye certifications) and breed health priorities including Mitral Valve Disease, Syringomyelia (MRI diagnosis), juvenile cataracts, dry eye (KCS), Episodic Falling, and middle-ear (PSOM) signs.
ackcsc-cavalier-health-information.publisher: American Cavalier King Charles Spaniel Club

pmc-mmvd-genetics-review-ckcs-2025.name: Genetic Basis of Myxomatous Mitral Valve Disease in Cavalier King Charles Spaniels (PMC12737390)
pmc-mmvd-genetics-review-ckcs-2025.note: Peer-reviewed 2025 review (PMC12737390) summarizing the complex polygenic basis, candidate gene loci (NEBL, ACE, CDK6, HEPACAM2, COL5A1, FAH), dysregulated TGF-beta/serotonin pathways, and selective breeding-program impact on Myxomatous Mitral Valve Disease (MMVD) in Cavalier King Charles Spaniels.

pmc-sm-mmvd-relationship-ckcs-2024.name: Relationship between syringomyelia and myxomatous mitral valve disease in Cavalier King Charles Spaniels (JVIM 2024)
pmc-sm-mmvd-relationship-ckcs-2024.note: Peer-reviewed study (J Vet Intern Med 2024, PMC10937514) documenting high heritability for clinical Syringomyelia (0.81) and MMVD (0.67) in Cavalier King Charles Spaniels, noting that MMVD accounts for up to 37% of total deaths in Cavaliers younger than 10 years.
pmc-sm-mmvd-relationship-ckcs-2024.publisher: Journal of Veterinary Internal Medicine / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-sm-clinical-predictors-ckcs-2024.name: Clinical predictors of syringomyelia in Cavalier King Charles Spaniels with Chiari-like malformation (Acta Vet Scand 2024)
pmc-sm-clinical-predictors-ckcs-2024.note: Peer-reviewed retrospective MRI study of 89 CKCSs (Acta Vet Scand 2024, PMC10851586) confirming MRI as gold-standard diagnosis and identifying high-PPV clinical predictors of a large clinical syrinx (>=4 mm): phantom scratching, bilateral neck/shoulder scratching, touch aversion around head/neck/shoulder, exacerbation with emotional arousal, and preferred head posture during sleep.
pmc-sm-clinical-predictors-ckcs-2024.publisher: Acta Veterinaria Scandinavica / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pubmed-forman-2012-ckcs-bcan-fam83h.name: Parallel mapping and simultaneous sequencing reveals deletions in BCAN and FAM83H associated with discrete inherited disorders in a domestic dog breed (PLOS Genetics 2012)
pubmed-forman-2012-ckcs-bcan-fam83h.note: Landmark peer-reviewed study by Forman et al. (PLoS Genet 2012 Jan;8(1):e1002462, PMID 22253609, PMC3257292) identifying causal autosomal-recessive deletions in BCAN for Episodic Falling Syndrome (EF) and in FAM83H for Congenital Keratoconjunctivitis Sicca and Ichthyosiform Dermatosis ('Dry Eye and Curly Coat' / CKCSID) in the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel.

wikimedia-ckcs-blenheim-2-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Cavalier King Charles Spaniel Blenheim 2.jpg
wikimedia-ckcs-blenheim-2-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (1055 x 918 px) of an adult Blenheim Cavalier King Charles Spaniel standing outdoors by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2020-09-13 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2020-09-14). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-ckcs-trio-tanakawho.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Cavalier King Charles Spaniel trio.jpg

fci-taiwan-dog-official-standard.name: FCI - Taiwan Dog Official Breed Standard No. 348
fci-taiwan-dog-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 348 (valid standard dated 2015-06-09, English publication dated 2015-08-18, translation revised by Renée Sporre-Willes). Covers Taiwanese central-mountain origin, 1980 cooperative study across 29 indigenous tribes by National Taiwan University, Gifu University, and Nagoya University, Group 5 Section 7 Primitive Type – Hunting Dogs classification without working trial, proportions (muzzle:skull 4.5:5.5, chest:height 4.5-4.7:10, height:body 10:10.5), 45-degree pricked ears, 105-110° shoulder angle, sickle tail, 180-degree quick turn agility, short hard coat (1.5-3 cm; >4.5 cm disqualifying), seven accepted colours, withers height (males 48-53 cm, females 43-48 cm), and weight (males 14-18 kg, females 12-16 kg).

fci-taiwan-dog-nomenclature.name: FCI - Taiwan Dog Breed Nomenclature (No. 348)
fci-taiwan-dog-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Taiwan as country of origin, Group 5 Section 7 Primitive type – Hunting Dogs classification without working trial, provisional acceptance date (2004-11-09), definitive acceptance date (2015-06-09), valid standard date (2015-06-09), and official multilingual names (Taiwan Dog, Chien de Taiwan).

kct-taiwan-dog-standard-348.name: Kennel Club of Taiwan (KCT) - Breed Introduction: Taiwan Dog (FCI Standard No. 348)
kct-taiwan-dog-standard-348.note: Official country-of-origin kennel club (Kennel Club of Taiwan / KCT) bilingual breed page publishing the full FCI Standard No. 348 conformation text, proportions, 1980 National Taiwan University / Gifu University / Nagoya University study summary, height (males 48-53 cm, females 43-48 cm), faults, and disqualifying faults.

akc-taiwan-dog-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Taiwan Dog Breed Information
akc-taiwan-dog-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Foundation Stock Service) documenting loyal/intelligent/versatile character, height (17-20 inches), weight (26-40 pounds), life expectancy (9-13 years), moderate shedding, minimal grooming, high activity needs, strong protective instinct requiring early socialization, indoor household integration, apartment exercise adaptability, and health summary noting no established breed-specific hereditary health issues or mandatory club health tests.

scc-chien-de-taiwan-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Chien de Taïwan
scc-chien-de-taiwan-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile for Chien de Taïwan confirming Southeast Asian hunting-dog descent, dry muscular build, 180-degree turning agility, 1.5 to 3 cm short hard coat, seven colours, weight (males 14-18 kg, females 12-16 kg), and overall height range (43-53 cm).

wikimedia-black-8-year-taiwan-dog-katieh.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Black 8 Year Taiwan Dog.jpg
wikimedia-black-8-year-taiwan-dog-katieh.note: High-resolution photograph (1280 x 1280 px) of an eight-year-old black Taiwan Dog by KatieHuang / Flyskykatie (captured and uploaded 2018-05-08). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-formosan-nina-aechris.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Formosan nina.jpg
wikimedia-formosan-nina-aechris.note: Photograph (315 x 266 px) of a Taiwan Dog (Formosan Dog) by Aechris (captured/originally uploaded to en.wikipedia 2007-05-09, transferred to Wikimedia Commons by ToB on 2007-05-18). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported (and GFDL) on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-smalandsstovare-official-standard.name: FCI - Smålandsstövare Official Breed Standard No. 129
fci-smalandsstovare-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 129 (valid standard dated 2017-08-22, English publication dated 2017-10-02, translation by Renée Sporre-Willes). Covers Swedish origin in Småland, 1611-1718 war-hound and spitz farm-dog heritage, 1921 first standard, Group 6 Section 1.2 Medium-sized Hounds classification with working trial, solo hare and fox utilization (never pack or deer), almost square build, naturally short (stumpy/bear-tail) or long/half-length tail, harsh medium-length double coat with dense hair between toes and pads, black-and-tan or liver-brown-and-tan coloration, and withers height (males 46-54 cm, ideal 50 cm; females 42-50 cm, ideal 46 cm). Omits weight.

fci-smalandsstovare-nomenclature.name: FCI - Smålandsstövare Breed Nomenclature (No. 129)
fci-smalandsstovare-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Sweden as country of origin, Group 6 Section 1.2 Medium-sized Hounds classification with working trial, definitive acceptance date (1955-01-12), English standard publication date (2017-10-02), and official multilingual names (Smålandsstövare, Chien courant du Småland).

skk-smalandsstovare-profile-sv.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Smålandsstövare Rasprofil
skk-smalandsstovare-profile-sv.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) Swedish-language breed profile for Smålandsstövare documenting Swedish national breed status, height (46-54 cm males, 42-50 cm females), densely furred closed paws for multi-day hunting, fast game-finding ('upptagare'), nuanced voice, reliable return to owner, unsuitability solely as a companion or apartment/kennel dog, easy-care coat, and health note documenting hip dysplasia (HD) and epilepsy.

skk-smalandsstovare-profile-en.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Smålandsstövare (Swedish Dog Breeds)
skk-smalandsstovare-profile-en.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) English-language national breed profile confirming 1921 SKK recognition, Småland county heritage, height (males 46-54 cm, ideal 50 cm; females 42-50 cm, ideal 46 cm), black or liver-brown with tan markings, high energy, strong family bonding, and international alternate names (Småland Hound, Chien courant du Småland, Sabueso de Småland, Smoolanninajokoira, Smålandsstøver).

ssf-smalandsstovare-ras-2026.name: Svenska Smålandsstövareföreningen / Svenska Stövarklubben - Rasspecifik avelsstrategi (RAS) för Smålandsstövare
ssf-smalandsstovare-ras-2026.note: Official Swedish breed-specific breeding strategy (RAS, published March 2026 via Svenska Stövarklubben) documenting everyday mental stability, general good health with isolated cases of epilepsy, Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA) / cardiac disease, and cryptorchidism, strict epilepsy breeding exclusions, removal of the mandatory pre-mating HD status requirement from 2020, and controlled outcross projects to broaden genetic diversity.

scc-chien-courant-du-smaland-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Chien courant du Småland
scc-chien-courant-du-smaland-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile for Chien courant du Småland confirming all-weather hunting capability, weight explicitly listed as unspecified (NP), 1950s final open-studbook infusion history, and calm companion nature.

wikimedia-smalandsstovare-female-canaria.note: Photograph (565 x 461 px) of an adult female Smålandsstövare (Smaland Hound) by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2013-12-13 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2014-04-16). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-smaland-hound-male-canarian.note: Photograph (399 x 332 px) of a male Smålandsstövare (Smaland Hound) by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2006-03-02, uploaded 2013-01-20). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-griffon-fauve-de-bretagne-official-s.name: FCI - Griffon Fauve de Bretagne (Fawn Brittany Griffon) Official Breed Standard No. 66
fci-griffon-fauve-de-bretagne-official-s.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 66 (valid standard dated 2003-03-25, English publication dated 2003-05-05). Covers French origin in Brittany, 14th-century Huet des Ventes pack, 19th-century wolf-hunting heritage, 1949 Marcel Pambrun club founding, 1980s Bernard Vallée revival, Group 6 Section 1.2 Medium-sized hounds classification with working trial, 'chopper' hunting voice, good-natured sociable temperament, dewlap-free skin, very rough harsh short golden-wheaten to brick-red coat, and withers height (males and females 48-56 cm, with 2 cm tolerance for exceptional specimens). Omits weight.

fci-griffon-fauve-de-bretagne-nomenclatu.name: FCI - Griffon Fauve de Bretagne Breed Nomenclature (No. 66)
fci-griffon-fauve-de-bretagne-nomenclatu.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming France as country of origin, Group 6 Section 1.2 Medium-sized Hounds classification with working trial, English standard publication date (2003-05-05), and official multilingual names (Griffon Fauve de Bretagne, Fawn Brittany Griffon, Grifón Leonado de Bretaña).

scc-griffon-fauve-de-bretagne-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Griffon fauve de Bretagne
scc-griffon-fauve-de-bretagne-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile for Griffon fauve de Bretagne confirming Breton wolf-hunting history, 1949 Club du Fauve de Bretagne founding under Marcel Pambrun, 1980s revival under Bernard Vallée, 'hunting first' motto, weight explicitly left unspecified ('-'), and rough dry fawn coat.

scc-griffon-fauve-de-bretagne-caractere.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Le griffon fauve de Bretagne : le caractère et la fonctionnalité
scc-griffon-fauve-de-bretagne-caractere.note: Official SCC breed feature (updated 2025-11-03) interviewing working judge Alain Rousseau, detailing gentle calm indoor nature, extreme sociability with visitors and pack mates (unsuited to guarding), early hunting awakening around 4 months, working career lasting to 10-12 years, all-climate versatility, 'chopper' voice, and minimal curry-brush coat care.

scc-griffon-fauve-de-bretagne-standard-c.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Le griffon fauve de Bretagne : standard et commentaires
scc-griffon-fauve-de-bretagne-standard-c.note: Official SCC standard commentary by Hervé Gourdon (updated 2025-11-03) detailing equal skull and muzzle lengths with parallel axes, non-pendulous lips with modest moustache, untrimmed/unstripped natural harsh coat, height (48-56 cm for both sexes, +2 cm tolerance), and disqualifying faults including hind dewclaws and long woolly coats.

rkc-griffon-fauve-de-bretagne-breed-stan.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Griffon Fauve de Bretagne (Imp) Breed Standard
rkc-griffon-fauve-de-bretagne-breed-stan.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Hound Group, updated April 1, 2025) confirming 10:9 body length-to-withers-height ratio, gentle sociable affectionate temperament, natural untrimmed rough coat, and size (48-56 cm, with 2 cm tolerance). Omits weight.

rkc-griffon-fauve-de-bretagne-breed-prof.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Griffon Fauve de Bretagne (Imp) Breeds A to Z
rkc-griffon-fauve-de-bretagne-breed-prof.note: Official Royal Kennel Club Breeds A to Z profile confirming medium size, country lifestyle with small house and small/medium garden, weekly grooming, shedding, up to 1 hour daily baseline exercise, and Breed Watch Category 1 status.

skk-griffon-fauve-de-bretagne-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Griffon fauve de bretagne Rasprofil
skk-griffon-fauve-de-bretagne-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for Griffon fauve de bretagne confirming historic name Grand Fauve de Bretagne, Brittany origin, height (approx. 48-56 cm), easy-care rough coat, unsuitability solely as a companion dog, high exercise and mental stimulation demands, friendly calm human interaction, and note that very small numbers in Sweden prevent reliable breed-wide health assessment.

fci-st-bernard-official-standard.name: FCI - St. Bernard (St. Bernhardshund, Bernhardiner) Official Breed Standard No. 61
fci-st-bernard-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 61 (valid standard dated 2016-04-04, English publication dated 2016-06-03). Covers Swiss origin at the Great St. Bernard Pass hospice, 1800 Bonaparte pass crossing, Barry, February 1884 Swiss Dog Stud Book (SHSB #1 Léon + 28 entries), March 15 1884 Basel club, June 2 1887 Swiss national dog recognition, Group 2 Section 2.2 Mountain-type Molossoids classification without working trial, two varieties (Short-haired Stockhaar and Long-haired), 9:10 height-to-body ratio, head >1/3 withers height, ~2:1 muzzle depth-to-length ratio, mantle and splash-coated white-and-red coloration, and withers height (males 70-90 cm, females 65-80 cm). Omits weight.

fci-st-bernard-nomenclature.name: FCI - St. Bernhardshund - Bernhardiner (St. Bernard) Breed Nomenclature (No. 61)
fci-st-bernard-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Switzerland as country of origin, Group 2 Section 2.2 Mountain-type Molossoids classification without working trial, Short-haired and Long-haired varieties, valid standard date (2016-04-04), publication date (2016-06-03), and official multilingual names (St. Bernhardshund - Bernhardiner, St. Bernard, Chien du Mont Saint-Bernard - Saint-Bernard).

skg-st-bernhardshund-profile.name: Schweizerische Kynologische Gesellschaft (SKG) - Rasseportrait St. Bernhardshund
skg-st-bernhardshund-profile.note: Official Swiss Kennel Club (SKG) breed profile authored jointly with the Schweizerischer St. Bernhards-Club (S.St.B.C.), confirming Great St. Bernard Pass altitude (2,473 m), 1695 pictorial and 1707 archival hospice records, Barry (>40 lives saved, died 1814, Natural History Museum Bern exhibit), 1954-08-28 definitive FCI recognition, height (70-90 cm males, 65-80 cm females), friendly/sensitive/occasionally stubborn character, daily shedding-season brushing, unsuitability for narrow stair-heavy apartments, and modern sport roles (mobility, search, mantrailing).

akc-st-bernard-official-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Saint Bernard
akc-st-bernard-official-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Working Group; approved April 13, 1998, effective May 31, 1998). Establishes shorthaired and longhaired varieties, massive broad skull, scissors or even bite (scissors preferable), pronounced throat/neck dewlap, chest not reaching below elbows, bushy tail without flag, red-and-white / brindle-and-white mantle and splash-coated patterns, and minimum shoulder height (27.5 inches dogs, 25.5 inches bitches).

akc-st-bernard-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Saint Bernard Dog Breed Information
akc-st-bernard-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile documenting 1885 AKC recognition, hospice rescue history, brandy-cask myth debunking, height (28-30 in males, 26-28 in females), weight (140-180 lb males, 120-140 lb females), life expectancy (8-10 years), moderate exercise needs, carting/drafting suitability, low alone-time tolerance, high drooling, and bloat/hip/eye health awareness.

rkc-st-bernard-breed-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club - St. Bernard Breed Standard
rkc-st-bernard-breed-standard.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Working Group, updated April 1, 2025) confirming steady kindly benevolent temperament, reasonably tight eyelids with excessive haw unacceptable, complete scissor bite, chest never below elbows, rough and smooth varieties, minimum height (75 cm dogs, 70 cm bitches), and unhurried sound movement.

rkc-st-bernard-breed-profile.name: The Royal Kennel Club - St. Bernard Breeds A to Z
rkc-st-bernard-breed-profile.note: Official Royal Kennel Club Breeds A to Z profile confirming extra-large size, large house requirement, up to 1 hour daily exercise, shedding, grooming more than once weekly, lifespan under 10 years, Sir Edwin Landseer brandy-cask myth origin, Breed Watch Category 3 status, and Good Practice pre-breeding tests (BVA/KC Elbow Dysplasia, Eye Scheme, and Hip Dysplasia).

sbca-breeder-referral-health-2024.name: Saint Bernard Club of America (SBCA) - Hereditary Defects & CHIC Health Screening Recommendations
sbca-breeder-referral-health-2024.note: Official US parent breed club (incorporated 1888) breeder-referral and health portal documenting common hereditary defects (hip and elbow dysplasia, entropion, epilepsy, heart defects) and CHIC basic health screening recommendations: Hip Dysplasia (min 24 mo, OFA/PennHIP), Elbow Dysplasia (min 24 mo, OFA), ACVO Eye Exam (min 22 mo), Boarded Cardiologist Cardiac Exam (min 24 mo), Degenerative Myelopathy DNA test, and optional Autoimmune Thyroiditis panel.

pmc-letko-2020-st-bernard-cntnap1-lppn3.name: A CNTNAP1 Missense Variant Is Associated with Canine Laryngeal Paralysis and Polyneuropathy (Genes 2020)
pmc-letko-2020-st-bernard-cntnap1-lppn3.note: Peer-reviewed whole-genome sequencing study by Letko et al. (Genes (Basel) 2020 Nov 27;11(12):1426, PMID 33261176, PMC7761076) identifying a likely pathogenic missense variant in CNTNAP1 (c.2810G>A; p.Gly937Glu) causing autosomal-recessive laryngeal paralysis and polyneuropathy (LPPN3) in Saint Bernard and Leonberger dogs.

pubmed-ekenstedt-2014-st-bernard-arhgef1.name: An ARHGEF10 deletion is highly associated with a juvenile-onset inherited polyneuropathy in Leonberger and Saint Bernard dogs (PLOS Genetics 2014)
pubmed-ekenstedt-2014-st-bernard-arhgef1.note: Peer-reviewed study by Ekenstedt et al. (PLoS Genet 2014 Oct 2;10(10):e1004635, PMID 25275565, PMC4183422) identifying a 10-bp deletion in ARHGEF10 (c.1955_1958+6del) highly associated with severe juvenile-onset inherited polyneuropathy (LPN1) in Leonberger and Saint Bernard dogs.

pubmed-bech-nielsen-1978-st-bernard-oste.name: Frequency of osteosarcoma among first-degree relatives of St. Bernard dogs (JNCI 1978)
pubmed-bech-nielsen-1978-st-bernard-oste.note: Peer-reviewed epidemiological and pedigree study (J Natl Cancer Inst 1978 Feb;60(2):349-353, PMID 271748) documenting familial aggregation and genetic predisposition to osteosarcoma among first-degree relatives of St. Bernard dogs.
pubmed-bech-nielsen-1978-st-bernard-oste.publisher: Journal of the National Cancer Institute / PubMed

fci-griffon-nivernais-official-standard.name: FCI - Griffon Nivernais Official Breed Standard No. 17
fci-griffon-nivernais-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 17 (valid standard dated 2004-03-24, English publication dated 2004-04-02, translated by John Miller and Raymond Triquet). Covers French origin in Nivernais, descent from Gallic Canis Segusius and Grey Dogs of Saint Louis, 1789 Revolution decline, 1925 club founding, Group 6 Section 1.2 Medium-sized hounds classification with working trial, wild-boar gun-hunting utilization, Barbouillaud rough shaggy coat, black-overlaid colour rules (never orange; wolf/boar/blue/hare shades), dry dewlap-free neck, elongated hare-like feet, and withers height (males 55-62 cm, females 53-60 cm). Omits weight.

fci-griffon-nivernais-nomenclature.name: FCI - Griffon Nivernais Breed Nomenclature (No. 17)
fci-griffon-nivernais-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming France as country of origin, Group 6 Section 1.2 Medium-sized Hounds classification with working trial, definitive acceptance date (1959-12-15), valid standard date (2004-03-24), English publication date (2004-04-02), and official multilingual names (Griffon Nivernais, Grifón del Nivernais).

scc-griffon-nivernais-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Griffon nivernais
scc-griffon-nivernais-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile for Griffon nivernais confirming height (males 55-62 cm, females 53-60 cm), weight explicitly listed as unspecified (NP), historical 'chien de pays' reconstruction with Vendéen/Foxhound/Otterhound blood, 1925 club founding under Vicomte d'Anchald and 1969 revival, balanced non-aggressive yet dominant pack character, unsuitability for city/apartment living, cold/wet hardiness with greater heat sensitivity, brushing 3-4 times yearly, ear hygiene, post-meal rest / two-meal veterinary advice against bloat (GDV), and absence of particular breed pathologies.

scc-club-du-griffon-nivernais.name: Club du Griffon Nivernais (SCC) - Site Officiel
scc-club-du-griffon-nivernais.note: Official French parent breed club (Club du Griffon Nivernais, founded in 1925 and affiliated with the Société Centrale Canine) overseeing breed conservation, hunting trials, and breeding standards in France.

skk-griffon-nivernais-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Griffon nivernais Rasprofil
skk-griffon-nivernais-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for Griffon nivernais confirming French origin, wild-boar hunting specialization, height (55-62 cm males, 53-60 cm females), burr-resistant coarse easy-care coat, regular ear cleaning, loud howling hunting cry, high exercise needs, friendly social family temperament when actively hunted, unsuitability solely as a companion dog, and note that very small Swedish numbers prevent definitive breed-wide health assessment.

sgnk-griffon-nivernais-ras-2016.name: Svenska Griffon Nivernais Klubben / SKK - Rasspecifik avelsstrategi (RAS) Griffon Nivernais
sgnk-griffon-nivernais-ras-2016.note: Official Swedish breed-specific breeding strategy (RAS Edition 2, dated 2016-09-27, published via SKK) citing French veterinary literature (Mondon, 2001) on absence of particular congenital/hereditary breed diseases, documenting 6 of 6 Swedish radiographed dogs as HD-free A (keeping HD screening voluntary), noting isolated cases of missing teeth, and emphasizing genetic-diversity management across unrelated lines.
sgnk-griffon-nivernais-ras-2016.publisher: Svenska Griffon Nivernais Klubben / Svenska Kennelklubben

wikimedia-griffon-nivernais-alephalpha.note: High-resolution photograph (1200 x 800 px) of an adult French Griffon Nivernais outdoors by Alephalpha (captured 2004-03-27, uploaded 2008-10-22). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported (and GFDL) on Wikimedia Commons.
