wikimedia-chien-griffon-nivernais-thomon.note: High-resolution photograph (1280 x 858 px) of an adult Griffon Nivernais at the Salon International de l'Agriculture de Paris 2023 by Thomon (captured and uploaded 2023-03-04). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

ukc-carolina-dog-official-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Carolina Dog Official Breed Standard
ukc-carolina-dog-official-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (Sighthound & Pariah Group, recognized 1995/1996, revised May 2008; also referenced directly by the AKC FSS Breed Standards compendium). Covers Southeastern US origin, shy/suspicious pariah character (outward aggression a very serious fault), equal skull and muzzle lengths, tight predominantly black lips, scissor or level bite, oblique dark brown almond eyes with unbroken black rims, versatile upright ears, solid pink tongue (dark spots disqualifying), seasonal double coat with erect coarse dorsal guard hairs, preferred deep red ginger colour (plus piebald and black blanket), average height (17 to 24 inches), and approximate weight (30 to 55 pounds, sexes overlapping broadly).

akc-carolina-dog-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Carolina Dog Breed Information
akc-carolina-dog-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Foundation Stock Service, admitted 2017; parent club Carolina Dog Fanciers of America) documenting height (17.75-19.5 inches), weight (30-55 pounds), life expectancy (12-15 years), moderate seasonal shedding, cat-like minimal grooming, low drooling, pack mentality, stranger reserve, daily exercise and sports suitability (agility, obedience, rally), and health note stating no mandatory national breed-club health tests are currently published.

cdfa-carolina-dog-breed-standard.name: Carolina Dog Fanciers of America (CDFA) - Breed Standard
cdfa-carolina-dog-breed-standard.note: Official AKC parent breed club (recognized April 2022) breed standard page for the Carolina Dog detailing history, general appearance, average withers height (18 to 24 inches depending on sex and build), weight, head, and body conformation.

pubmed-brisbin-risch-1997-primitive-dogs.name: Primitive dogs, their ecology and behavior: unique opportunities to study the early development of the human-canine bond (JAVMA 1997)
pubmed-brisbin-risch-1997-primitive-dogs.note: Peer-reviewed landmark paper by I. Lehr Brisbin Jr. (Savannah River Ecology Laboratory, University of Georgia, Aiken, SC) and Thomas S. Risch (J Am Vet Med Assoc 1997 Apr 15;210(8):1122-1126, PMID 9108912) documenting the ecology, social behaviour, digging habits, and American Dingo / Carolina Dog population of the Southeastern United States.
pubmed-brisbin-risch-1997-primitive-dogs.publisher: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association / PubMed

pmc-van-asch-2013-precolumbian-dogs.name: Pre-Columbian origins of Native American dog breeds, with only limited replacement by European dogs, confirmed by mtDNA analysis (Proc Biol Sci 2013)
pmc-van-asch-2013-precolumbian-dogs.note: Peer-reviewed mitochondrial DNA study by van Asch, Zhang, Oskarsson, and Savolainen (Proc Biol Sci 2013 Sep 7;280(1766):20131142, PMID 23843389, PMC3730590) providing the first DNA-based evidence that free-ranging Carolina Dogs of South Carolina and Georgia retain ancient East Asian / pre-Columbian maternal ancestry, including the frequent unique haplotype A184.
pmc-van-asch-2013-precolumbian-dogs.publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-mealey-2023-pglycoprotein-abcb1.name: Canine and feline P-glycoprotein deficiency: What we know and where we need to go (J Vet Pharmacol Ther 2023)
pmc-mealey-2023-pglycoprotein-abcb1.note: Peer-reviewed veterinary pharmacology review by Katrina L. Mealey, Jane G. Owens, and Elaine Freeman (J Vet Pharmacol Ther 2023 Jan;46(1):1-16, Epub 2022-11-03, PMID 36326478, PMC10092536) documenting ABCB1-1Δ (MDR1) P-glycoprotein deficiency drug sensitivity (e.g., ivermectin neurotoxicity) and reporting detection of the variant in 4 of 13 tested Carolina Dogs.
pmc-mealey-2023-pglycoprotein-abcb1.publisher: Journal of Veterinary Pharmacology and Therapeutics / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

wikimedia-carolina-dog-hunter-calabash13.note: High-resolution photograph (1776 x 1198 px) of Carolina Dog 'Hunter' in Calabash, North Carolina, by Calabash13 (EXIF capture date 2007-06-10 on Kodak DX4330, file description dated 2013-03-13, uploaded 2013-05-05). fci-kishu-official-standard.name: FCI - Kishu Official Breed Standard No. 318
fci-kishu-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 318 (valid standard dated 2016-10-30, English publication dated 2017-02-10). Covers Japanese origin in Kishu (Wakayama and Mie Prefectures), 1934 Natural Monument designation, Group 5 Section 5 Asian Spitz and related breeds classification without working trial, 10:11 height-to-body ratio, faithful/docile/alert temperament, tight lips, scissor bite, nearly triangular dark brown eyes, small forward-inclined prick ears, curled or sickle tail, harsh straight double coat (white, red, and sesame), and withers height (males 52 cm, females 49 cm, tolerance +/- 3 cm). Omits weight.

fci-kishu-nomenclature.name: FCI - Kishu Breed Nomenclature (No. 318)
fci-kishu-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Japan as country of origin, Group 5 Section 5 Asian Spitz and related breeds classification without working trial, definitive acceptance date (1982-02-01), English publication date (2017-02-10), and official breed name (Kishu).

jkc-kishu-breed-standard.name: Japan Kennel Club (JKC) - Kishu (紀州) Breed Standard
jkc-kishu-breed-standard.note: Official country-of-origin kennel club (Japan Kennel Club / JKC) breed standard page for Kishu (紀州, Standard No. 318), confirming Kishu region origin (Wakayama and Mie Prefectures), 1934 colour unification and disappearance of spotted coats after 1945, predominance of white coats, 1934 Natural Monument status, accepted colours (white, red, sesame), and withers height (males 52 cm +/- 3 cm, females 49 cm +/- 3 cm).

akc-kishu-ken-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Kishu Ken Dog Breed Information
akc-kishu-ken-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Foundation Stock Service since 2005, Hound Group designation, Companion Events since 2008) documenting Wakayama police mascot 'Kishu-kun', height (19-22 inches), weight (30-60 pounds), life expectancy (12-15 years), seasonal moulting (1-2 times/year), fast-paced food-motivated training, sports versatility, starch/beef/chicken dietary allergy sensitivity, and autoimmune health priorities (allergies, autoimmune thyroiditis, Addison's disease, SLE/CLE/DLE) with recommended patella, hip, elbow, ophthalmologist, and thyroid tests.

nkkc-national-kishu-ken-club.name: National Kishu Ken Club (NKKC) - Breed Standard, History & NAKC Health Statement
nkkc-national-kishu-ken-club.note: Official US AKC parent breed club portal documenting Japan's most common purebred boar-hunting dog, late-1960s US introduction (1971 California/Massachusetts breeding), Japanese temperament principles (kan'i, ryosei, soboku), conformation (oval chest 45-50% of height, 110-120° shoulder angle, full seasonal undercoat shed), and NAKC Health Statement covering owner-reported allergy rates (30% skin inflammation, 40% itching), genetic Autoimmune Thyroiditis (OFA thyroid panel CHIC required, retest every 2-3 years), Addison's Disease, SLE/CLE, OFA dentition and eye CHIC requirements, DNA repository recommendation, and optional joint evaluations.

skk-kishu-breed-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Kishu Rasprofil
skk-kishu-breed-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for Kishu confirming Kii Peninsula origin (Wakayama and Mie), shika-inu grouping alongside Kai and Shikoku, 2020 first Swedish registration, height (approx. 52 cm males, 49 cm females), easy-care double coat, loyal yet stranger-reserved hunting/watchdog character, and note that very few Swedish individuals prevent national health assessment.

scc-kishu-breed-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Kishu
scc-kishu-breed-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile for the Kishu confirming Japanese Kishu mountain origin, 1934 Natural Monument designation, rough straight double coat, and approximate unsexed weight note (20 to 25 kg).

pmc-tanabe-2007-japanese-asian-dog-phylo.name: Phylogenetic studies of dogs with emphasis on Japanese and Asian breeds (Proc Jpn Acad Ser B 2007)
pmc-tanabe-2007-japanese-asian-dog-phylo.note: Peer-reviewed study by Yuichi Tanabe (Proc Jpn Acad Ser B Phys Biol Sci 2007 Jan;82(10):375-387, PMID 25792769, PMC4338834) analyzing the phylogeny and blood protein polymorphisms of Japanese native dog breeds including the Kishu (designated Natural Monument in 1934).
pmc-tanabe-2007-japanese-asian-dog-phylo.publisher: Proceedings of the Japan Academy, Series B / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-cmah-2019-japanese-dogs-neu5gc.name: Molecular characterization of cytidine monophospho-N-acetylneuraminic acid hydroxylase (CMAH) associated with the erythrocyte Neu5Gc/Neu5Ac phenotype in dogs (PMC6842231)
pmc-cmah-2019-japanese-dogs-neu5gc.note: Peer-reviewed molecular haematology study (2019, PMC6842231) documenting erythrocyte Neu5Ac/Neu5Gc sialic acid polymorphism (CMAH gene variation) across traditional Japanese dog breeds including Kishu dogs, Kai dogs, Shiba dogs, and Japanese Spaniels.

wikimedia-kishu-ken-snow-crispette.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Kishu Ken in the Snow.png
wikimedia-kishu-ken-snow-crispette.note: High-resolution photograph (2000 x 1333 px) of an eight-month-old white Kishu Ken ('Fionna') in snow by CJ Hammond / Crispette (EXIF capture date 2015-01-27 on Canon EOS Rebel T3i, uploaded 2015-01-29). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-kishu-sesame2-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Kishu-sesame2.jpg
wikimedia-kishu-sesame2-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (2001 x 1940 px) of an adult sesame Kishu Ken standing outdoors by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2021-08-07 on Canon EOS 1100D, uploaded 2021-08-11). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-leonberger-official-standard.name: FCI - Leonberger Official Breed Standard No. 145
fci-leonberger-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 145 (valid standard dated 1996-01-04, English publication dated 2002-09-20). Covers German origin in Leonberg near Stuttgart (Baden-Württemberg), Heinrich Essig's 1830s–1846 foundation crossing black-and-white Newfoundland, Grand St. Bernard 'Barry', and Pyrenean Mountain Dog, Group 2 Section 2.2 Mountain-type Molossoids classification without working trial, 9:10 height-to-body ratio, ~50% chest depth, 1:1 skull-to-muzzle ratio, wrinkle-free head, tight black lips, dewlap-free neck, 42-tooth scissor bite (pincer accepted), lion-yellow/red/red-brown/sandy coat with mandatory black mask, and withers height (dogs 72-80 cm, avg 76 cm; bitches 65-75 cm, avg 70 cm). Omits weight.

fci-leonberger-nomenclature.name: FCI - Leonberger Breed Nomenclature (No. 145)
fci-leonberger-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Germany as country of origin, Group 2 Section 2.2 Molossian/Mountain type classification without working trial, definitive acceptance date (1955-02-17), valid standard date (1996-01-04), and official breed name (Leonberger).

akc-leonberger-official-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Leonberger
akc-leonberger-official-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Working Group, recognized January 1, 2010). Establishes strong sexual dimorphism, untrimmed natural water-resistant double coat with lion-like male mane, tight dry black lips, mandatory black mask, cat feet, height (males 28-31.5 in, 30 in preferred; females 25.5-29.5 in, 27.5 in preferred), 9:10 body ratio, white chest patch <=5 in limit, and gentle, steady family temperament.

akc-leonberger-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Leonberger Dog Breed Information
akc-leonberger-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile documenting Heinrich Essig's Leonberg history, nickname 'Leo', pronunciation ('Lee-uhn-berger'), height (28-31.5 in males, 25.5-29.5 in females), weight (110-170 lb males, 90-140 lb females), life expectancy (7 years), heavy year-round and seasonal shedding, daily vigorous adult exercise, unsuitability for apartments/small lots, group obedience training, and therapy/drafting versatility.

rkc-leonberger-breed-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Leonberger Breed Standard
rkc-leonberger-breed-standard.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Working Group, updated April 1, 2025) confirming friendly, self-assured, playful non-aggressive temperament, 9:10 body ratio, tight black lips, dewlap-free neck, natural double coat with lion mane and mandatory black mask, and withers height (dogs 72-80 cm, bitches 65-75 cm). Omits weight.

rkc-leonberger-breed-profile.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Leonberger Breeds A to Z
rkc-leonberger-breed-profile.note: Official Royal Kennel Club Breeds A to Z profile specifying large house requirement, country lifestyle, shedding, lifespan under 10 years, Breed Watch Category 2 status, Good Practice pre-breeding tests (BVA/KC Elbow Dysplasia, BVA/KC/ISDS Eye Scheme with gonioscopy for PLA, BVA/KC Hip Dysplasia), and Best Practice DNA tests (LPPN3, LPN1, LPN2, LEMP).

lca-leonberger-health-glossary.name: Leonberger Club of America (LCA) - New Owner's Glossary & CHIC Required Health Tests
lca-leonberger-health-glossary.note: Official US parent breed club owner's glossary detailing CHIC required breeding health tests: hip conformation (OFA fair/good/excellent or PennHIP <=0.47), elbow conformation (OFA), eye evaluation (CERF/OFA), OFA thyroid, LPN1, LPN2, and LEMP DNA status, plus recommended OFA cardiac evaluation.

lca-leonberger-find-a-leo.name: Leonberger Club of America (LCA) - Find a Leonberger
lca-leonberger-find-a-leo.note: Official Leonberger Club of America breed overview noting Leonberg, Germany origin, thick double-coat frequent care, daily exercise, regular nail trimming, and average lifespan of 8 to 10 years.

pmc-becker-2017-leonberger-gja9-lpn2.name: A GJA9 frameshift variant is associated with polyneuropathy in Leonberger dogs (BMC Genomics 2017)
pmc-becker-2017-leonberger-gja9-lpn2.note: Peer-reviewed whole-genome sequencing study by Becker et al. (BMC Genomics 2017 Aug 25;18(1):662, PMID 28841859, PMC5574090) identifying a GJA9 frameshift variant (c.1107_1108delAG; p.Glu370AsnfsTer12) causing autosomal incomplete-dominant Leonberger Polyneuropathy Type 2 (LPN2).
pmc-becker-2017-leonberger-gja9-lpn2.publisher: BMC Genomics / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-minor-2018-leonberger-napepld-lemp.name: Canine NAPEPLD-associated models of human myelin disorders (Scientific Reports 2018)
pmc-minor-2018-leonberger-napepld-lemp.note: Peer-reviewed study by Minor, Letko, Becker, Drögemüller et al. (Sci Rep 2018 Apr 11;8:5818, PMID 29643404, PMC5895582) identifying an autosomal-recessive NAPEPLD missense variant (c.538G>C; p.A180P) causing juvenile-onset Leukoencephalomyelopathy (LEMP, onset ages 1.3 to 4 years) in Leonberger dogs.
pmc-minor-2018-leonberger-napepld-lemp.publisher: Scientific Reports / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-letko-2020-leonberger-genomic-divers.name: Genomic diversity and population structure of the Leonberger dog breed (Genetics Selection Evolution 2020)
pmc-letko-2020-leonberger-genomic-divers.note: Peer-reviewed study (2020, PMC7557023) examining genomic diversity, historical wartime population bottlenecks, inbreeding, and longevity (mean male lifespan 7.9 years, lower than female longevity) in the Leonberger breed.
pmc-letko-2020-leonberger-genomic-divers.publisher: Genetics Selection Evolution / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pubmed-adamts17-poag-basset-fauve-de-bre.name: Forman et al. (2015) - Two Independent Mutations in ADAMTS17 Are Associated with Primary Open Angle Glaucoma in the Basset Hound and Basset Fauve de Bretagne Breeds of Dog
pubmed-adamts17-poag-basset-fauve-de-bre.note: Peer-reviewed PLoS One study (PMID 26474315; DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0140436) establishing the strong association between an ADAMTS17 mutation and primary open angle glaucoma (POAG) in the Basset Fauve de Bretagne.
pubmed-adamts17-poag-basset-fauve-de-bre.publisher: National Library of Medicine (PubMed / PLoS One)

fci-braque-francais-pyrenees-official-st.name: FCI - Braque Français, type Pyrénées (French Pointing Dog Pyrenean Type) Official Breed Standard No. 134
fci-braque-francais-pyrenees-official-st.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 134 (valid standard dated 2023-08-01, English publication dated 2023-09-22, translated by Peggy Davis). Covers French origin, Group 7 Section 1.1 Continental Pointing Dogs ('Braque' type) classification with working trial, structural distinctions from the Gascogne type (tighter skin, chestnut-brown nose, less pendulous lips, ears set above eye line ending 2 cm from nose leather, slight or no dewlap, lighter limbs, tight feet, finer shorter coat, fine docked or naturally short tail), disqualifications (entropion, ectropion, anury, split nose, syndactyly), and withers height (males 51-58 cm, females 49-56 cm). Omits weight.

fci-braque-francais-pyrenees-nomenclatur.name: FCI - Braque Français - Type Pyrénées Breed Nomenclature (No. 134)
fci-braque-francais-pyrenees-nomenclatur.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming France as country of origin, Group 7 Section 1.1 Continental Pointing Dogs ('Braque' type) classification with working trial, definitive acceptance date (1955-01-18), English standard publication date (2023-09-22), and official multilingual names.

scc-braque-francais-type-pyrenees-profil.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Braque français, type pyrénées
scc-braque-francais-type-pyrenees-profil.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile confirming Gaston Phebus (Count of Foix) heritage, height (males 51-58 cm, females 49-56 cm), weight explicitly unspecified (NP), finer shorter coat than Gascogne, intelligent/obedient temperament sensitive to undeserved punishment, strong bond with owner and children, and city adaptability when acclimated young with regular sporting exercise.

ckc-braque-francais-pyrenees-standard.name: Canadian Kennel Club (CKC) - Official Breed Standard: Braque Français (Pyrenees)
ckc-braque-francais-pyrenees-standard.note: Official Canadian Kennel Club breed standard (Group I Sporting Dogs; recognized 1992, effective January 2015) establishing weight (17 to 25 kg / 37.5 to 55 lb), chestnut/cinnamon-and-white or solid brown coloration with optional pale tan points, disqualifications (black nose, split nose, traces of black in coat), and structural traits.

akc-braque-francais-pyrenean-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Braque Francais Pyrenean Dog Breed Information
akc-braque-francais-pyrenean-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Foundation Stock Service) documenting smaller and more popular status vs. Gascogne type, natural retrieve and love of water, gentle sociable submissive temperament, height (18.5-23 in), weight (40-55 lb via AKC weight chart), life expectancy (12-15 years), minimal weekly grooming, nail/ear/dental care, sports versatility, and generally healthy breed profile.

skk-braque-francais-type-pyrenees-profil.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Braque français, type pyrénées Rasprofil
skk-braque-francais-type-pyrenees-profil.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile confirming southwestern France and central Pyrenees origin, twice-yearly seasonal shedding, very easy-care short fine coat, friendly/easygoing/cooperative hunting and active-family character, and note that very few individuals in Sweden preclude national breed-wide health assessment.

skk-skf-braque-francais-pyrenees-ras.name: Specialklubb för Kontinentala Fågelhundar (SKF) / SKK - Rasspecifik avelsstrategi (RAS): Braque français, type pyrénées
skk-skf-braque-francais-pyrenees-ras.note: Official Swedish breed-specific breeding strategy (RAS, published via SKK and SKF) documenting small regional population management and recommending pre-breeding radiographic hip dysplasia screening (HD-A or HD-B).
skk-skf-braque-francais-pyrenees-ras.publisher: Specialklubb för Kontinentala Fågelhundar / Svenska Kennelklubben

pmc-mastrangelo-2018-bfp-genomic-charact.name: Genomic characterization of the Braque Français type Pyrénées dog and relationship with other breeds (PLOS ONE 2018)
pmc-mastrangelo-2018-bfp-genomic-charact.note: Peer-reviewed genome-wide SNP study by Mastrangelo, Biscarini, Tolone, Auzino, Ragatzu, Spaterna, and Ciampolini (PLoS One 2018 Dec 5;13(12):e0208548, PMID 30517199, PMC6281230) analyzing genetic variation, LD decay, recent Ne (51 at 13 generations ago vs. ~1,530 historically), and FROH inbreeding in Braque Français, type Pyrénées, showing inbreeding well within the range of other dog breeds.
pmc-mastrangelo-2018-bfp-genomic-charact.publisher: PLOS ONE / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-mastrangelo-2018-bfp-roh-diversity.name: Genome-wide diversity and runs of homozygosity in the 'Braque Français, type Pyrénées' dog breed (BMC Research Notes 2018)
pmc-mastrangelo-2018-bfp-roh-diversity.note: Peer-reviewed high-density SNP-array study by Mastrangelo, Biscarini, Auzino, Ragatzu, Spaterna, and Ciampolini (BMC Res Notes 2018 Jan 9;11:13, PMC5761150) reporting observed/expected heterozygosity (0.371 / 0.359), effective population size (Ne = 27.5), and FROH range (0.0526-0.225), concluding the breed retains sufficient genetic variability for conservation and improvement.
pmc-mastrangelo-2018-bfp-roh-diversity.publisher: BMC Research Notes / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

fci-poodle-official-standard-172.name: FCI - Caniche (Poodle) Official Breed Standard No. 172
fci-poodle-official-standard-172.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 172 (dated 2024-04-05). Covers Group 9 Section 2 Poodle classification without working trial, conformation, curly and corded coat types, colours, and size categories (Standard 45-62 cm, Medium 35-45 cm, Miniature 28-35 cm, Toy 24-28 cm).

akc-poodle-toy-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Poodle (Toy) Dog Breed Information
akc-poodle-toy-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile covering Caniche and Pudel history, temperament, sports versatility, coat grooming, and health screening.

pcaf-poodle-health-concerns.name: The Poodle Club of America - Health Concerns & Testing
pcaf-poodle-health-concerns.note: Breed club health resource documenting sebaceous adenitis, Addison's disease, Cushing's disease, bloat/GDV, hip and patella evaluations, eye exams, and prcd-PRA screening.

pmc-canine-sebaceous-adenitis-7877684.name: Canine sebaceous adenitis (PMC7877684)
pmc-canine-sebaceous-adenitis-7877684.note: Peer-reviewed veterinary review (PMC7877684, PMID 33692587) on canine sebaceous adenitis clinical signs, breed predisposition including Poodles, and lifelong management.

wikimedia-standard-poodle-black-lying-do.note: Photograph (1828 x 1827 px) of a black Standard Poodle by Belinda Hankins Miller (captured 2007-09-18, uploaded 2007-09-24). Licensed under CC BY 2.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-standard-poodle-black-male-sit.note: Photograph (854 x 1279 px) of a black male Standard Poodle named Theo by A W (captured 2007-06-29, uploaded 2007-07-05). Licensed under CC BY-SA 2.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-karelian-bear-dog-official-standard.name: FCI - Karelian Bear Dog (Karjalankarhukoira) Official Breed Standard No. 48
fci-karelian-bear-dog-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 48 (valid standard dated 2014-11-03, English publication dated 2015-05-27, translated by Finnish Kennel Club and revised by Renée Sporre-Willes). Covers Finnish origin (Ladoga Karelia, Olonets, Russian Karelia; Komi/Zyrians dog ancestry; 1936 breeding start, 1945 first standard, 1946 first registrations), Group 5 Section 2 Nordic hunting dogs classification (working trial in Finland, Sweden, and Norway), elk and bear baying role, 2:3 muzzle-to-skull ratio, 42-tooth scissor bite, natural bobtail equal to curled tail, harsh straight black-and-white double coat, withers height (males 54-60 cm, ideal 57 cm; females 49-55 cm, ideal 52 cm), and ideal weight (males 25-28 kg, females 17-20 kg).

fci-karelian-bear-dog-nomenclature.name: FCI - Karjalankarhukoira (Karelian Bear Dog) Breed Nomenclature (No. 48)
fci-karelian-bear-dog-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Finland as country of origin, Group 5 Section 2 Nordic Hunting Dogs classification, definitive acceptance date (1954-08-02), valid standard date (2014-11-03), English publication date (2015-05-27), and official multilingual names (Karjalankarhukoira, Karelian Bear Dog, Chien d'ours de Carélie).

spj-karjalankarhukoira-pevisa-2026-2028.name: Suomen Pystykorvajärjestö (SPJ) - Karjalankarhukoiran PEVISA-ohjelma 2026–2028
spj-karjalankarhukoira-pevisa-2026-2028.note: Official Finnish parent breed club (Suomen Pystykorvajärjestö) publication of the Finnish Kennel Club Breeding Science Committee decision (17.9.2025) establishing the mandatory 2026–2028 PEVISA breeding programme for Karelian Bear Dogs: official hip dysplasia radiographs (HD-D mated only to HD-A), official eye exams (min age 12 mo; excluding hereditary cataracts, PRA, and PHTVL/PHPV grades 2–6; grade 1 mated to clear), and genetic-diversity cap of max 60 registered offspring per dog (max 25 from matings under age 5).

kennelliitto-karjalankarhukoira-hirvenha.name: Suomen Kennelliitto - Karjalankarhukoirien Hirvenhaukut-ottelu 2026 (90th Anniversary)
kennelliitto-karjalankarhukoira-hirvenha.note: Official Finnish Kennel Club (Suomen Kennelliitto) news report documenting the 2026 national Hirvenhaukut moose-barking championship in Ilmajoki and confirming the Karelian Bear Dog's 90th anniversary year (1936–2026) as one of Finland's three flagship native hunting-trial breeds.

skk-karelsk-bjornhund-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Karelsk björnhund Rasprofil
skk-karelsk-bjornhund-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for Karelsk björnhund confirming Finnish/Karelian origin, elk and bear baying utilization, unsuitability solely as a companion dog, ideal height (approx. 57 cm males, 52 cm females), easy-care double coat brushed during moults, strong fighting spirit and potential dog aggression (never human aggression), and health status noting hip dysplasia (HD) occurs.

akc-karelian-bear-dog-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Karelian Bear Dog Breed Information
akc-karelian-bear-dog-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Foundation Stock Service; parent club American Karelian Bear Dog Alliance) documenting pronunciation ('Ka-reel-e-an Bear Dog'), height (19-23.5 in), weight (44-49 lb), life expectancy (11-13 years), weekly grooming, nail/ear/dental care, fenced yard exercise, fighting spirit around other dogs, and non-recommendation with young children.

wrbi-wind-river-bear-institute.name: Wind River Bear Institute (WRBI) - About Us & Karelian Bear Dog Partners
wrbi-wind-river-bear-institute.note: Official portal of the Wind River Bear Institute (founded 1996 in Montana by wildlife biologist Carrie L. Hunt) documenting the training and deployment of Finnish-lineage Karelian Bear Dogs for non-lethal human-wildlife conflict mitigation with black, grizzly, and polar bears.

guardian-2023-karelian-bear-conflict-dog.name: The Guardian - How training dogs to chase bears might just save a grizzly or two (2023)
guardian-2023-karelian-bear-conflict-dog.note: Feature report by Isabelle Groc (The Guardian, May 23, 2023) documenting Wind River Bear Institute Karelian Bear Dog deployments across Montana, Alaska (including Denali National Park and Alaska fire service), Canada, and Japan, noting that roughly 20% of evaluated puppies qualify as bear-conflict dogs.

pmc-kyostila-2013-itga10-chondrodysplasi.name: Canine Chondrodysplasia Caused by a Truncating Mutation in Collagen-Binding Integrin Alpha Subunit 10 (PLOS ONE 2013)
pmc-kyostila-2013-itga10-chondrodysplasi.note: Peer-reviewed study by Kyöstilä, Lappalainen, and Lohi (PLoS One 2013 Sep 25;8(9):e75621, PMID 24086591, PMC3783422) identifying an autosomal-recessive nonsense mutation (c.2083C>T; p.Arg695*) in ITGA10 causing short-limbed chondrodysplasia in Norwegian Elkhound and Karelian Bear Dog breeds.
pmc-kyostila-2013-itga10-chondrodysplasi.publisher: PLOS ONE / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-kyostila-2019-alpl-hypophosphatasia.name: A homozygous missense variant in the alkaline phosphatase gene ALPL is associated with a severe form of canine hypophosphatasia (Scientific Reports 2019)
pmc-kyostila-2019-alpl-hypophosphatasia.note: Peer-reviewed study by Kyöstilä, Syrjä, Lappalainen, Arumilli, Hundi, Karkamo, Viitmaa, Hytönen, and Lohi (Sci Rep 2019 Jan 30;9:973, PMID 30700765, PMC6353930) reporting the first naturally occurring hypophosphatasia (HPP) in animals, caused by an autosomal-recessive missense variant in ALPL (c.1301T>G; p.Val434Gly) in Karelian Bear Dogs with a 17% carrier frequency across 509 tested KBDs.
pmc-kyostila-2019-alpl-hypophosphatasia.publisher: Scientific Reports / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-kyostila-2021-pou1f1-pituitary-dwarf.name: Intronic variant in POU1F1 associated with canine pituitary dwarfism (Human Genetics 2021)
pmc-kyostila-2021-pou1f1-pituitary-dwarf.note: Peer-reviewed study by Kyöstilä, Niskanen, Arumilli, Donner, Hytönen, and Lohi (Hum Genet 2021;140:1553-1562, Epub 2021-02-06, PMID 33550451, PMC8519942) identifying an autosomal-recessive intronic splice-region variant in POU1F1 (c.605-3C>A) causing combined pituitary hormone deficiency / pituitary dwarfism in Karelian Bear Dogs (8% carrier frequency across screened KBDs).
pmc-kyostila-2021-pou1f1-pituitary-dwarf.publisher: Human Genetics / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

wikimedia-karjalankarhukoira-looking-at-.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Karjalankarhukoira, Karelian Bear Dog looking at camera.jpg
wikimedia-karjalankarhukoira-looking-at-.note: High-resolution photograph (3888 x 2592 px) of a 10-year-old male Karelian Bear Dog sitting on grass by Uusijani (EXIF capture date 2010-09-17 on Canon EOS 1000D, uploaded 2010-09-20). Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-karjalankarhukoira-standing-pr.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Karjalankarhukoira, Karelian Bear Dog standing profile.jpg
wikimedia-karjalankarhukoira-standing-pr.note: High-resolution photograph (2444 x 3667 px) of a 10-year-old male Karelian Bear Dog standing outdoors by Uusijani (EXIF capture date 2010-09-17 on Canon EOS 1000D, uploaded 2010-09-20). Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-lapponian-herder-official-standard.name: FCI - Lapponian Herder (Lapinporokoira) Official Breed Standard No. 284
fci-lapponian-herder-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 284 (valid standard dated 2026-02-11, English publication dated 2026-03-23, translated by the Finnish Kennel Club). Covers Finnish origin, Sámi reindeer-herding history, 1950s registration and 1966-12-10 separation from Finnish Lapphund, Group 5 Section 3 Nordic Watchdogs and Herders classification without working trial, rectangular proportions (+10% length, chest depth ~half height), docile/calm/friendly/energetic temperament barking readily when working, low-set hanging/rotating tail never curled over back, coarse straight Arctic double coat, black/greyish/dark brown coloration with lighter markings (blue, sable, and fawn disqualified), and withers height (ideal males 51 cm, females 46 cm, tolerance +/- 3 cm). Omits weight.

fci-lapponian-herder-nomenclature.name: FCI - Lapinporokoira (Lapponian Herder) Breed Nomenclature (No. 284)
fci-lapponian-herder-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Finland as country of origin, Group 5 Section 3 Nordic Watchdogs and Herders classification without working trial, definitive acceptance date (1970-11-13), English publication date (2026-03-23), and official multilingual names (Lapinporokoira, Lapponian Herder, Berger Finnois de Laponie, Finnischer Lapplandhirtenhund).

kennelliitto-lapinporokoira-breed-profil.name: Suomen Kennelliitto - Lapinporokoira Rotuesittely
kennelliitto-lapinporokoira-breed-profil.note: Official country-of-origin Finnish Kennel Club (Suomen Kennelliitto) breed profile confirming height (males 51 cm +/- 3 cm, females 46 cm +/- 3 cm), sexed weight (males 19-25 kg, females 15-20 kg), average lifespan (11-14 years), May 2025 survey count of 61 actively herding Lapponian Herders in Finland, open breed register for northern working reindeer dogs, tangle-free dirt- and snow-repelling double coat, PEVISA eye-exam timing, and hereditary eye priorities (cataracts and two DNA-testable types of PRA).

lappalaiskoirat-lapinporokoira-pevisa-20.name: Lappalaiskoirat ry - Lapinporokoiran PEVISA-ohjelma (valid through 31.12.2029)
lappalaiskoirat-lapinporokoira-pevisa-20.note: Official Finnish parent breed club (Lappalaiskoirat ry) publication of the Lapponian Herder PEVISA breeding health programme valid until 31 December 2029: minimum mating age 22 months, mandatory valid eye examination (<=24 months old at mating) required before a dog's third mating (after two litters), and official Finnish Kennel Club hip dysplasia radiograph evaluations.

lappalaiskoirat-hereditary-diseases-appe.name: Lappalaiskoirat ry - Hereditary Diseases Occurring in Lapponian Dogs (Buyer Agreement Appendix)
lappalaiskoirat-hereditary-diseases-appe.note: Official English-language health disclosure appendix published by Lappalaiskoirat ry (dated 5 January 2025) summarizing hereditary diseases occurring in Lapponian breeds: cataracts, PRA, elbow dysplasia, hip dysplasia, hypothyroidism, rare Addison's disease, Pompe disease (genetic test available), malocclusions, and rarity of allergies.

skk-lapsk-vallhund-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Lapsk vallhund Rasprofil
skk-lapsk-vallhund-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for Lapsk vallhund confirming 1966 breed separation, open studbook registration of working reindeer dogs in Sweden and Finland to protect genetic diversity, profuse twice-yearly shedding, minimal dirt-repelling coat care, vocal barking herding style, and health notes covering PRA (at least two variants), RD, PPM, cataract, retinopathy, HD, cryptorchidism, and isolated cases of epilepsy and hypothyroidism.

akc-lapponian-herder-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Lapponian Herder Dog Breed Information
akc-lapponian-herder-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Foundation Stock Service, Herding Group) documenting Sámi reindeer-herding history, vocal barking (4/5), trainability (4/5), life expectancy (10-14 years), stranger reserve (especially females), and high mental/physical stimulation needs. (Note: AKC's web summary box prints an unsexed 70-pound weight figure that conflicts with country-of-origin Finnish Kennel Club weights of 19-25 kg / 15-20 kg).

pmc-kaukonen-2021-lapponian-herder-ift12.name: A missense variant in IFT122 associated with a canine model of retinitis pigmentosa (Human Genetics 2021)
pmc-kaukonen-2021-lapponian-herder-ift12.note: Peer-reviewed University of Helsinki study (Hum Genet 2021 Nov;140(11):1569-1579, Epub 2021-02-19, PMID 33606121, PMC8519925) screening 563 Lapponian Herders and identifying an autosomal-recessive missense variant in IFT122 (c.3176G>A; p.R1059H) causing slowly progressing late-onset PRA (mean diagnosis age 9.0 +/- 2.9 years) distinct from PRCD-PRA and BEST1 cmr3.
pmc-kaukonen-2021-lapponian-herder-ift12.publisher: Human Genetics / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-zangerl-2010-lapponian-herder-best1-.name: Assessment of canine BEST1 variations identifies new mutations and establishes an independent bestrophinopathy model (cmr3) (Molecular Vision 2010)
pmc-zangerl-2010-lapponian-herder-best1-.note: Peer-reviewed ocular genetics study by Zangerl, Wickström, Slavik, Lindauer et al. (Mol Vis 2010 Dec 16;16:2791-2804, PMID 21197113, PMC3008713) identifying two linked exon 10 mutations in BEST1 (p.P463fs, p.G489V) causing autosomal-recessive Canine Multifocal Retinopathy Type 3 (cmr3) in the Lapponian Herder.
pmc-zangerl-2010-lapponian-herder-best1-.publisher: Molecular Vision / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-seppala-2013-lapphund-gaa-pompe.name: A Nonsense Mutation in the Acid α-Glucosidase Gene Causes Pompe Disease in Finnish and Swedish Lapphunds (PLOS ONE 2013)
pmc-seppala-2013-lapphund-gaa-pompe.note: Peer-reviewed study by Seppälä, Reuser, and Lohi (PLoS One 2013 Feb 14;8(2):e56825, PMID 23457621, PMC3573005) identifying the autosomal-recessive GAA nonsense mutation (c.2237G>A; p.W746*) causing Pompe disease in Finnish and Swedish Lapphunds and explicitly documenting heterozygous carriers in Lapponian Herders (with no clinical cases reported in the breed at publication).
pmc-seppala-2013-lapphund-gaa-pompe.publisher: PLOS ONE / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

wikimedia-lapponian-herder-black-tan-3-c.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Lapponian Herder black & tan 3.jpg
wikimedia-lapponian-herder-black-tan-3-c.note: High-resolution photograph (1099 x 1193 px) of an adult black-and-tan male Lapponian Herder by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2020-08-23 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2020-08-23). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-lapinporokoira-in-riga-tomasin.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Lapinporokoira in Riga.JPG
wikimedia-lapinporokoira-in-riga-tomasin.note: High-resolution photograph (2254 x 1742 px) of an adult Lapponian Herder (Lapinporokoira) at Baltic Winner 2013 in Riga by Томасина (EXIF capture date 2013-11-10 on Canon PowerShot SX50 HS, uploaded 2013-11-25). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-australian-kelpie-official-standard.name: FCI - Australian Kelpie Official Breed Standard No. 293
fci-australian-kelpie-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 293 (valid standard dated 2012-10-08, English publication dated 2012-12-11). Covers Australian origin, Group 1 Section 1 Sheepdogs classification without working trial, lithe muscular appearance free of weediness, fox-like head, tight clean lips, scissor bite, almond brown eyes, pointed erect ears, right-angle shoulder/upper arm, low-set brushed tail never carried past vertical, single-tracking movement settling four-square, 2-3 cm rain-resisting double coat, seven accepted colours (black, black and tan, red, red and tan, fawn, chocolate, smoke blue), and withers height (males 46-51 cm, females 43-48 cm). Omits weight.

fci-australian-kelpie-nomenclature.name: FCI - Australian Kelpie Breed Nomenclature (No. 293)
fci-australian-kelpie-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Australia as country of origin, Group 1 Section 1 Sheepdogs classification without working trial, definitive acceptance date (1973-09-03), valid standard date (2012-10-08), English publication date (2012-12-11), and official multilingual names (Australian Kelpie, Kelpie Australien).

fci-australian-kelpie-extended-standard.name: FCI / ANKC - Extended Breed Standard of the Australian Kelpie (No. 293)
fci-australian-kelpie-extended-standard.note: Official FCI/ANKC illustrated extended breed standard for the Australian Kelpie detailing breed history (Warrock Station in Victoria, Gleeson's Kelpie, Brutus & Jennie, Caesar, King's Kelpie, Forbes trial, Barb named after the Melbourne Cup horse, John Quinn, King & McLeod), height (dogs 46-51 cm, bitches 43-48 cm), coat (2-3 cm), anatomical faults, and temperament (human biting foreign to the breed).
fci-australian-kelpie-extended-standard.publisher: Fédération Cynologique Internationale / Australian National Kennel Council

dogs-australia-australian-kelpie-standar.name: Dogs Australia (ANKC) - Australian Kelpie Breed Standard
dogs-australia-australian-kelpie-standar.note: Official country-of-origin kennel club (Dogs Australia / ANKC) breed standard (Group 5 Working Dogs) confirming Australian origin, mild tractable disposition with inexhaustible energy, 10:9 body-length-to-withers-height proportion, chest deep rather than wide, fox-like head, almond eyes, pricked ears, and low-set brush tail.

akc-australian-kelpie-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Australian Kelpie Dog Breed Information
akc-australian-kelpie-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Foundation Stock Service, Herding Group) covering New South Wales and Victoria pastoral history, height (17-20 inches), weight (35-50 pounds), life expectancy (10-13 years), moderate shedding, weekly brushing, unsuitability for apartment living, indoor 'off switch' after heavy exercise, herding tendency toward children/pets, and sports versatility.

skk-australian-kelpie-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Australian kelpie Rasprofil
skk-australian-kelpie-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for Australian kelpie confirming 1902 first standard, height (46-51 cm males, 43-48 cm females), easy-care short double coat, mild benevolent human temperament, unsuitability solely as a companion dog, tendency to become stressed if mismanaged, age-appropriate puppy walk lengths, working/rescue/agility/obedience roles, and health status (relatively healthy; low proportion of mostly mild HD; isolated ED and patellar luxation).

svekk-australian-kelpie-health.name: Svenska Kelpieklubben (SVEKK) - Hälsa hos Australian Kelpie
svekk-australian-kelpie-health.note: Official Swedish breed club health resource for Australian Kelpie documenting Cerebellar Abiotrophy (CA, two variants, DNA risk/marker test), Inborn Lipid Malabsorption (ILM / lipase 1 deficiency in newborn puppies with breed-validated DNA test and lipase 2 onset around 12 weeks), Collie Eye Anomaly (CEA), caution regarding unvalidated multi-breed DNA panels, 2011-2015 screened HD average (~12%, range 7-14%), and Agria Breed Profile heart-disease notes (endocardiosis / mitral insufficiency).

scc-kelpie-australien-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Kelpie australien
scc-kelpie-australien-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile for Kelpie australien confirming height (43-51 cm), weight unspecified (NP), divergence of Working Kelpie and Show Kelpie lines, 'backing' over sheep's backs, preference for company over solitary confinement, and recommendation to divide adult meals into two daily feedings.

pmc-wade-2022-kelpie-cerebellar-abiotrop.name: Cerebellar Abiotrophy in Australian Working Kelpies Is Associated with Two Major Risk Loci (Genes 2022)
pmc-wade-2022-kelpie-cerebellar-abiotrop.note: Peer-reviewed University of Sydney GWAS study by Wade, Pan, Taylor, and Williamson (Genes (Basel) 2022 Sep 23;13(10):1709, PMID 36292596, PMC9602046) analyzing 49 affected Kelpies and mapping autosomal-recessive Cerebellar Abiotrophy (CA) to two major risk loci: an early-onset locus on CFA20 (visible within days to weeks of birth) and a later-onset ataxia locus on CFA9 carrying a missense variant in exon 5 of VMP1 (p.P160Q).

pmc-kucharczyk-2019-kelpie-cea-nhej1.name: Collie Eye Anomaly in Australian Kelpie dogs in Poland (BMC Veterinary Research 2019)
pmc-kucharczyk-2019-kelpie-cea-nhej1.note: Peer-reviewed clinical and molecular report by Kucharczyk, Cislo-Pakuluk, and Bedford (BMC Vet Res 2019 Nov 4;15(1):392, PMID 31684941, PMC6829813) documenting choroidal hypoplasia (Collie Eye Anomaly) confirmed by the 7.8-kb NHEJ1 deletion DNA test in an Australian Kelpie breeding line in Poland (affected proband, affected dam, and 8 carriers among 21 tested relatives) and emphasizing DNA testing alongside ophthalmoscopy due to 'go normal' masking.
pmc-kucharczyk-2019-kelpie-cea-nhej1.publisher: BMC Veterinary Research / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-chew-2019-kelpie-morphology-dingo.name: Genomic Characterization of External Morphology Traits in Kelpies Does Not Support Common Ancestry with the Australian Dingo (Genes 2019)
pmc-chew-2019-kelpie-morphology-dingo.note: Peer-reviewed University of Sydney genomic study by Chew, Willet, Haase, and Wade (Genes (Basel) 2019 May 3;10(5):337, PMID 31058880, PMC6563003) characterizing external morphology gene variants (ear carriage and coat colour) across Australian Kelpies and Working Kelpies and showing they do not support shared ancestry with the Australian Dingo.

pmc-kelpie-herding-personality-2022.name: Valued personality traits in livestock herding Kelpies—Development and application of the Herding Dog Assessment Form (PLOS ONE 2022)
pmc-kelpie-herding-personality-2022.note: Peer-reviewed behavioural study (PLOS ONE 2022 Apr 26, PMC9041829) analyzing personality and working-trait assessments across 228 purebred livestock-herding Kelpies in Australia, highlighting behavioural regulation/cognition (calmness, intelligence, patience), persistence, and stamina.
pmc-kelpie-herding-personality-2022.publisher: PLOS ONE / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

wikimedia-australian-kelpie-red-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:AustralianKelpieRed.jpg
wikimedia-australian-kelpie-red-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (1222 x 1038 px) of an adult red Australian Kelpie by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2021-07-03 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2021-07-05). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-australian-kelpie-portrait-dav.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Australian Kelpie portrait.jpg
wikimedia-australian-kelpie-portrait-dav.note: High-resolution outdoor portrait (2592 x 3872 px) of a purebred Australian Kelpie named Diesel by Flickr user davepaku (EXIF capture date 2007-05-13 on Nikon D80, uploaded to Wikimedia Commons by Pharaoh Hound on 2007-05-16, license reviewed by Vaya on 2007-05-17). Licensed under CC BY-SA 2.0 Generic.

fci-borzoi-official-standard.name: FCI - Russkaya Psovaya Borzaya (Borzoi – Russian Hunting Sighthound) Official Breed Standard No. 193
fci-borzoi-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 193 (dated 2019-11-05, translated by Anna Samsonova and edited by Dr. Eugene Yerusalimsky). Covers Russian origin (15th-century roots; Greyhound / Chistopsovy, Mountain Gorsky, and Crimean Sighthound heritage), Group 10 Section 1 Long-haired or fringed Sighthounds classification, hare/fox/wolf coursing utilization, 5-10% elongated proportions, calm temperament, thin fold-free skin, always-black nose and eye rims, long silky coat, disqualifying colours (brown, blue, isabella/lilac, dilute with non-black nose), and desirable withers height (males 75-85 cm, females 68-78 cm). Omits weight.

fci-borzoi-nomenclature.name: FCI - Russkaya Psovaya Borzaya (Borzoi) Breed Nomenclature (No. 193)
fci-borzoi-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Russia as country of origin, Group 10 Section 1 Long-haired or fringed Sighthounds classification, definitive acceptance date (1956-01-13), English standard publication date (2019-11-05), and official multilingual names (Russkaya Psovaya Borzaya, Borzoi – Russian Hunting Sighthound, Barzoï).

bcoa-borzoi-breed-standard.name: Borzoi Club of America (BCOA) - Official Breed Standard of the Borzoi
bcoa-borzoi-breed-standard.note: Official US parent breed club publication of the AKC Borzoi Breed Standard detailing Roman-nosed profile, scissor or even bite, blade-like flattened forelegs, hare-shaped feet, silky coat with curly neck frill, low-carried curved tail, minimum heights (males >=28 in, bitches >=26 in), weight range (males 75-105 pounds, bitches 15-20 pounds less), and ground-covering single-tracking trot.

akc-borzoi-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Borzoi Dog Breed Information
akc-borzoi-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile confirming height (28 in & up male, 26 in & up female), weight (75-105 pounds male, 60-85 pounds female), life expectancy (9-14 years), 35-40 mph running speed, calm housedog demeanour, on-leash safety around small running animals, modest adult food intake vs. growing puppies, sighthound anaesthetic sensitivity, bloat awareness, and national breed club recommended health tests (Cardiac Exam, Ophthalmologist Evaluation, Thyroid Evaluation, and Degenerative Myelopathy DNA SOD1A).

rkc-borzoi-breed-profile.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Borzoi Breeds A to Z
rkc-borzoi-breed-profile.note: Official Royal Kennel Club Breeds A to Z profile (Hound Group) confirming 'Borzoi' etymology ('swift'), 16th-century Russian imperial aristocracy wolf-hunting history, large house requirement, up to 1 hour daily exercise baseline, shedding, grooming more than once weekly, and Breed Watch Category 2 status.

skk-borzoi-breed-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Borzoi Rasprofil
skk-borzoi-breed-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for Borzoi confirming Russian origin, height (75-85 cm males, 68-78 cm females), easy-care silky coat brushed a couple of times weekly with heavy twice-yearly seasonal shedding, calm quiet indoor demeanour (rarely barks; may refuse rainy outings), strong dog-pack sociability, and bloat exercise precautions around feeding.

skk-borzoi-ras-2022.name: Borzoi-Ringen / SKK - Rasspecifik avelsstrategi (RAS) för Borzoi (2022)
skk-borzoi-ras-2022.note: Official Swedish breed-specific breeding strategy (RAS, revised 2022, published via SKK) detailing the 2021 Borzoi-Ringen owner health survey (cancer 8% mainly in older dogs, thyroid, bloat, rapid-growth musculoskeletal injuries, and mean longevity of 8.8 years overall: 7.4 years males, 9.8 years females).

bcoa-health-information.name: Borzoi Club of America (BCOA) - Health Information & Holter Screening Program
bcoa-health-information.note: Official Borzoi Club of America Health Committee portal (updated December 29, 2025) documenting the BCOA Holter monitor rental committee, OFA open-database screening clinics, degenerative myelopathy education, and bloat (GDV) research links.

pmc-sykes-2023-borzoi-cardiac-disease.name: A multicenter, retrospective study of cardiac disease in Borzoi dogs (Frontiers in Veterinary Science 2023)
pmc-sykes-2023-borzoi-cardiac-disease.note: Peer-reviewed multicenter study across 14 veterinary cardiology centres by Sykes, Wesselowski, Saunders et al. (Front Vet Sci 2023 Jan 26;10:1102494, PMID 36777677, PMC9909344) evaluating 152 client-owned Borzoi: ventricular arrhythmias identified in 25/131 (19%, with 76% having minimal or no structural heart disease), DCM (n = 13), MMVD (n = 12, 92% mild), tricuspid valve dysplasia (n = 6), and sudden death in 3/55 (5%) with long-term follow-up.
pmc-sykes-2023-borzoi-cardiac-disease.publisher: Frontiers in Veterinary Science / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pubmed-borzoi-echocardiography-2024.name: Echocardiographic values and prevalence of cardiac abnormalities in clinically healthy adult Borzoi dogs (Am J Vet Res 2024)
pubmed-borzoi-echocardiography-2024.note: Peer-reviewed cardiology study (Am J Vet Res 2024 Jan 2:1-10, PMID 38154250) establishing Borzoi-specific echocardiographic reference intervals and reporting DCM and mild MMVD at similar frequencies in clinically healthy adult Borzoi, supporting echocardiographic screening for DCM.
pubmed-borzoi-echocardiography-2024.publisher: American Journal of Veterinary Research / PubMed

pmc-zeng-2014-sod1-dm-breeds.name: Breed Distribution of SOD1 Alleles Previously Associated with Canine Degenerative Myelopathy (JVIM 2014)
pmc-zeng-2014-sod1-dm-breeds.note: Peer-reviewed multi-breed genetic survey (J Vet Intern Med 2014, PMC4238831) reporting SOD1:c.118G>A genotypes across 787 tested Borzoi (548 G/G, 209 G/A, 30 A/A; mutant A allele frequency 0.17).
pmc-zeng-2014-sod1-dm-breeds.publisher: Journal of Veterinary Internal Medicine / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-grahn-2006-borzoi-retinopathy.name: Diagnostic Ophthalmology: Multi-focal chorioretinopathy of Borzoi dogs (Canadian Veterinary Journal / PMC1482450)
pmc-grahn-2006-borzoi-retinopathy.note: Peer-reviewed veterinary ophthalmology report (PMC1482450, citing Storey, Grahn, and Alcorn, Vet Ophthalmol 2005;8:337-347) detailing multifocal chorioretinopathy ('Borzoi retinopathy') and confirming it is distinct from Progressive Retinal Atrophy.
pmc-grahn-2006-borzoi-retinopathy.publisher: Canadian Veterinary Journal / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pubmed-conaway-1985-borzoi-lymphocytic-t.name: The familial occurrence of lymphocytic thyroiditis in borzoi dogs (Am J Med Genet 1985)
pubmed-conaway-1985-borzoi-lymphocytic-t.note: Peer-reviewed six-year clinical and pedigree study across four generations of Borzoi dogs (PMID 3840332) documenting the familial occurrence of autoimmune lymphocytic thyroiditis causing primary hypothyroidism.
pubmed-conaway-1985-borzoi-lymphocytic-t.publisher: American Journal of Medical Genetics / PubMed

wikimedia-borzoi-white-grey-2-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Borzoi white & grey 2.jpg
wikimedia-borzoi-white-grey-2-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (1708 x 1471 px) of an adult white-and-grey male Borzoi by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2020-08-23 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2020-08-24). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-borzoi-red-white-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Borzoi red & white.jpg
wikimedia-borzoi-red-white-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (1950 x 1699 px) of an adult red-and-white female Borzoi by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2020-08-23 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2020-08-24). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

pubmed-dogo-argentino-deafness-2021.name: Congenital sensorineural deafness in Dogo Argentino dogs: Prevalence and phenotype associations (Vet Rec 2021)
pubmed-dogo-argentino-deafness-2021.note: Peer-reviewed Veterinary Record retrospective study (Vet Rec. 2021 May;188(9):e299, Epub 2021-04-19, PMID 33870537, DOI 10.1002/vetr.299) analyzing BAER results for 811 US Dogo Argentinos: 74.23% bilaterally hearing, 20.35% unilaterally deaf, and 5.43% bilaterally deaf (25.77% overall), with significantly lower prevalence in head-patched dogs.

fci-japanese-terrier-official-standard.name: FCI - Nihon Teria (Japanese Terrier) Official Breed Standard No. 259
fci-japanese-terrier-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 259 (valid standard dated 2016-04-04, English publication dated 2016-06-03). Covers Japanese origin (17th-century Dutch Smooth Fox Terrier imports to Nagasaki crossed with small pointers/native dogs; Kobe and Yokohama lapdogs; ~1920 planned breeding; ~1930 established type), Group 3 Section 2 Small-sized Terriers classification without working trial, companion-dog utilization, 1:1 square proportion, 1:1 skull-to-nasal-bridge ratio, thin tight lips, scissor bite, high-set V-shaped forward-drop or folded ears, traditionally docked or slightly curved natural tail, ultra-short ~2 mm smooth dense glossy coat (long coat disqualified), tricolour head with white spotted/marked body, and withers height (males and females approx. 30-33 cm). Omits weight.

fci-japanese-terrier-nomenclature.name: FCI - Nihon Teria (Japanese Terrier) Breed Nomenclature (No. 259)
fci-japanese-terrier-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Japan as country of origin, Group 3 Section 2 Small-sized Terriers classification without working trial, definitive acceptance date (1964-04-01), valid standard date (2016-04-04), English publication date (2016-06-03), and official multilingual names (Nihon Teria, Japanese Terrier, Terrier Japonais, Japanischer Terrier, Terrier Japonés).

jkc-japanese-terrier-breed-standard.name: Japan Kennel Club (JKC) - Japanese Terrier (日本テリア) Breed Standard
jkc-japanese-terrier-breed-standard.note: Official country-of-origin kennel club (Japan Kennel Club / JKC) breed standard page for Japanese Terrier (日本テリア, Standard No. 259) confirming Edo-era Nagasaki Dutch Smooth Fox Terrier origins, historic nicknames 'Oyuki Terrier' (お雪テリア) and 'Mikado Terrier' (ミカド・テリア) in Kobe and Yokohama, early Showa planned breeding, ~2 mm coat length, tricolour head and white spotted body, and withers height (both sexes approx. 30-33 cm).

akc-japanese-terrier-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Japanese Terrier Dog Breed Information
akc-japanese-terrier-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Foundation Stock Service, accepted October 2020) documenting only-terrier-from-Japan status, WWII and ~1948 near-extinction bottlenecks, height (10-13 inches), weight (10-12 lbs), life expectancy (13-15 years), reserved/independent/curious one-person character, alert watchdog barking, moderate exercise (walks/fenced yard plus couch companionship), minimal smooth-coat care, frequent nail trims, daily toothbrushing, and supervision with children and other dogs.

jtca-japanese-terrier-health.name: Japanese Terrier Club of America (JTCA) - Breed Health & Recommended Testing
jtca-japanese-terrier-health.note: Official US parent breed club health portal documenting owner-reported health concerns (minor to moderate food/environmental allergies, umbilical hernia, cataracts, and general small-breed luxating patella) and parent-club recommended screenings (PRA, OFA CAER eye exam, OFA Patellar Luxation) plus additional elective screenings (OFA Elbows and OFA Hips).

jtca-japanese-terrier-history.name: Japanese Terrier Club of America (JTCA) - Breed History
jtca-japanese-terrier-history.note: Official US parent breed club history portal documenting 1916 Nada/Hyogo foundation dog Kuro-Go (bred with Kobe Terriers), Osaka close breeding establishing the breed in the 1930s, 1980s near-extinction, FCI (1964) / UKC (2008) / AKC FSS (2020) milestones, and current global rarity (~50-80 puppies born and registered annually with JKC).

skk-nihon-teria-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Nihon teria Rasprofil
skk-nihon-teria-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for Nihon teria confirming Japanese companion-dog status, height (approx. 30-33 cm for both sexes), very easy-care short glossy coat, cold-weather sweater/coat recommendation, lively affectionate family nature, and note that very few Swedish individuals prevent reliable national health assessment.

scc-terrier-japonais-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Terrier japonais
scc-terrier-japonais-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile for Terrier japonais confirming height (30-33 cm), weight explicitly unspecified (NP), ~2 mm glossy coat, historic ladies' lapdog ('chiens de dames') role in Kobe and Yokohama, and lively, vigilant, affectionate temperament.

wikimedia-japanese-terrier-22-04-2012-2p.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Japanese Terrier 22.04.2012 2pl.jpg
wikimedia-japanese-terrier-22-04-2012-2p.note: High-resolution photograph (2012 x 2016 px) of Japanese Terrier 'Amakakeru-Meiji White Oleander' at a dog show in Konopiska, Poland, by Pleple2000 (EXIF capture date 2012-04-22 on Canon EOS 350D DIGITAL, uploaded 2012-05-07). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported (multi-licensed with 2.5/2.0/1.0 and GFDL) on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-nihon-teria-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Nihon teria aka Japanese Terrier.JPG
wikimedia-nihon-teria-canarian.note: Photograph (530 x 483 px) of an adult female Japanese Terrier by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2013-12-14 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2014-04-16). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-fila-brasileiro-official-standard.name: FCI - Fila Brasileiro Official Breed Standard No. 225
fci-fila-brasileiro-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 225 (valid standard dated 2016-09-29, English publication dated 2016-10-04, translated by Jennifer Mulholland and Raymond Triquet). Covers Brazilian origin, Group 2 Section 2.1 Mastiff-type Molossoids classification without working trial, watch-dog utilization, 15% rectangular proportion, trapezoid/pear head, wider-than-long teeth, dark-brown-to-yellow eyes, courage/loyalty/stranger aloofness with controlled handling, disqualifying faults (not walking at camel's pace, skin not loose and supple, croup lower than withers, cropped ears/docked tail), withers height (males 65-75 cm, females 60-70 cm), and minimum weights (males min 50 kg, females min 40 kg).

fci-fila-brasileiro-nomenclature.name: FCI - Fila Brasileiro Breed Nomenclature (No. 225)
fci-fila-brasileiro-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Brazil as country of origin, Group 2 Section 2.1 Mastiff-type Molossoids classification without working trial, definitive acceptance date (1960-01-01), valid standard date (2016-09-29), English publication date (2016-10-04), and official breed name (Fila Brasileiro).

cbkc-fila-brasileiro-official-standard.name: Confederação Brasileira de Cinofilia (CBKC) - Padrão Oficial da Raça Fila Brasileiro (FCI No. 225)
cbkc-fila-brasileiro-official-standard.note: Official country-of-origin Portuguese breed standard published by the Confederação Brasileira de Cinofilia (CBKC, updated 18 October 2016) confirming Brazil origin, guarding and cattle-herding role, 15% body-length excess, short/soft/dense close-lying coat, height (males 65-75 cm, females 60-70 cm), minimum weight (males 50 kg, females 40 kg), and disqualifying faults (absence of camel's pace, absence of loose skin, croup lower than withers, white/mouse-grey/dappled/black-and-tan/blue coats, cropped ears/docked tail, blue eyes, and dental faults).

skk-fila-brasileiro-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Fila brasileiro Rasprofil
skk-fila-brasileiro-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for Fila brasileiro confirming 16th-century Spanish/Portuguese origins (mastiff, bloodhound, Portuguese cattle dogs), 1946 first official standard, Brazilian proverb ('Trofast som en fila'), height (65-75 cm males, 60-70 cm females), minimum weight (50 kg males, 40 kg females), easy-care short coat, unsuitability for first-time owners, strong guarding instinct and stranger suspicion, and health note documenting hip dysplasia (HD) occurrence with no other known breed-bound diseases currently established in Sweden.

scc-fila-brasileiro-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Fila brasileiro
scc-fila-brasileiro-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile for Fila brasileiro confirming 16th-century colonial arrival and plantation history prior to slavery abolition, 1946 standard, height (60-75 cm), minimum weight (40 kg female, 50 kg male), intense family affection and stranger wariness, structured visitor management, unsuitability for urban apartments ('chien des champs'), and slow-growth mastiff nutritional demands.

uk-gov-dangerous-dogs-act-2026.name: UK Government (GOV.UK) - Dangerous Dogs Act 1991 Prohibited Dog Types (2026 Response)
uk-gov-dangerous-dogs-act-2026.note: Official UK Government publication (25 March 2026) confirming that Section 1 of the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991 prohibits the ownership, breeding, gifting, and sale of five designated dog types in the United Kingdom, including the Fila Brasileiro.

ofa-fila-brasileiro-hip-statistics.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals (OFA) - Hip Dysplasia Disease Statistics by Breed (Fila Brasileiro)
ofa-fila-brasileiro-hip-statistics.note: Official OFA breed-by-breed radiographic hip dysplasia statistics table recording 228 evaluated Fila Brasileiros: 67.5% graded normal and 32.5% graded dysplastic (19.7% mild, 9.6% moderate, 3.1% severe; screened registry cohort).

pmc-belerenian-2022-fila-brasileiro-acm.name: Left-dominant arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy in a Fila Brasileiro dog (PMC9473371)
pmc-belerenian-2022-fila-brasileiro-acm.note: Peer-reviewed veterinary cardiology case report by Belerenian, Donati, Rodríguez, Castillo, and Guevara (PMC9473371) documenting an isolated clinical and postmortem case of left-dominant arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy with myocardial fibroadipose replacement in a Fila Brasileiro dog.

pmc-brazilian-mastiff-mitogenomics-2026.name: Mitogenomic sequencing of the Brazilian Mastiff and Brazilian Terrier suggests a complex scenario of breed formation for two established Brazilian dog breeds (2026)
pmc-brazilian-mastiff-mitogenomics-2026.note: Peer-reviewed 2026 mitochondrial genomics study (PMID 42047518, PMC13123249) investigating the complex historical breed formation of Brazil's two FCI-recognized native breeds, the Brazilian Mastiff (Fila Brasileiro) and Brazilian Terrier.

wikimedia-brazilianmastifffila-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Brazilianmastifffila.jpg
wikimedia-brazilianmastifffila-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (2028 x 1859 px) of an adult fawn Fila Brasileiro (Brazilian Mastiff) by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2023-08-26 on Canon EOS 1100D, uploaded 2023-08-27). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-fila-brasileiro-ppk9-pleple200.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Fila brasileiro ppk9.jpg
wikimedia-fila-brasileiro-ppk9-pleple200.note: High-resolution photograph (1758 x 1782 px) of an adult brindle Fila Brasileiro ('Almodovar Rio Grande') at the Rybnik Dog Show 2006 by Pleple2000 (captured 2006-10-01, uploaded 2006-10-04). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported (multi-licensed with 2.5/2.0/1.0 and GFDL) on Wikimedia Commons.

cane-corso-ncl-ppt1-study-2017.name: Homozygous PPT1 Splice Donor Mutation in a Cane Corso Dog With Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis
cane-corso-ncl-ppt1-study-2017.note: Peer-reviewed study (Kolicheski et al., J Vet Intern Med 2017 Jan;31(1):149-157, Epub 2016-12-23, PMID 28008682, PMCID PMC5259623, DOI 10.1111/jvim.14632) identifying a homozygous PPT1 splice donor mutation (c.124+1G>A) causing CLN1-type Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis in a Cane Corso dog.
cane-corso-ncl-ppt1-study-2017.publisher: Journal of Veterinary Internal Medicine / PubMed

lagotto-romagnolo-lsd-atg4d-study-2015.name: A Missense Change in the ATG4D Gene Links Aberrant Autophagy to a Neurodegenerative Vacuolar Storage Disease (PLoS Genet 2015)
lagotto-romagnolo-lsd-atg4d-study-2015.note: Peer-reviewed study (Kyöstilä et al., PLoS Genet 2015 Apr 15;11(4):e1005169, PMID 25875846) identifying an autosomal recessive ATG4D missense variant (c.1288G>A; p.A430T) causing Lagotto Storage Disease in a cohort of >2,300 Lagotto Romagnolo dogs.

fci-field-spaniel-official-standard.name: FCI - Field Spaniel Official Breed Standard No. 123
fci-field-spaniel-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 123 (published 2026-10-06). Covers Great Britain origin, Group 8 Section 2 Flushing Dogs classification with working trial, rough-shooting / country-dweller utilization (not suitable for city), unusually docile/active/sensitive/independent temperament, noble chiselled head, dark hazel almond eyes, low-set feathered ears, ribcage 2/3 body length, low-set tail (natural to hocks or previously docked 1/3), long flat glossy silky weatherproof coat (clean hock to ground), eight accepted colours (black, black & tan, blue roan, blue roan & tan, liver, liver & tan, liver roan, liver roan & tan; white/roan on chest acceptable in solids), withers height (approx. 46 cm for both sexes), and weight (18-25 kg for both sexes).

fci-field-spaniel-nomenclature.name: FCI - Field Spaniel Breed Nomenclature (No. 123)
fci-field-spaniel-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Great Britain as country of origin, Group 8 Section 2 Flushing Dogs classification with working trial, definitive acceptance date (1954-12-27), valid standard publication date (2026-10-06), and official breed name (Field Spaniel).

rkc-spaniel-field-breed-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Spaniel (Field) Breed Standard
rkc-spaniel-field-breed-standard.note: Official country-of-origin Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Gundog Group, updated August 1, 2025) for Spaniel (Field) establishing conformation, temperament, coat texture, and accepted colours.

rkc-spaniel-field-breed-profile.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Spaniel (Field) Breeds A to Z
rkc-spaniel-field-breed-profile.note: Official Royal Kennel Club Breeds A to Z profile confirming Vulnerable Native Breed status, country lifestyle, medium size, more than 2 hours daily exercise, grooming more than once weekly, shedding, eight accepted colours, Breed Watch Category 1 status, and Best Practice health tests (BVA/KC Elbow Dysplasia, BVA/KC/ISDS Eye Scheme, and BVA/KC Hip Dysplasia).

akc-field-spaniel-official-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Field Spaniel
akc-field-spaniel-official-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Sporting Group; approved April 6, 2020, effective June 30, 2020). Establishes 7:6 length-to-height proportion, ideal height (18 inches dogs, 17 inches bitches, +/- 1 inch acceptable), single water-repellent glossy coat, close-fitting clean non-pendulous lips, scissor or level bite (scissor preferred), large rounded webbed feet, and docked or natural low-set tail.

akc-field-spaniel-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Field Spaniel Dog Breed Information
akc-field-spaniel-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile documenting sweet/fun-loving/sensitive 'thinking dog' temperament, Phineas Bullock history, height (18 in male, 17 in female), weight (35-50 pounds), life expectancy (12-13 years), 'Food Spaniels' food motivation, weekly brushing (no body clipping), ear checks, frequent toothbrushing, and breeding-stock testing across orthopaedics, thyroid, eyes, cardiac, and late-onset seizures.

akc-field-spaniel-history-2022.name: American Kennel Club - Field Spaniel History: A Type Brought Back From Extinction (2022)
akc-field-spaniel-history-2022.note: Published AKC historical feature (May 9, 2022) documenting the 1900 25-pound weight division between Cockers and Fields ('before breakfast a Cocker, after breakfast a Field'), the late-1800s 'cucumber or caterpillar' exaggeration era, and the mid-20th-century rescue of the breed.

fssa-field-spaniel-health.name: Field Spaniel Society of America (FSSA) - Health & CHIC Overview
fssa-field-spaniel-health.note: Official US parent breed club health overview confirming typical lifespan (11-15 years), close genetic relatedness due to rarity, 2003 FSSA health survey (446 dogs), CHIC database participation (eyes, hips, thyroid), and ongoing Data Collection for Late Onset Seizure Disorder.

fssa-field-spaniel-health-issues.name: Field Spaniel Society of America (FSSA) - Health Issues in Field Spaniels
fssa-field-spaniel-health-issues.note: Official FSSA health monograph detailing polygenic hip dysplasia (OFA/PennHIP), fairly common hypothyroidism (and possible autoimmune link with anemia/sterility), eye issues (retinal folds, ectropion, entropion, very rare PRA), heart defects, and suspected polygenic epilepsy.

fssa-health-committee-2023-cardiac.name: Field Spaniel Society of America (FSSA) - Health Committee Update: Advanced Cardiac CHIC Requirement (2023)
fssa-health-committee-2023-cardiac.note: Official FSSA Health Committee announcement (September 14, 2023) elevating the Field Spaniel CHIC cardiac clearance requirement to Advanced Cardiac (cardiologist echocardiogram) to detect subtle heart murmurs missed by basic auscultation.

skk-field-spaniel-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Field spaniel Rasprofil
skk-field-spaniel-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for Field spaniel confirming height (~46 cm), weight (18-25 kg), solid liver as most common colour, slow physical and mental maturation (females 2-3 years, males ~4 years), monthly paw/inner-ear trimming, peaceful yet mildly stubborn dignified character (rarely barks; reserved with strangers, never shy), 1950s English Springer Spaniel outcross revival, and hip dysplasia (HD) occurrence.

scc-field-spaniel-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Field spaniel
scc-field-spaniel-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile confirming height (~46 cm), weight (18-25 kg), gentle sensitive owner-oriented character, unsuitability for apartment living (requiring a garden and generous exercise), and historic crosses with Sussex, Basset, and English Springer Spaniels.

pmc-syrja-2025-field-spaniel-cesd-lal.name: Cholesterol Ester Storage Disease in Two Field Spaniels With Lysosomal Acid Lipase Deficiency (JVIM 2025)
pmc-syrja-2025-field-spaniel-cesd-lal.note: Peer-reviewed University of Helsinki clinical, enzymatic, and lipidomic case report by Syrjä, Ylenius, Kråkström, Dickens, Rautala, Huupponen, Eriksson, and Viitanen (J Vet Intern Med 2025 Sep-Oct;39(5):e70223, PMID 40859629, PMC12380722) documenting Lysosomal Acid Lipase (LAL) deficiency causing Cholesterol Ester Storage Disease (CESD) in two unrelated Field Spaniels.
pmc-syrja-2025-field-spaniel-cesd-lal.publisher: Journal of Veterinary Internal Medicine / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-robinson-1996-field-spaniel-coat-col.name: Inheritance of coat colour in the field spaniel dog (Genetics Selection Evolution 1996)
pmc-robinson-1996-field-spaniel-coat-col.note: Peer-reviewed genetics paper by Roy Robinson (Genet Sel Evol 1996 Sep 15;28(3):285-288, PMC2708312) analyzing the Mendelian inheritance of black, liver, tan-point, and roan coat colours in the Field Spaniel.
pmc-robinson-1996-field-spaniel-coat-col.publisher: Genetics Selection Evolution / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

wikimedia-field-liver1-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Field-liver1.jpg
wikimedia-field-liver1-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (1790 x 1504 px) of an adult solid liver Field Spaniel outdoors by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2021-07-31 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2021-07-31). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.
