wikimedia-field-liverwhite1-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (1527 x 1377 px) of an adult liver-roan Field Spaniel standing outdoors in profile by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2021-07-31, uploaded 2021-07-31). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

the-kennel-club-slovakian-rough-haired-p.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Slovakian Rough Haired Pointer (Imp) Breed Standard
the-kennel-club-slovakian-rough-haired-p.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Gundog Group, updated 2025-04-01) covering general appearance, versatile field/forest/water characteristics, double coat (~4 cm harsh outer coat, summer-shedding undercoat), amber adult / blue young eyes, and tail carriage.

fci-pumi-official-standard.name: FCI - Pumi Official Breed Standard No. 56
fci-pumi-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 56 (valid standard dated 2000-04-06, English publication dated 2000-09-13, translated by Mrs. C. Seidler and Mrs. Elke Peper). Covers Hungarian origin (17th–18th century primitive Puli crossed with imported German and French prick-eared terrier-type dogs; independent breed since early 20th century), Group 1 Section 1 Sheepdogs classification without working trial, apartment-capable active family/sport dog utilization, 1:1 square proportions, 50-55° neck angle (45% of height), 55° shoulder layback (100-110° angle), terrier-like narrow head, barely visible stop, always-black nose, tight lips, reverse-V ears tipped forward in upper third, wide-circle tail (7-12 cm wiry underside hair; docking/bobtail banned), curly 4-7 cm solid coat (grey born black, black, fawn/fakó, white), withers height (dogs 41-47 cm, ideal 43-45 cm; bitches 38-44 cm, ideal 40-42 cm), and weight (dogs 10-15 kg, ideal 12-13 kg; bitches 8-13 kg, ideal 10-11 kg).

fci-pumi-nomenclature.name: FCI - Pumi Breed Nomenclature (No. 56)
fci-pumi-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Hungary as country of origin, Group 1 Section 1 Sheepdogs classification without working trial, definitive acceptance date (1954-08-11), valid standard date (2000-04-06), English publication date (2000-09-13), four colour varieties (grey, black, fawn/fakó, white), and official breed name (Pumi).

akc-pumi-official-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Pumi
akc-pumi-official-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Herding Group, eligible July 1, 2016) establishing medium alert agile Hungarian herding conformation, ideal weight (dogs 27-29 pounds, bitches 22-24 pounds), height limits (disqualification >1/2 inch beyond range), corkscrew-curled coat, and semi-erect tipped ears.

akc-pumi-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Pumi Dog Breed Information
akc-pumi-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile documenting 1815 first printed mention of 'Pumi', 1972 first Finnish imports (most popular Hungarian herding dog in Finland), July 1, 2016 AKC Herding Group entry, life expectancy (12-13 years), 50/50 soft-and-harsh coat composition, combing every 3-6 weeks followed by wetting and air-drying (no blow-dryer), non-shedding indoor coat, bark management, fetch/agility/obedience aptitude, and health screening for hips, elbows, patellas, DM, and eyes.

rkc-hungarian-pumi-breed-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Hungarian Pumi Breed Standard
rkc-hungarian-pumi-breed-standard.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Pastoral Group, updated April 1, 2025) under the UK designation 'Hungarian Pumi', covering conformation, terrier-like herding character, and coat.

rkc-hungarian-pumi-breed-profile.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Hungarian Pumi Breeds A to Z
rkc-hungarian-pumi-breed-profile.note: Official Royal Kennel Club Breeds A to Z profile confirming 1960 modern standard milestone, small house and small/medium garden suitability, weekly grooming, Sheds No, lifespan over 12 years, Breed Watch Category 1 status, and Good Practice pre-breeding tests (BVA/KC Elbow Dysplasia Scheme and BVA/KC Hip Dysplasia Scheme).

kennelliitto-pumi-breed-profile.name: Suomen Kennelliitto - Pumi Rotuesittely ja PEVISA
kennelliitto-pumi-breed-profile.note: Official Finnish Kennel Club (Suomen Kennelliitto) breed profile confirming height (41-47 cm males, 38-44 cm females), weight (10-15 kg males, 8-13 kg females), average lifespan (12-15 years), urban/apartment adaptability despite barkiness, weekly combing and continuous scissor-trimmed coat growth, mandatory PEVISA hip radiographs and eye exams (<=36 months old at mating), plus club recommendations for knees (patellar luxation and cruciate ligament care), elbows, spine, and PLL DNA testing.

skk-pumi-breed-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Pumi Rasprofil
skk-pumi-breed-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for Pumi confirming height (41-47 cm males, 38-44 cm females), weight (10-15 kg males, 8-13 kg females), koala-like face, 4-7 cm dirt-repelling non-shedding curly coat requiring periodic combing and trimming, calm indoor behaviour with vocal herding bark, stranger reserve, and generally healthy status with hip dysplasia (HD) occurring.

scc-pumi-breed-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Pumi
scc-pumi-breed-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile for Pumi confirming height (41-47 cm males, 38-44 cm females), weight (10-15 kg males, 8-13 kg females), black-born grey colour transition, hand-grooming, affectionate yet stranger-wary watchdog character, and apartment adaptability with ample exercise.

hpca-pumi-health.name: Hungarian Pumi Club of America (HPCA) - Pumi Health & CHIC Requirements
hpca-pumi-health.note: Official US parent breed club health portal detailing OFA/CHIC required pre-breeding screenings (Hip Dysplasia X-ray, Patellar Luxation certification, Primary Lens Luxation DNA test citing Scandinavian cases, and Degenerative Myelopathy DNA test) alongside optional ACVO eye exam, elbow dysplasia X-ray, DNA repository, and rule against breeding two carriers together.

pmc-sod1-dm-allele-frequencies-8304418.name: Allele and genotype frequencies of the SOD1 gene polymorphism associated with canine degenerative myelopathy across breeds (PMC8304418)
pmc-sod1-dm-allele-frequencies-8304418.note: Peer-reviewed veterinary genetics compilation (PMID 34316194, PMC8304418) reporting SOD1:c.118G>A Degenerative Myelopathy genotype and allele frequencies in the Pumi (0.88 G/G clear, 0.13 G/A heterozygous carriers, 0.00 A/A homozygotes; mutant A allele frequency 0.06).

wikimedia-pumi-grey-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Pumi grey.jpg
wikimedia-pumi-grey-canarian.note: Photograph (600 x 522 px) of an adult grey female Pumi by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2016-11-13 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2016-11-14). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-pumi-agility-frantsei-ble.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Pumi-agility.jpg
wikimedia-pumi-agility-frantsei-ble.note: High-resolution photograph (5743 x 3829 px) of a Pumi clearing an agility jump by Frantseï Blè (EXIF capture date 2019-11-20 on Canon EOS M50, uploaded to Wikimedia Commons 2020-11-19). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

akc-thai-bangkaew-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Thai Bangkaew Dog Breed Information
akc-thai-bangkaew-breed-profile.note: Official AKC Foundation Stock Service breed profile (accepted July 2023) covering height (18-21 in / 16-19 in), weight (40-43 lb / 35-40 lb), life expectancy (14-17 years), 1983 'Bang Kaew Khuen Thin' revival by Dr. Nisit Tangtrakarnpong, grooming tools (avoid bladed deshedders), moderate exercise, gentle training, and health priorities (early-onset eye conditions/PRA and precautionary hip testing).

thai-bangkaew-erg-study-2015.name: Normal clinical electroretinography parameters for poodle, Labrador retriever, Thai ridgeback, and Thai Bangkaew (J Vet Sci 2015)
thai-bangkaew-erg-study-2015.note: Peer-reviewed study (J Vet Sci 2015;16(1):67-74, Epub 2014-09-30, PMID 25269713, PMCID PMC4367151, DOI 10.4142/jvs.2015.16.1.67) documenting distinct normal electroretinography (ERG) implicit times in Thai Bangkaew Dogs.

akc-rat-terrier-official-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Rat Terrier
akc-rat-terrier-official-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Terrier Group; approved November 11, 2009, effective July 1, 2010). Establishes two size divisions at the withers (Miniature 10 to 13 inches; Standard over 13 up to 18 inches; <10 in or >18 in over 6 months disqualified), body depth equal to elbow-to-ground height, smooth blunt wedge head, clean tight lips, scissor preferred / level bite acceptable, erect / semi-erect tipped / button ears (cropped disqualified), docked / natural bobtail / natural long tail, short smooth shiny coat with intact whiskers (kink, curl, or genetic hairlessness disqualified), pied patterning (solid non-white, <1 in white, brindle, and merle disqualified), and non-sparring, devoted, easily trained temperament.

akc-rat-terrier-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Rat Terrier Dog Breed Information
akc-rat-terrier-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile documenting 19th-century US farm-ratting origins, 2013 AKC Terrier Group recognition, height (10-13 in miniature, 13-18 in standard), weight (10-25 pounds), life expectancy (12-18 years), friendly/inquisitive/lovable temperament, occasional barking, moderate shedding, lure coursing and agility aptitude, and national breed club recommended health tests (Patella Evaluation, Hip Evaluation, Cardiac Exam, and Primary Lens Luxation DNA Test).

rtca-about-the-rat-terrier.name: Rat Terrier Club of America (RTCA) - About the Rat Terrier
rtca-about-the-rat-terrier.note: Official AKC parent breed club overview confirming US origin, Theodore Roosevelt naming legend, two size divisions (10-13 in miniature, 13-18 in standard), weight (10-25 pounds), life expectancy (12-18 years), and compact, portable companion nature.

rtca-health-and-genetics.name: Rat Terrier Club of America (RTCA) - Health & Genetics
rtca-health-and-genetics.note: Official parent breed club health and genetics portal detailing OFA Rat Terrier CHIC program requirements, breed-specific owner/breeder health survey links, and OFA Rat Terrier health testing statistics.

rtca-find-a-rat-terrier.name: Rat Terrier Club of America (RTCA) - Finding a Rat Terrier & Pre-Breeding Health Screening
rtca-find-a-rat-terrier.note: Official RTCA buyer guide and Health & Genetics Committee summary detailing consistent puppy obedience, public socialization, breeding age >=2 years, genetic carrier testing, OFA hips and elbows X-rays, patellar luxation checks, veterinary ophthalmologist eye exams, and cardiac evaluations (noting cardiologist exams are preferred due to reported heart issues in the breed).

ofa-rat-terrier-chic-requirements.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals (OFA) - Rat Terrier CHIC Program
ofa-rat-terrier-chic-requirements.note: Official OFA Canine Health Information Center (CHIC) breed screening registry page for the Rat Terrier (code RT), maintained jointly with the Rat Terrier Club of America.

ofa-primary-lens-luxation.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals (OFA) - Primary Lens Luxation (PLL) DNA Testing
ofa-primary-lens-luxation.note: Official OFA veterinary genetics resource (with University of Missouri-Columbia College of Veterinary Medicine) explaining Primary Lens Luxation (zonular ligament weakness, secondary uveitis and glaucoma, typical clinical onset 4-8 years) and cheek-swab DNA screening for affected terrier breeds including the Rat Terrier.

pubmed-pettigrew-2007-rat-terrier-tpo-ch.name: CNS hypomyelination in Rat Terrier dogs with congenital goiter and a mutation in the thyroid peroxidase gene (Veterinary Pathology 2007)
pubmed-pettigrew-2007-rat-terrier-tpo-ch.note: Peer-reviewed study by Pettigrew, Fyfe, Gregory, Lipsitz, de Lahunta, Summers, and Shelton (Vet Pathol 2007 Jan;44(1):50-56, PMID 17197623) documenting central nervous system hypomyelination and congenital goiter in Rat Terrier dogs caused by a mutation in the thyroid peroxidase (TPO) gene shared with Toy Fox Terriers.

omia-canine-congenital-hypothyroidism-tp.name: OMIA (Online Mendelian Inheritance in Animals) - Congenital Hypothyroidism with Goiter (TPO) in Canis lupus familiaris (OMIA 000536-9615)
omia-canine-congenital-hypothyroidism-tp.note: Curated veterinary genetics database entry (OMIA000536/9615, edited by Dr. John C. Fyfe) confirming the autosomal-recessive TPO nonsense mutation (c.331C>T; p.Arg111Ter) on CFA17 causing Congenital Hypothyroidism with Goiter (CHG) in Rat Terriers and Toy Fox Terriers and documenting DNA test availability.
omia-canine-congenital-hypothyroidism-tp.publisher: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Animals (University of Sydney)

wikimedia-amberina-the-rat-terrier-jaden.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Amberina the Rat Terrier.jpg
wikimedia-amberina-the-rat-terrier-jaden.note: High-resolution photograph (3070 x 2456 px) of an adult Rat Terrier with a natural undocked tail by Jadenschaul (captured 2020-10-19, uploaded 2024-08-31). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-rat-terrier-bree-bailey.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Rat Terrier.jpg
wikimedia-rat-terrier-bree-bailey.note: High-resolution photograph (1280 x 960 px) of an adult male Rat Terrier by Flickr user Bree Bailey (EXIF capture date 2006-09-28 on Fujifilm FinePix S602 Zoom, uploaded to Wikimedia Commons by Pharaoh Hound on 2007-02-19, license reviewed by FlickreviewR on 2007-04-08). Licensed under CC BY-SA 2.0 Generic.

fci-pudelpointer-official-standard.name: FCI - Pudelpointer Official Breed Standard No. 216
fci-pudelpointer-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 216 (valid standard dated 2004-11-09, English publication dated 2004-12-06). Covers German origin (strictly from Poodle and English Pointer crosses without other pointing breeds), Group 7 Section 1.1 Continental Pointing Dogs ('Braque' type) classification with working trial, balanced calm self-controlled temperament free of game or gun shyness, heavy-Pointer conformation, large dark amber eyes, medium high-set close-lying rounded drop ears, hard flat medium-length coat with dense undercoat and facial furnishings, solid brown / dead-leaf / black colours with small white marks permitted, and withers height (males 60-68 cm, females 55-63 cm). Omits weight.

fci-pudelpointer-nomenclature.name: FCI - Pudelpointer Breed Nomenclature (No. 216)
fci-pudelpointer-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Germany as country of origin, Group 7 Section 1.1 Continental Pointing Dogs ('Braque' type) classification with working trial, definitive acceptance date (1959-11-13), valid standard date (2004-11-09), English publication date (2004-12-06), and official multilingual name (Pudelpointer).

vpp-pudelpointer-zuchtordnung.name: Verein Pudelpointer e.V. (VPP) - Zuchtordnung & Rassestandard
vpp-pudelpointer-zuchtordnung.note: Official German parent breed club (Verein Pudelpointer e.V., founded 1897; VDH/JGHV/FCI member) breeding regulations effective 7 October 2022. Specifies conformation (nearly square dry muscular build; males 60-68 cm, females 55-63 cm; 4-6 cm hard flat coat at withers with dense undercoat and belly cover; beard, eyebrows, forelock; solid dark/medium brown, dead-leaf/dürrlaubfarben, or black), abbreviation 'PP', mandatory hunting tests (VJP, HZP/VGP), mandatory pre-breeding DNA registration, HD, ED, and OCD radiographic findings, and strict breeding exclusions for ED, OCD, epilepsy, chronic skin diseases, entropion/ectropion of any degree, hairless eyelids, dental abnormalities, and cryptorchidism.

akc-pudelpointer-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Pudelpointer Dog Breed Information
akc-pudelpointer-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Foundation Stock Service) documenting calm/self-controlled versatile gun-dog character, height (22-26 inches), weight (45-70 pounds), life expectancy (14 years), moderate seasonal shedding, eager-to-please trainability, occasional barking, strong love of water, weekly grooming, nail/ear/dental care, and overall healthy breed profile.

ckc-pudelpointer-profile.name: Canadian Kennel Club (CKC) - Pudelpointer Breed Profile
ckc-pudelpointer-profile.note: Official Canadian Kennel Club (Sporting Dogs Group) breed profile documenting Sigismund Freiherr von Zedlitz und Neukirch's 1881 foundation litter (black Poodle 'Molly' x Pointer 'Tell' owned by future Emperor Friedrich III), height (males 24-27 in / 60-68 cm; females 22-25 in / 55-63 cm), medium-long dense hard coat with woolly undercoat, eyebrows and whiskered muzzle, dark liver / autumn-leaves / black colours, weekly brushing, and hand-stripping.

skk-pudelpointer-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Pudelpointer Rasprofil
skk-pudelpointer-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for Pudelpointer confirming German origin, height (60-68 cm males, 55-63 cm females), easy-care weather-and-injury-protective harsh double coat, calm balanced temperament with strong hunting drive requiring abundant exercise and hunting-ground access (unsuitable solely as a companion pet), and note that very small numbers in Sweden prevent statistical national health assessment.

scc-pudelpointer-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Pudelpointer
scc-pudelpointer-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile confirming height (60-68 cm males, 55-63 cm females), weight explicitly unspecified (NP), Poodle-and-Pointer foundation without other pointing breeds, calm balanced fearless temperament, and unsuitability for city living.

navhda-bodo-winterhelt-2018.name: NAVHDA - Sigbot 'Bodo' Winterhelt Tribute (Versatile Hunting Dog, July 2018)
navhda-bodo-winterhelt-2018.note: Official North American Versatile Hunting Dog Association (NAVHDA) biographical tribute (July 2018) documenting Sigbot 'Bodo' Winterhelt's 1956 introduction of North America's first Pudelpointer ('Cati v. Waldhof') and his co-founding role in establishing North American versatile hunting dog testing.
navhda-bodo-winterhelt-2018.publisher: North American Versatile Hunting Dog Association

wikimedia-pudelpointer-brown1-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Pudelpointer-brown1.jpg
wikimedia-pudelpointer-brown1-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (1547 x 1437 px) of an adult brown/liver Pudelpointer by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2023-04-22 on Canon EOS 1100D, uploaded 2023-04-23). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-pudelpointer-2-sciencia58.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Pudelpointer 2.jpg
wikimedia-pudelpointer-2-sciencia58.note: High-resolution photograph (3523 x 3312 px) of an adult Pudelpointer outdoors by Sciencia58 (inception date 2020-11-16, uploaded 2021-03-17). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

belgian-shepherd-gastric-carcinoma-study.name: Gastric mucosal pathology in Belgian Shepherd dogs with and without clinical signs of gastric disease (Acta Vet Scand 2021)
belgian-shepherd-gastric-carcinoma-study.note: Peer-reviewed study (Candido et al., Acta Vet Scand 2021 Feb 9;63(1):7, PMID 33563310, DOI 10.1186/s13028-021-00570-6) documenting breed predisposition to gastric carcinoma in Belgian Shepherd Tervuren and Groenendael varieties and recommending timely endoscopy for persistent vomiting.

fci-miniature-pinscher-official-standard.name: FCI - Miniature Pinscher (Zwergpinscher) Official Breed Standard No. 185
fci-miniature-pinscher-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 185 (valid standard dated 2007-03-06, English publication dated 2007-04-18). Covers German origin, 1925 Stud Book (1,300 entries), Group 2 Section 1.1 Pinscher classification without working trial, square proportions, head length equal to half topline, flat wrinkle-free forehead, 42-tooth scissor bite, tight black lips, prick or high-set V-shaped drop ears, dry dewlap-free neck, 50° shoulder layback (95-100° shoulder-upper arm angle), natural sabre/sickle tail, cat feet, short dense smooth glossy coat, self-coloured deer-red and black-and-tan coloration, withers height (dogs and bitches 25-30 cm), and weight (dogs and bitches 4-6 kg).

fci-miniature-pinscher-nomenclature.name: FCI - Zwergpinscher (Miniature Pinscher) Breed Nomenclature (No. 185)
fci-miniature-pinscher-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Germany as country of origin, Group 2 Section 1.1 Pinscher classification without working trial, standard publication date (2007-04-18), two FCI colour groups (self-coloured deer red to dark red-brown, and black and tan), and official multilingual names (Zwergpinscher, Miniature Pinscher, Pinscher Nain).

rkc-miniature-pinscher-breed-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Miniature Pinscher Breed Standard
rkc-miniature-pinscher-breed-standard.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Toy Group, updated August 1, 2025) confirming fearless animated self-possessed temperament, precise hackney gait, complete scissor bite, cat-like feet, smooth hard lustrous coat, accepted UK colours (black, blue, or chocolate with tan markings, plus solid red), and height at withers (25-30 cm / 10-12 in).

rkc-miniature-pinscher-breed-profile.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Miniature Pinscher Breeds A to Z
rkc-miniature-pinscher-breed-profile.note: Official Royal Kennel Club Breeds A to Z profile confirming 1895 first German breed club, 1950s UK arrival, USA/UK hackney gait development differing from German standard, flat/apartment and small/medium garden suitability, up to 30 minutes daily baseline exercise, weekly grooming, Sheds Yes, lifespan over 12 years, Breed Watch Category 1 status, and Best Practice Eye Scheme testing (including litter screening).

akc-miniature-pinscher-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Miniature Pinscher Dog Breed Information
akc-miniature-pinscher-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Toy Group) documenting 'King of Toys' nickname, 1929 Miniature Pinscher Club of America founding, US height (10-12.5 inches), US weight (8-10 pounds), life expectancy (12-16 years), and breed health concerns including patellar luxation, cervical (dry) disc disease, Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease, and epilepsy.

akc-miniature-pinscher-history-2025.name: American Kennel Club - Miniature Pinscher History: From Vermin Catcher to the 'King of Toys' (2025)
akc-miniature-pinscher-history-2025.note: Published AKC historical article (April 17, 2025) documenting the Miniature Pinscher's barnyard vermin-catching heritage, high-stepping hackney gait, 'King of Toys' status, and 1929 Miniature Pinscher Club of America organization.

skk-dvargpinscher-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Dvärgpinscher Rasprofil
skk-dvargpinscher-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for Dvärgpinscher confirming German origin (1925 Stud Book with 1,300 entries), height (25-30 cm), weight (4-6 kg), easy-care short smooth coat, cheerful active temperament (enjoys tracking and burrowing under blankets), strong personal integrity, need for friendly firm early boundaries and alone-time training, and health status noting eye diseases and patellar luxation occur.

scc-pinscher-nain-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Pinscher nain
scc-pinscher-nain-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile for Pinscher nain confirming height (25-30 cm), weight (4-6 kg), historic Bavaria and Württemberg coach-house rat-hunting heritage, non-submissive character requiring calm firmness without brutality, easy apartment adaptation, and strict on-leash city walking advice.

pubmed-penngen-2020-minpin-mps6-arsb.name: ARSB gene variants causing Mucopolysaccharidosis VI in Miniature Pinscher and Miniature Schnauzer dogs (Animal Genetics 2020)
pubmed-penngen-2020-minpin-mps6-arsb.note: Peer-reviewed PennGen (University of Pennsylvania) study (Anim Genet 2020 Dec;51(6):982-986, Epub 2020-09-28, PMID 32985704, PMC8008615) identifying an autosomal-recessive exon 5 missense variant in ARSB (NM_001048133.1:c.910G>A; p.Gly304Arg) causing arylsulfatase B deficiency / Mucopolysaccharidosis VI in Miniature Pinschers.

pmc-brons-2013-minpin-slc7a9-cystinuria.name: SLC3A1 and SLC7A9 Mutations in Autosomal Recessive or Autosomal Dominant Canine Cystinuria: A New Classification System (JVIM 2013)
pmc-brons-2013-minpin-slc7a9-cystinuria.note: Peer-reviewed study (J Vet Intern Med, PMC3946761) identifying an exon 9 missense variant in SLC7A9 (c.964G>A; p.Gly322Arg) associated with autosomal-dominant cystinuria and urinary cystine stone formation in a 4-generation European Miniature Pinscher family.
pmc-brons-2013-minpin-slc7a9-cystinuria.publisher: Journal of Veterinary Internal Medicine / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-mcmillan-2024-uk-dog-longevity.name: Longevity of companion dog breeds: those at risk from early death (Scientific Reports 2024)
pmc-mcmillan-2024-uk-dog-longevity.note: Peer-reviewed UK survival analysis by McMillan, Bielby, Williams, Upjohn, Casey, and Christley (Sci Rep 2024 Feb 1;14(1), PMC10834484) reporting a median life expectancy of 13.7 years for Miniature Pinschers compared with 12.7 years for purebred dogs overall and 12.0 years for crossbreeds.
pmc-mcmillan-2024-uk-dog-longevity.publisher: Scientific Reports / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

wikimedia-zwergpinscher-denzo-kpt-vernun.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Zwergpinscher.Denzo-vom-Reichsgraf-zu-Herrenheim 1500X1500.jpg
wikimedia-zwergpinscher-denzo-kpt-vernun.note: High-resolution photograph (1500 x 1500 px) of an adult black-and-tan male Miniature Pinscher ('Denzo vom Reichsgraf zu Herrenheim', 4.1 kg, natural ears and tail) by Kpt vernunft (uploaded 2006-07-14). wikimedia-miniature-pinscher-sebastian-w.note: Photograph (800 x 532 px) of a Miniature Pinscher with natural drop ears by Sebastian Wallin / Sebwal (captured 2007-02-18, uploaded 2009-03-31). Licensed under CC BY 3.0 Unported (and GFDL) on Wikimedia Commons.

ofa-cddy-ivdd.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals - Chondrodystrophy with Intervertebral Disc Disease (CDDY/IVDD)
ofa-cddy-ivdd.note: OFA genetic disease overview documenting the CFA12 FGF4 retrogene (12-FGF4R) responsible for chondrodystrophy and intervertebral disc disease (IVDD) in affected breeds including the Pekingese, citing Brown et al. (2017) and Batcher et al. (2019).

pmc-vetcompass-corneal-ulceration-2017.name: Corneal ulcerative disease in dogs under primary veterinary care in England (VetCompass)
pmc-vetcompass-corneal-ulceration-2017.note: Peer-reviewed VetCompass primary-care veterinary study documenting elevated predisposition to corneal ulcerative disease in brachycephalic breeds including the Pekingese.

fci-ariege-pointer-official-standard.name: FCI - Braque de l'Ariège (Ariege Pointing Dog) Official Breed Standard No. 177
fci-ariege-pointer-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 177 (valid standard dated 2023-08-10, English publication dated 2023-09-15). Covers French origin (descended from old French Braques, World Wars decline, 1990 breeder revival), Group 7 Section 1.1 Continental Pointing Dogs ('Braque' type) classification with working trial, stable and sociable temperament with humans and other dogs, braccoid lean muscular build, divergent cranial axes, orange-to-pale-brown nose (never black), fine non-droopy lips, scissor bite (pincer and max 2 PM1 or 1 PM2/PM3 tolerated; >1 mm gap disqualified), amber/brown eyes, fine long curled-in drop ears at eye level, slight neck dewlap, horizontal tail (6/10 docked or natural long), short thick glossy white coat with pale-to-vivid orangy fawn or light brown patches/ticking (black spots disqualified), and withers height (males 58-65 cm, preferred 61 cm; females 54-63 cm, preferred 59 cm; +/- 2 cm tolerance). Omits weight.

fci-ariege-pointer-nomenclature.name: FCI - Braque de l'Ariège (Ariege Pointing Dog) Breed Nomenclature (No. 177)
fci-ariege-pointer-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming France as country of origin, Group 7 Section 1.1 Continental Pointing Dogs ('Braque' type) classification with working trial, definitive acceptance date (1955-06-28), valid standard date (2023-08-10), English publication date (2023-09-15), and official multilingual names (Braque de l'Ariège, Ariege Pointing Dog, Ariège-Vorstehhund, Braco del Ariège).

scc-braque-de-l-ariege-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Braque de l'Ariège
scc-braque-de-l-ariege-profile.note: Official country-of-origin French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile confirming 19th-century crosses of old Braque Français with white-and-orange southern pointers for lightness and liveliness, Ariège hunters' preservation, 1990 rescue effort, short glossy ticked white-and-orange/brown coat, and weight (25 to 30 kg).

scc-braque-de-l-ariege-dossier.name: Société Centrale Canine / Union Mondiale des Braques de Race Française - Le Braque de l'Ariège
scc-braque-de-l-ariege-dossier.note: Official SCC / Union Mondiale des Braques de Race Française historical and working dossier (published 2020-02-16, updated 2020-09-24) documenting the 1964–1990 LOF registration hiatus, the 1990 Toulouse revival meeting (MM. Desmolles, Maestripieri, Nau, Bartolozzi, Abadie, and Séguéla), the first two Initial-Title LOF puppies since 1964, the 1990 founding of the Club du Braque de l'Ariège, the 1991 SCC breeding plan, specialization in partridge and quail hunting, and daily exercise and firm education requirements.

scc-club-du-braque-de-l-ariege.name: Club du Braque de l'Ariège (SCC) - Club Officiel de Race
scc-club-du-braque-de-l-ariege.note: Official French parent breed club portal (Club du Braque de l'Ariège, affiliated with the Société Centrale Canine) overseeing breed preservation, litters, field trials, and breeding standards in France.

wikimedia-ariegepointerbraque1-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Ariegepointerbraque1.jpg
wikimedia-ariegepointerbraque1-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (2395 x 2134 px) of an adult Ariège Pointer outdoors by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2023-08-25 on Canon EOS 1100D, uploaded 2023-08-25). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-ariege-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (1316 x 1206 px) of an adult orange-and-white male Ariège Pointer outdoors by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2020-01-25 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2020-01-27). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

ofa-legg-calve-perthes.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals - Legg-Calve-Perthes Disease
ofa-legg-calve-perthes.note: OFA veterinary disease overview of Legg-Calve-Perthes disease (avascular necrosis of the femoral head) in miniature and toy breeds.

pmc-affenpinscher-craniometric-2017.name: Craniometric Analysis of the Hindbrain and Craniocervical Junction in Toy Breeds (PMC)
pmc-affenpinscher-craniometric-2017.note: Peer-reviewed craniometric study including the Affenpinscher evaluating brachycephalic cranial conformation and risk factors for Chiari-like malformation and syringomyelia.

wikimedia-an-affenpinscher-lori-branham.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:An Affenpinscher.jpg
wikimedia-an-affenpinscher-lori-branham.note: High-resolution photograph (3318 x 2212 px) of a black Affenpinscher by Lori Branham (captured 2009-02-10, uploaded via Flickr upload bot 2014-03-02). Licensed under CC BY 2.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-affenpinscher-breed-futurebrea.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Affenpinscher breed.jpg
wikimedia-affenpinscher-breed-futurebrea.note: High-resolution photograph (3024 x 4032 px) of an adult Affenpinscher by Futurebreak (captured 2023-08-24, uploaded 2026-07-08). Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-small-munsterlander-official-standar.name: FCI - Kleiner Münsterländer (Small Münsterländer) Official Breed Standard No. 102
fci-small-munsterlander-official-standar.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 102 (valid standard dated 2019-09-04, English publication dated 2019-11-14). Covers German origin (1912 Heidewachtelhunde club founding, 1921 Dr. Friedrich Jungklaus first standard), Group 7 Section 1.2 Continental Pointing Dogs (Spaniel type) classification with working trial, versatile hunting utilization, 1:1 skull-to-muzzle ratio, elbow-to-ground ~ elbow-to-withers, solid brown nose, short tight brown lips, 42-tooth scissor bite (+/- 2 P1 permissible), 110° shoulder angle, dense medium water-repellent coat, brown-and-white / brown roan coloration with permissible 'Jungklaus' tan markings, disqualifications (ectropion, entropion, distichiasis, >4 cm height deviation), and withers height (dogs 54 cm, bitches 52 cm, +/- 2 cm within standard). Omits weight.

fci-small-munsterlander-nomenclature.name: FCI - Kleiner Münsterländer Breed Nomenclature (No. 102)
fci-small-munsterlander-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Germany as country of origin, Group 7 Section 1.2 Continental Pointing Dogs (Spaniel type) classification with working trial, definitive acceptance date (1955-02-14), English standard publication date (2019-11-14), and official multilingual names (Kleiner Münsterländer, Petit Epagneul de Münster).

vklm-zuchtordnung-2019.name: Verband für Kleine Münsterländer e.V. (KlM) - Zuchtordnung (Stand 01.07.2019)
vklm-zuchtordnung-2019.note: Official German parent breed club (Verband für Kleine Münsterländer e.V.) breeding regulations effective 1 July 2019 establishing versatile hunting breeding goals, official abbreviation 'KlM', minimum form/coat evaluation over 15 months, hip dysplasia (HD) radiographic screening above 12 months, central puppy/health tracking, mandatory reporting of hereditary disease symptoms, and breeding exclusion of dogs exhibiting hereditary disorders.

klm-international-minutes-2019.name: Verband Kleine Münsterländer International (KlM-I) e.V. - Executive Board Minutes (September 2019)
klm-international-minutes-2019.note: Official international parent breed club (KlM-I) Executive Board summary (meeting 19 September 2019, published 29 October 2019) affirming versatile before-and-after-the-shot hunting standards and documenting Germany's ongoing Ectopic Ureter Project in Kleiner Münsterländer.

rkc-small-munsterlander-breed-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Small Munsterlander (Imp) Interim Breed Standard
rkc-small-munsterlander-breed-standard.note: Official Royal Kennel Club interim breed standard (Gundog Group, published August 1, 2026; breed on Imported Breed Register since 2005) confirming 1870 North German Munsterland documentation, 1921 Dr. Friedrich Jungklaus standard, 11:10 body length-to-height ratio, brown-and-white / brown roan coloration with white tail tip and permissible tan markings, and size (dogs 52-56 cm, bitches 50-54 cm). Omits weight.

rkc-small-munsterlander-breed-profile.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Small Munsterlander (Imp) Breeds A to Z
rkc-small-munsterlander-breed-profile.note: Official Royal Kennel Club Breeds A to Z profile confirming medium size, country lifestyle, small house and small/medium garden suitability, up to 1 hour daily baseline exercise, weekly grooming, Sheds Yes, Brown & White and Brown Roan standard colours, and Breed Watch Category 1 status.

akc-small-munsterlander-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Small Munsterlander Dog Breed Information
akc-small-munsterlander-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Miscellaneous Class; parent club Small Munsterlander Club of America) documenting intelligent/devoted/self-confident character, height (20.5-21 inches), weight (40-60 pounds), life expectancy (12-14 years), moderate shedding, eager-to-please trainability, only-to-alert barking, slow mental maturation to ~2 years of age, outdoor supervision to prevent wandering/self-hunting, and national breed club recommended Hip and Elbow Certification.

skk-kleiner-munsterlander-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Kleiner münsterländer Rasprofil
skk-kleiner-munsterlander-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile confirming Münsterland origin, 1960s Swedish arrival, height (approx. 54 cm males, 52 cm females), winter paw-fur trimming, easy brushing, social family/dog nature with mild stubbornness, unsuitability solely as a companion dog, and health note confirming robust health with hip dysplasia (HD) occurring.

skk-kleiner-munsterlander-ras-2024.name: Svenska Vorstehklubben / SKK - Rasspecifik avelsstrategi (RAS) Kleiner Münsterländer
skk-kleiner-munsterlander-ras-2024.note: Official Swedish breed-specific breeding strategy (RAS, published via SKK, timestamp 2024-01-25) documenting mandatory pre-breeding HD screening (goal >=50% litter HD X-rayed, no HD E), growing ED radiographic monitoring, and low-frequency occurrences of food/mite allergies (typically onset <3 yr), hypothyroidism (typically onset 2-3 yr or late-onset >8 yr), ectopic ureter, and epilepsy—all strictly excluded from breeding.

scc-petit-epagneul-de-munster-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Petit épagneul de Münster (Petit Münsterländer)
scc-petit-epagneul-de-munster-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile for Petit épagneul de Münster (Kleiner Münsterländer) confirming German origin, continental spaniel-type pointing versatility, height (54 cm males, 52 cm females, +/- 2 cm), and attentive family-friendly character.

pmc-sweden-hd-ed-2026-13261803.name: Prevalence of hip and elbow dysplasia in young adult dogs in Sweden (2026)
pmc-sweden-hd-ed-2026-13261803.note: Peer-reviewed Swedish radiographic epidemiological study (published January 4, 2026, PMID 41485113, PMC13261803) reporting hip dysplasia screening outcomes across 441 young adult Kleiner Münsterländers in Sweden: 355 (80.5%) graded normal and 57 (12.9%) graded mild dysplasia (screened cohort).

pmc-body-weight-heritability-10276637.name: Heritability and genetic trend of body weight in dogs of different breeds (PMC10276637)
pmc-body-weight-heritability-10276637.note: Peer-reviewed quantitative genetics study (PMC10276637) estimating body weight heritability alongside hip dysplasia screening records across purebred dogs, reporting a body-weight heritability of 0.34 for the Kleiner Münsterländer.

wikimedia-kleiner-munsterlander-4028mdk0.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Kleiner Münsterländer.jpg
wikimedia-kleiner-munsterlander-4028mdk0.note: Photograph (924 x 552 px) of an adult Small Münsterländer (Kleiner Münsterländer) outdoors by 4028mdk09 (captured 2009-10-09, uploaded 2009-10-10, colour-cleaned 2017-04-23). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-kleiner-munsterlander-2-canari.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Kleiner Münsterländer aka Small Munsterlander 2.JPG
wikimedia-kleiner-munsterlander-2-canari.note: Photograph (744 x 527 px) of an adult brown-and-white male Small Münsterländer standing outdoors by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2013-06-29 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2014-06-01). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported on Wikimedia Commons.

akc-american-foxhound-official-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard for the American Foxhound
akc-american-foxhound-official-standard.note: Official country-of-origin AKC breed standard (Hound Group; approved January 11, 2011, effective March 1, 2011). Establishes withers height (dogs 23 to 28 inches, bitches 21 to 26 inches), fairly long slightly domed head, moderately low long fine broad ears reaching nearly to nose tip, 3-inch springy flank, straight well-boned forelegs, foxlike compact feet, gaily carried tail with slight brush, close hard medium-length hound coat, and any-colour allowance. Omits weight.

akc-american-foxhound-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - American Foxhound Dog Breed Information
akc-american-foxhound-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile documenting 1886 AKC recognition, Virginia heritage, weight (65-70 pounds male, 60-65 pounds female), life expectancy (11-13 years), independent/easy-going/sweet-tempered character, friendliness with children, dogs, and cats, 1 to 2 hours of daily exercise, strict on-leash advice, weekly brushing, drop-ear care, and breed health considerations including hip dysplasia and thrombocytopathy. (Summary box still displays older 22-25 / 21-24 in height figures).

akc-george-washington-foxhounds-2020.name: American Kennel Club - By George: A Founding Father and His American Foxhounds (2020)
akc-george-washington-foxhounds-2020.note: Published AKC historical article (May 26, 2020) documenting Robert Brooke's 1650 arrival in Maryland with British hounds and George Washington's Mount Vernon breeding program crossing colonial hounds with French staghounds gifted by the Marquis de Lafayette (1785) and Irish hounds.

akc-state-dogs-virginia-2021.name: American Kennel Club - Celebrate the 4th with 5 State Dogs (Virginia: American Foxhound, 2021)
akc-state-dogs-virginia-2021.note: Published AKC feature (April 20, 2021) confirming 1886 AKC recognition and Virginia's 1966 statutory designation of the American Foxhound as its official State Dog.

fci-american-foxhound-official-standard.name: FCI - American Foxhound Official Breed Standard No. 303
fci-american-foxhound-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 303 (valid standard dated 1979-11-02, English publication dated 1998-03-05). Covers US origin, Group 6 Section 1.1 Large-sized Hounds classification with working trial, large soft pleading brown/hazel eyes, clean throat free of dewlap, chest narrower in proportion to depth than English Foxhound (28 in girth in a 23 in hound; 3 in flank), close hard medium-length coat in any colour, and earlier withers height bounds (dogs 22-25 in / 56-63.5 cm, bitches 21-24 in / 53-61 cm). Omits weight.

fci-american-foxhound-nomenclature.name: FCI - American Foxhound Breed Nomenclature (No. 303)
fci-american-foxhound-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming the United States as country of origin, Group 6 Section 1.1 Large-sized Hounds classification with working trial, definitive acceptance date (1979-11-02), standard publication date (1998-03-05), and official multilingual name (American Foxhound).

skk-american-foxhound-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - American foxhound Rasprofil
skk-american-foxhound-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile confirming US origin from British foxhounds, driving hunting dog unsuited solely as a companion pet, short hard easy-care coat over softer undercoat, barking/howling trailing voice, family friendliness with children and other dogs, stubborn streak, high exercise needs, and note that very few Swedish individuals prevent national breed health assessment.

scc-foxhound-americain-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Foxhound américain
scc-foxhound-americain-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile for Foxhound américain confirming Robert Brooke's ~1650 hound imports, English/French/Irish ancestry, faster lighter build and keen nose compared with English Foxhound, musical singing voice ('voix chantante'), and approximate unsexed weight (~30 kg).

pmc-boggiatto-2011-foxhound-leishmania.name: Transplacental Transmission of Leishmania infantum as a Means for Continued Disease Incidence in North America (PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases 2011)
pmc-boggiatto-2011-foxhound-leishmania.note: Peer-reviewed study by Boggiatto, Gibson-Corley, Metz, Gallup, Hostetter, Mullin, and Petersen (PLoS Negl Trop Dis 2011 Apr 12;5(4):e1019, PMC3075227) demonstrating transplacental (vertical) transmission of Leishmania infantum in naturally infected US Foxhounds (10 of 12 pups / 83% positive by kqPCR) and documenting ~12% kqPCR incidence in Midwest Foxhound kennels.
pmc-boggiatto-2011-foxhound-leishmania.publisher: PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pmc-mahachi-2021-foxhound-leishmania.name: Demographics and travel history of imported and autochthonous Leishmania infantum-infected dogs in the United States and Canada (JVIM / PMC7995368)
pmc-mahachi-2021-foxhound-leishmania.note: Peer-reviewed retrospective surveillance study (J Vet Intern Med, PMC7995368) reviewing Leishmania infantum infections across the US and Canada (2006–2019), citing the 2000–2003 Foxhound serosurvey (8.9% seroprevalence) and a 9-year hunting-hound PCR survey averaging 20% prevalence.
pmc-mahachi-2021-foxhound-leishmania.publisher: Journal of Veterinary Internal Medicine / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

pubmed-foxhound-pelger-huet-1979.name: Studies of the Pelger-Huët anomaly in foxhounds (American Journal of Pathology 1979)
pubmed-foxhound-pelger-huet-1979.note: Peer-reviewed haematology and pedigree study (Am J Pathol 1979 Jul;96(1):237-248, PMID 464021) documenting the inherited Pelger-Huët neutrophil nuclear-segmentation anomaly in Foxhounds.

wikimedia-american-foxhound-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:American Foxhound.jpg
wikimedia-american-foxhound-canarian.note: High-resolution photograph (1787 x 1744 px) of an adult American Foxhound outdoors by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2017-12-09 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2018-01-27). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-americanfoxhound-peepe.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:AmericanFoxhound.jpg
wikimedia-americanfoxhound-peepe.note: High-resolution photograph (1932 x 2576 px) of American Foxhound 'Sobe' by User:Peepe (EXIF capture date 2005-10-06 on Kodak Z7590, transferred to Wikimedia Commons by Caronna on 2005-12-22). Released into the public domain by the copyright holder.

pmc-dachslife-ivdd-2016.name: DachsLife 2015: an investigation of lifestyle associations with the risk of intervertebral disc disease in Dachshunds (PMC)
pmc-dachslife-ivdd-2016.note: Peer-reviewed epidemiological study of 2,031 Dachshunds documenting 15.7% overall IVDD prevalence (ranging from 7.1% in Standard Wire-Haired to 24.4% in Standard Smooth-Haired) and citing an estimated 19-24% lifetime clinical risk.

omia-schnauzer-dcm-rbm20.name: OMIA:002365-9615 - Cardiomyopathy, dilated, RBM20-related in Canis lupus familiaris
omia-schnauzer-dcm-rbm20.note: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Animals record documenting autosomal recessive RBM20 22-bp deletion dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) in Standard Schnauzers and Giant Schnauzers, citing Leach et al. (2014, 2022) and Harmon et al. (2017).

akc-chesapeake-bay-retriever-official-st.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard for the Chesapeake Bay Retriever
akc-chesapeake-bay-retriever-official-st.note: Official country-of-origin AKC breed standard (Sporting Group; approved November 9, 1993, effective December 31, 1993). Establishes height (males 23-26 inches, females 21-24 inches), weight (males 65-80 pounds, females 55-70 pounds), hindquarters as high as or a trifle higher than shoulders, clear yellowish/amber eyes, broad round skull, thin non-pendulous lips, scissor preferred / level acceptable bite, well-webbed hare feet (hind dewclaws disqualified), short thick oily coat (nowhere over 1.5 inches; feathering <=1.75 in; waving only on neck/shoulders/back/loins), brown/sedge/deadgrass coloration (black or misplaced white disqualified), and honorable scars not penalized.

akc-chesapeake-bay-retriever-breed-profi.name: American Kennel Club - Chesapeake Bay Retriever Dog Breed Information
akc-chesapeake-bay-retriever-breed-profi.note: Official AKC breed profile documenting bright/affectionate/sensitive temperament, height (23-26 in males, 21-24 in females), weight (65-80 lb males, 55-70 lb females), life expectancy (10-13 years), moderate shedding, weekly grooming, occasional barking, family protectiveness, independent working nature, and athletic exercise needs.

akc-chesapeake-bay-retriever-history-202.name: American Kennel Club - Chesapeake Bay Retriever History: From Bay Waters to Family Homes (2024)
akc-chesapeake-bay-retriever-history-202.note: Published AKC historical feature by Denise Flaim (updated October 28, 2024) documenting the 1807 Canton shipwreck rescue of St. John's Water Dog pups Sailor (dingy-red male) and Canton (black female) purchased by George Law for a guinea each, Dr. James Stewart of Sparrow's Point, and how guarding hunters' catch and gear forged the breed's protective independence (making it less ideal for first-time owners).

fci-chesapeake-bay-retriever-official-st.name: FCI - Chesapeake Bay Retriever Official Breed Standard No. 263
fci-chesapeake-bay-retriever-official-st.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 263 (dated 1999-03-12). Covers US origin, Group 8 Section 1 Retrievers classification with working trial, clear yellowish/amber eyes, hindquarters as high or a trifle higher than shoulders, short double coat waving only on neck/shoulders/back/loins, height (males 23-26 in / 58-66 cm; females 21-24 in / 53-61 cm), weight (males 65-80 lb / 29.5-36.5 kg; females 55-70 lb / 25-32 kg), and disqualifications.

fci-chesapeake-bay-retriever-nomenclatur.name: FCI - Chesapeake Bay Retriever Breed Nomenclature (No. 263)
fci-chesapeake-bay-retriever-nomenclatur.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming the United States as country of origin, Group 8 Section 1 Retrievers classification with working trial, definitive acceptance date (1964-09-15), English standard publication date (1999-03-12), and official multilingual names (Chesapeake Bay Retriever, Retriever de la Baie de Chesapeake).

acc-chesapeake-bay-retriever-health.name: American Chesapeake Club (ACC) - Breed Health Statement & Testing
acc-chesapeake-bay-retriever-health.note: Official US parent breed club health portal publishing the ACC Board-approved Breed Health Statement (September 11, 2016) covering Hip Dysplasia, Elbow Dysplasia, Eyes, Progressive Retinal Atrophy (prcd), Degenerative Myelopathy (DM), Exercise-Induced Collapse (EIC), Ectodermal Dysplasia–Skin Fragility Syndrome (ED-SFS), Chondrodysplasia (CDPA), and Chondrodystrophy & Intervertebral Disc Disease (CDDY/IVDD), alongside nickname 'Chessie' and abbreviation 'CBR'.

rkc-retriever-chesapeake-bay-profile.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Retriever (Chesapeake Bay) Breeds A to Z
rkc-retriever-chesapeake-bay-profile.note: Official Royal Kennel Club Breeds A to Z profile (Gundog Group) confirming icy-Atlantic retrieving strength, more substantial build than Labrador, large house requirement, more than 2 hours daily exercise, weekly grooming, Sheds Yes, accepted UK colours (Ash, Brown, Dark Brown, Deadgrass, Light Brown, Sedge), Breed Watch Category 1 status, Good Practice tests (Elbows, Hips, DM DNA), and Best Practice tests (prcd-PRA DNA, Eye Scheme).

skk-chesapeake-bay-retriever-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Chesapeake bay retriever Rasprofil
skk-chesapeake-bay-retriever-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile confirming 1807 shipwreck legend, 1973 first Swedish registration, naturally oily waterproof double coat (shampoo only rarely; sheds a couple of times yearly), reserved/neutral attitude toward strangers paired with fierce handler loyalty, and health summary noting hip dysplasia (HD) as the most common health problem alongside ED, few cataract cases, and rare PRA.

scc-retriever-de-la-baie-de-chesapeake-p.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Retriever de la baie de Chesapeake
scc-retriever-de-la-baie-de-chesapeake-p.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile documenting Maryland Chesapeake Bay development, 1876 first Baltimore exhibition, 1890 first standard, 1918 parent club founding, 1948 French arrival, oily weatherproof short coat, guarding instinct, and need for firm, consistent training.

pmc-olivry-2012-cbr-pkp1-ed-sfs.name: Deficient Plakophilin-1 Expression Due to a Mutation in PKP1 Causes Ectodermal Dysplasia-Skin Fragility Syndrome in Chesapeake Bay Retriever Dogs (PLOS ONE 2012)
pmc-olivry-2012-cbr-pkp1-ed-sfs.note: Peer-reviewed veterinary dermatology and genetics study by Olivry, Linder, Wang, Bizikova et al. (PLoS One 2012;7(2):e32072, PMID 22384142, PMC3284538) characterizing the first naturally occurring animal model of human Ectodermal Dysplasia–Skin Fragility Syndrome (ED-SFS) in 9 of 28 Chesapeake Bay Retriever puppies across 4 related litters, caused by an autosomal-recessive splice-site mutation in PKP1 (c.202+1G>C).
pmc-olivry-2012-cbr-pkp1-ed-sfs.publisher: PLOS ONE / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

wikimedia-chesapeake-bay-retriever1-rous.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Chesapeake Bay Retriever1.jpg
wikimedia-chesapeake-bay-retriever1-rous.note: High-resolution photograph (3324 x 2544 px) of an adult Chesapeake Bay Retriever ('Central N.Y.'s Brute Force') in a marsh by Keith Rousseau / Roussk (EXIF capture date 2007-06-16 on Nikon D80, first uploaded to en.wikipedia 2007-07-07, transferred to Wikimedia Commons by Pharaoh Hound on 2007-08-23). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported (and GFDL).

wikimedia-chesapeake-bay-retriever-snow-.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Chesapeake Bay Retriever in the snow.jpg
wikimedia-chesapeake-bay-retriever-snow-.note: High-resolution photograph (4489 x 3304 px) of a brown Chesapeake Bay Retriever in winter snow by Will Thomas / Forge Mountain Photography (captured 2017-03-13, uploaded to Wikimedia Commons by A11w1ss3nd on 2019-10-11, license verified by FlickreviewR 2 on 2019-10-11). Licensed under CC BY 2.0 Generic.

omia-boston-terrier-hsf4-cataract.name: OMIA:001758-9615 - Cataract, early onset, HSF4-related in Canis lupus familiaris
omia-boston-terrier-hsf4-cataract.note: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Animals record documenting the autosomal recessive HSF4 mutation responsible for early-onset (but not late-onset) hereditary cataracts in the Boston Terrier, citing Mellersh et al. (Journal of Heredity, 2007; PMID 17611257).

pmc-boston-terrier-boas-2024.name: BOAS in the Boston Terrier: A healthier screw-tailed breed? (PLOS ONE / PMC)
pmc-boston-terrier-boas-2024.note: University of Cambridge prospective respiratory-function grading study of Boston Terriers (Tomlinson et al., PLOS ONE 2024) finding 37.5% Grade 0 (unaffected), 35.6% Grade 1, 26.0% Grade 2, and 0.96% Grade 3, with nostril stenosis and facial foreshortening significantly associated with BOAS.

pmc-boston-terrier-ced-2021.name: A Retrospective Study of Corneal Endothelial Dystrophy in Dogs (PMC)
pmc-boston-terrier-ced-2021.note: UC Davis Veterinary Medical Teaching Hospital retrospective study (99 CED dogs vs. 458,680 reference dogs) showing Boston Terriers are significantly overrepresented for corneal endothelial dystrophy, particularly in older dogs.

fci-dutch-shepherd-dog-official-standard.name: FCI - Hollandse Herdershond (Dutch Shepherd Dog) Official Breed Standard No. 223
fci-dutch-shepherd-dog-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 223 (valid official standard dated 2019-12-21, English publication dated 2020-01-09). Covers Netherlands origin, 12 June 1898 first standard, Group 1 Section 1 Sheepdogs classification with working trial, 10:9 body proportion, 1:1 skull-to-muzzle ratio, dry wedge head, complete scissor bite, dark oblique almond eyes, high erect ears, hock-length tail never curled over back, no hind dewclaws, free supple trot, three coat varieties (short-, long-, and wire-haired; wire hand-plucked twice yearly), golden or silver brindle with preferred black mask, and withers height (males 57-62 cm, females 55-60 cm). Omits weight.

fci-dutch-shepherd-dog-nomenclature.name: FCI - Hollandse Herdershond (Dutch Shepherd Dog) Breed Nomenclature (No. 223)
fci-dutch-shepherd-dog-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming the Netherlands as country of origin, Group 1 Section 1 Sheepdogs classification with working trial, definitive acceptance date (1955-05-11), valid official standard date (2019-12-21), English standard publication date (2020-01-09), and official multilingual names (Hollandse Herdershond, Dutch Shepherd Dog, Berger Hollandais, Holländischer Schäferhund).

akc-dutch-shepherd-official-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard for the Dutch Shepherd
akc-dutch-shepherd-official-standard.note: Official AKC Miscellaneous Class breed standard (approved January 11, 2016, effective January 1, 2017) detailing short-, long-, and rough-haired varieties, gold and silver brindle coloration, natural untrimmed presentation with whiskers intact, and disqualifications (males <21 or >26 in, females <20 or >25 in, drooping/hanging ears, yellow or blue eyes, cropped/stump tail, and misplaced solid white markings).

akc-dutch-shepherd-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Dutch Shepherd Dog Breed Information
akc-dutch-shepherd-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (FSS since April 2012, Miscellaneous Class since January 1, 2017) documenting 1898 first standard, 1914 brindle-only decision, historic farm duties, weight (42-75 pounds), life expectancy (11-14 years), moderate seasonal shedding, high working energy, eager-to-please trainability with mild independence, supervision with children and other dogs, and national club recommended health tests (Hip, Elbow, Ophthalmologist; thyroid for long-haired, goniodysplasia for rough-haired).

nhc-dutch-shepherd-vfr-2021.name: Nederlandse Herdershonden Club (NHC) - Verenigingsfokreglement (VFR 2021)
nhc-dutch-shepherd-vfr-2021.note: Official country-of-origin Dutch parent breed club (Nederlandse Herdershonden Club, founded 1898; Raad van Beheer approved) breeding regulations effective 1 May 2021 establishing rules across all three varieties: mandatory pre-breeding behavioural test (verplichte gedragstest), pectinate ligament abnormality (PLA, formerly goniodysplasia) eye screening, HD evaluation guidelines, and minimum breeding age of 18 months for females.

nhc-dutch-shepherd-vfr-update-2024.name: Nederlandse Herdershonden Club (NHC) - Verenigingsfokreglement gewijzigd (2024 Update)
nhc-dutch-shepherd-vfr-update-2024.note: Official NHC 2024 breeding-regulation update (published 27 February 2024) detailing ECVO-protocol eye examinations including gonioscopy and keratitis assessment alongside HD-A/B and HD-C x HD-A pairing rules.

adsa-dutch-shepherd-health.name: American Dutch Shepherd Association (ADSA) - Breed Health & Recommended Testing
adsa-dutch-shepherd-health.note: Official AKC parent breed club (American Dutch Shepherd Association) health portal listing recommended variety-specific pre-breeding screenings: OFA Hips and Elbows, Degenerative Myelopathy (DM), OFA Spine and Spongy Cerebellar Degeneration 1 & 2 (SDCA1/SDCA2) for short-haired, yearly Thyroid and von Willebrand Disease Type I (vWD1) for long-haired, and Goniodysplasia for rough-haired, plus nickname 'Dutchie'.

skk-hollandse-herdershond-kortharig-prof.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Hollandse herdershond, korthårig Rasprofil
skk-hollandse-herdershond-kortharig-prof.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for short-haired Hollandse herdershond confirming Netherlands origin, 1898 NHC founding, height (57-62 cm males, 55-60 cm females), weight (approx. 22-32 kg), easy-care short double coat, unsuitability for first-time owners, daily physical and mental activation needs, and health note confirming relatively healthy status with hip dysplasia (HD) occurring.

skk-hollandse-herdershond-stravharig-pro.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Hollandse herdershond, strävhårig Rasprofil
skk-hollandse-herdershond-stravharig-pro.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile for wire-haired Hollandse herdershond confirming blue-grey / pepper-and-salt / gold- and silver-brindle coat tones, twice-yearly coat stripping (keeping cheeks, forehead, and ears short), and health note highlighting glaucoma caused by anterior-chamber angle malformation detectable via gonioscopy in the wire-haired variety alongside HD.

scc-berger-hollandais-profile.name: Société Centrale Canine (SCC) - Berger hollandais
scc-berger-hollandais-profile.note: Official French Kennel Club (SCC) breed profile confirming height (55-62 cm), weight unspecified (NP), three coat varieties (noting wire-haired rarity outside the Netherlands), jumping ability, weather and fatigue resistance, non-picky appetite, and need for spacious daily outdoor exercise.

pmc-shelton-2019-dutch-shepherd-slc25a12.name: A Mutation in the Mitochondrial Aspartate/Glutamate Carrier Leads to a More Oxidizing Intramitochondrial Environment and an Inflammatory Myopathy in Dutch Shepherd Dogs (J Neuromuscul Dis 2019)
pmc-shelton-2019-dutch-shepherd-slc25a12.note: Peer-reviewed study by Shelton, Minor, Li, Naviaux, Leegwater, Mickelson, Palmieri et al. (J Neuromuscul Dis 2019;6(4):485-501, Epub 2019-09-24, PMID 31594244, PMC6918910) providing the first description in any species of an SLC25A12 variant (c.1046T>C; p.L349P in mitochondrial carrier AGC1) causing an early-onset autosomal-recessive inflammatory myopathy in Dutch Shepherd Dogs.
pmc-shelton-2019-dutch-shepherd-slc25a12.publisher: Journal of Neuromuscular Diseases / National Library of Medicine (PMC)

wikimedia-hollandse-herder-langhaar-djen.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:2014-03-22-16-28-15.djennarechts.jpg
wikimedia-hollandse-herder-langhaar-djen.note: High-resolution photograph (1024 x 680 px) of an adult long-haired Dutch Shepherd Dog ('Djenna') outdoors by Femkederapper (captured 2014-03-22, uploaded 2021-02-18). Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 International on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-short-haired-dutch-shepherd-2-.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Short-haired Dutch Shepherd 2.JPG
wikimedia-short-haired-dutch-shepherd-2-.note: Photograph (509 x 382 px) of an adult short-haired Dutch Shepherd Dog outdoors by Canarian (EXIF capture date 2013-06-29 on Sony DSLR-A350, uploaded 2013-10-23). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported on Wikimedia Commons.

wikimedia-hollandse-herder-ruwhaar-teuni.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Hollandse herder ruwhaar.jpg
wikimedia-hollandse-herder-ruwhaar-teuni.note: Photograph (600 x 450 px) of an adult wire-haired Dutch Shepherd Dog by Teunie (originally uploaded to nl.wikipedia on 2005-04-16, transferred to Wikimedia Commons by SieBot on 2007-03-19; camera EXIF clock uncalibrated). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported (and GFDL) on Wikimedia Commons.

akc-saarloos-wolfhond-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Saarloos Wolfhond Dog Breed Information (FSS)
akc-saarloos-wolfhond-profile.note: Official AKC Foundation Stock Service breed profile for the Saarloos Wolfhond covering weight (70-90 lb males, 60-80 lb females), life expectancy (12-15 years), temperament, and breed traits.

pmc-saarloos-lhx3-dwarfism-2014.name: Pituitary Dwarfism in Saarloos and Czechoslovakian Wolfdogs is Associated with a Mutation in LHX3 (JVIM / PMC)
pmc-saarloos-lhx3-dwarfism-2014.note: Peer-reviewed Utrecht University study (Voorbij et al., JVIM 2014; PMID 25273400) identifying the autosomal recessive 7-bp deletion in intron 5 of LHX3 in Saarlooswolfhonds and documenting a 31% carrier frequency (75 of 239 healthy breeding dogs).
pmc-saarloos-lhx3-dwarfism-2014.publisher: PubMed Central (Journal of Veterinary Internal Medicine)

pmc-dm-sod1-cohort-2025.name: Survival and deterioration time of walking abilities in dogs with SOD1-related degenerative myelopathy (PMC)
pmc-dm-sod1-cohort-2025.note: Peer-reviewed clinical cohort study (Frontiers in Veterinary Science, 2025) of dogs homozygous for the SOD1 degenerative myelopathy mutation including Saarloos Wolfhounds.

fci-norwegian-lundehund-official-standar.name: FCI - Norsk Lundehund (Norwegian Lundehund) Official Breed Standard No. 265
fci-norwegian-lundehund-official-standar.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 265 (valid official standard dated 2011-11-10, English publication dated 2012-02-22, hosted by Norsk Lundehund Klubb). Covers Norwegian origin ('lunde' puffin Fratercula arctica + 'hund' dog; >400-year history; distemper bottlenecks and Christie/Værøy rescue), Group 5 Section 2 Nordic Hunting Dogs classification without working trial, wedge head, scissor preferred / pincer & moderate lower prognathism permitted, accepted bilateral premolar absence, yellowish-brown eyes with dark halo, retractable folding ear cartilage, at least 6 toes per foot (forefeet 5 resting / 8 pads; hindfeet 4 resting / 7 pads), rotary paddling foreleg gait, dense rough double coat, white-combined red-to-fawn/dark-patched colours, withers height (males 35-38 cm, females 32-35 cm), and weight (males about 7 kg, females about 6 kg).

fci-norwegian-lundehund-nomenclature.name: FCI - Norsk Lundehund (Norwegian Lundehund) Breed Nomenclature (No. 265)
fci-norwegian-lundehund-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Norway as country of origin, Group 5 Section 2 Nordic Hunting Dogs classification without working trial, definitive acceptance date (1965-10-06), English standard publication date (2012-02-22), and official multilingual names (Norsk Lundehund, Norwegian Lundehund, Chien norvégien de macareux).

nkk-norsk-lundehund-profile.name: Norsk Kennel Klub (NKK) - Norsk lundehund Rasebeskrivelse
nkk-norsk-lundehund-profile.note: Official country-of-origin Norwegian Kennel Club (NKK) breed profile confirming >400-year puffin-hunting heritage, 1850s shift to net hunting, survival at Måstad on Værøy, Eleanor and Christian Christie's 60-70 dog Hamar kennel and late-1950s rescue from 5 Måstad dogs plus a 6th dog, height (32-38 cm), weight (6-7 kg), friendly/curious/watchful family & hiking character, and moderate exercise needs.

nkk-nlk-norwegian-lundehund-compendium.name: Norsk Kennel Klub / Norsk Lundehund Klubb - The Norwegian Lundehund Breed Compendium
nkk-nlk-norwegian-lundehund-compendium.note: Official NKK Standard Committee-approved illustrated Breed Compendium (2010) documenting the 1591 account by bailiff Erik Hansen Schønnebøl, Petter Dass's ~1700 poem 'Nordlands Trompet' (Lovund), Måstad/Værøy descent of all modern Lundehunds, shoulder and neck flexibility, climbing function of extra toes/pads (noting 5 hind digits acceptable), and 'Norwegian Puffin Dog' translation.
nkk-nlk-norwegian-lundehund-compendium.publisher: Norsk Kennel Klub / Norsk Lundehund Klubb

skk-norsk-lundehund-profile.name: Svenska Kennelklubben (SKK) - Norsk lundehund Rasprofil
skk-norsk-lundehund-profile.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed profile confirming Værøy/Lofoten origin, height (35-38 cm males, 32-35 cm females), weight (7 kg males, 6 kg females), lifespan (13-14 years not uncommon), backward neck flexion to back, foldable ears, paddling circular foreleg gait, dirt-repelling Nordic coat, vocal alert barking, slower housetraining, stranger caution, and intestinal lymphangiectasia (IL) affecting roughly 1 in 10 dogs per year.

akc-norwegian-lundehund-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Norwegian Lundehund Dog Breed Information
akc-norwegian-lundehund-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Non-Sporting Group; FSS since 1996, Companion Events 2004, full AKC recognition 2011) documenting Værøy puffin-hunting heritage, US height (13-15 in male, 12-14 in female), US weight (15-18 lb male, 12-15 lb female), weekly brushing, frequent nail trims, regular ear checks, brisk 30-minute walks or ball-chasing, clever problem-solving, and foldable ears.

akc-norwegian-lundehund-history-2022.name: American Kennel Club - Rarest Dog Breed: Norwegian Lundehund History From the Brink of Extinction (2022)
akc-norwegian-lundehund-history-2022.note: Published AKC historical article by Denise Flaim (updated March 16, 2022) documenting Norway's puffin-hunting ban, the breed's near-extinction and rescue, and modern conservation work locating seabird nests non-invasively.

nlaa-norwegian-lundehund-association.note: Official AKC parent breed club portal (established 2004) preserving breed heritage, supporting CHIC/OFA health testing (patella, eye exam, and DNA repository), and collaborating with the Norwegian Lundehund Club on breed health.

pmc-metzger-2016-lundehund-syndrome-lepr.name: Variant detection and runs of homozygosity in next generation sequencing data elucidate the genetic background of Lundehund syndrome (BMC Genomics 2016)
pmc-metzger-2016-lundehund-syndrome-lepr.note: Peer-reviewed whole-genome sequencing and ROH study by Metzger et al. (BMC Genomics 2016 Aug 2;17:535, PMC4971756) detailing Lundehund Syndrome clinical signs (onset 2.5-10.5 years; diarrhea, vomiting, weight loss, apathy, hypoalbuminemia, hypoglobulinemia, vitamin B deficiency, ascites/edema) and identifying a CFA34 GWAS signal, candidate LEPREL1:g.139212C>G missense mutation, and immunoregulatory ROH enrichment (including NOD1).

(PLoS One 2017 Jun 1;12(6):e0177429, PMC5453418) analyzing 165K SNPs across Norwegian Lundehund (HE 0.035) and three Nordic Spitz outcrossing candidate breeds (Norwegian Buhund, Icelandic Sheepdog, Norrbottenspets; HE 0.209-0.284), documenting the 1940s/1960s bottlenecks (~1,500 worldwide dogs) and endorsing multi-breed genetic rescue.
